domains.name: exploration
domains.description: Manages all upstream exploration activities including seismic surveys, geological and geophysical (G&G) interpretation, prospect evaluation, basin analysis, and wildcat well planning. Serves as the SSOT for prospect and play data, resource potential assessments, lead/prospect generation, and PRMS-aligned resource classifications (1P/2P/3P). Integrates with Landmark DecisionSpace and Schlumberger Petrel for subsurface modeling and G&G workflows.

products.name: basin
products.description: Master record for sedimentary basins under evaluation. Captures basin name, type (foreland, rift, passive margin, etc.), geographic extent, tectonic setting, hydrocarbon system maturity, PRMS classification tier, and basin-level resource potential estimates (OOIP/OGIP). Serves as the top-level geographic and geological hierarchy for all exploration activities. Integrates with Landmark DecisionSpace basin analysis workflows.

attributes.name: basin_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the sedimentary basin. Primary key for the basin master record.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: champion_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Links basin to the accountable technical champion. Required for portfolio governance, resource allocation decisions, and succession planning. Basin champion is a named role in exploration organization

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the basin is currently active in the exploration portfolio. False indicates basin has been relinquished, divested, or deprioritized.

attributes.name: area_sq_km
attributes.description: Total geographic extent of the sedimentary basin in square kilometers. Represents the full basin boundary as defined by geological interpretation.
attributes.references: USGS Basin Area Definitions, Landmark DecisionSpace Basin Modeling

attributes.name: basin_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code for the basin used in regulatory filings and internal systems. May align with USGS province codes or company-specific taxonomy.
attributes.references: USGS National Assessment of Oil and Gas Resources, BOEM Basin Codes

attributes.name: basin_name
attributes.description: Official name of the sedimentary basin as recognized by geological surveys and industry standards (e.g., Permian Basin, Gulf of Mexico Basin, Williston Basin).
attributes.references: USGS Basin and Province Definitions, SPE PRMS

attributes.name: basin_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the basin in the company's exploration and production portfolio. Indicates level of activity and investment priority.

attributes.name: basin_type
attributes.description: Geological classification of the basin based on tectonic setting and formation mechanism. Critical for understanding hydrocarbon system maturity and trap styles. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: foreland|rift|passive_margin|strike_slip|intracratonic|forearc|backarc|pull_apart — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SPE Basin Classification Standards, AAPG Memoir 51

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Operating business unit or geographic division responsible for exploration activities in the basin. Used for portfolio segmentation and financial reporting.
attributes.references: Internal Organization Hierarchy, SAP S/4HANA Organizational Structure

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary country where the basin is located. For transboundary basins, represents the country with majority acreage or operational focus.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the basin record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for data lineage and governance.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Assessment of geological and geophysical data quality and coverage for the basin on a scale of 0.00 to 1.00. Higher scores indicate better data density, vintage, and reliability for decision-making.

attributes.name: discovery_count
attributes.description: Number of commercial hydrocarbon discoveries made in the basin. Used to calculate exploration success rate and basin prospectivity metrics.
attributes.references: Internal Exploration Database, IHS Markit Discovery Records

attributes.name: environmental_sensitivity
attributes.description: Assessment of environmental and ecological sensitivity of the basin. Considers protected areas, endangered species habitat, water resources, and community proximity. Impacts permitting and HSE requirements.
attributes.references: EPA Environmental Sensitivity Index, ESG Risk Assessment Framework

attributes.name: eur_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent (MMBOE)
attributes.description: Basin-level estimated ultimate recovery in million barrels of oil equivalent. Represents technically recoverable resources under current and anticipated technology and economics.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS, USGS Resource Assessment Methodology

attributes.name: exploration_maturity
attributes.description: Stage of exploration lifecycle for the basin. Indicates drilling density, geological understanding, and remaining prospectivity. Drives exploration strategy and risk profile.
attributes.references: Internal Exploration Portfolio Standards, SPE Exploration Maturity Framework

attributes.name: fiscal_regime_type
attributes.description: Type of fiscal and contractual framework governing hydrocarbon development in the basin. Critical for economic evaluation and partner negotiations.
attributes.references: OPEC Fiscal Regime Database, Wood Mackenzie Fiscal Terms

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: High-level geographic region where the basin is located (e.g., North America, West Africa, Middle East, Asia Pacific). Used for portfolio segmentation and regional reporting.
attributes.references: Internal Geographic Taxonomy, OPEC Regional Classifications

attributes.name: geological_risk_score
attributes.description: Composite geological risk score for the basin on a scale of 0.00 to 1.00, where lower values indicate higher risk. Aggregates source, reservoir, trap, and seal risk factors.
attributes.references: SPE Risk Assessment Guidelines, Internal Exploration Risk Framework

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_system_maturity
attributes.description: Assessment of the basin's petroleum system maturity based on source rock thermal history, generation timing, and migration pathways. Critical for play risk assessment.
attributes.references: SPE Petroleum Systems Analysis, Schlumberger Petrel Basin Modeling

attributes.name: infrastructure_maturity
attributes.description: Level of existing oil and gas infrastructure in the basin including pipelines, processing facilities, export terminals, and service networks. Impacts development economics and time-to-market.
attributes.references: Internal Infrastructure Database, FERC Pipeline Registry

attributes.name: last_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent basin-level resource assessment or portfolio review. Indicates currency of resource estimates and geological understanding.

attributes.name: lead_count
attributes.description: Number of exploration leads (unrisked prospects) currently identified in the basin. Represents early-stage opportunities requiring further technical work.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the basin record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data currency verification.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next basin assessment or portfolio review. Used for planning technical work programs and resource estimate updates.

attributes.name: ogip_bcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Gas In Place (OGIP) Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
attributes.description: Basin-level estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Represents total gas volume before any production. Includes associated and non-associated gas.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS, SEC Reserves Disclosure Requirements

attributes.name: onshore_offshore_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the basin is primarily onshore, offshore, or contains both onshore and offshore acreage. Impacts regulatory jurisdiction and operational complexity.
attributes.references: BSEE Offshore Definitions, BOEM Leasing Classifications

attributes.name: ooip_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Oil In Place (OOIP) Million Barrels (MMBBL)
attributes.description: Basin-level estimate of original oil in place in million barrels. Represents total oil volume before any production. Aggregated from prospect and play-level assessments.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS, SEC Reserves Disclosure Requirements

attributes.name: play_count
attributes.description: Number of distinct exploration plays identified in the basin. Each play represents a unique combination of source-reservoir-trap-seal elements.
attributes.references: SPE Play Analysis Framework, Internal Play Catalog

attributes.name: primary_reservoir_rock
attributes.description: Main reservoir formation or lithology hosting producible hydrocarbons in the basin (e.g., sandstone, carbonate, shale). May include multiple stacked reservoirs.

attributes.name: primary_source_rock
attributes.description: Dominant source rock formation or interval responsible for hydrocarbon generation in the basin (e.g., Woodford Shale, Kimmeridge Clay, Bakken Formation).
attributes.references: USGS Source Rock Assessments, SPE Source Rock Characterization

attributes.name: prms_classification_tier
attributes.business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Classification Tier
attributes.description: Highest PRMS resource classification tier assigned to the basin's aggregate resources. Indicates confidence level in resource estimates for SEC and SPE reporting.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS 2018, SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200

attributes.name: prospect_count
attributes.description: Number of drillable prospects (risked, mature opportunities) in the basin. Represents near-term drilling inventory with AFE-ready technical packages.
attributes.references: Internal Exploration Drilling Inventory, AFE Portfolio

attributes.name: prospective_area_sq_km
attributes.description: Subset of basin area considered prospective for hydrocarbon accumulation based on geological and geophysical analysis. Used for resource potential calculations.

attributes.name: recovery_factor_percent
attributes.description: Basin-wide average recovery factor expressed as percentage of OOIP/OGIP. Reflects reservoir quality, drive mechanism, and technology application potential.
attributes.references: SPE Recovery Factor Guidelines, EOR Screening Criteria

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Primary government agency or regulatory body with jurisdiction over exploration and production activities in the basin (e.g., BSEE, state oil and gas commission, national oil ministry).
attributes.references: BSEE Jurisdiction, BOEM Regulatory Framework, State Regulatory Agencies

attributes.name: seismic_coverage_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of prospective basin area covered by 2D or 3D seismic surveys. Indicates data availability for prospect generation and geological interpretation.

attributes.name: tectonic_setting
attributes.description: Detailed description of the basin's tectonic environment and structural evolution. Includes plate boundary type, deformation history, and current stress regime.
attributes.references: AAPG Tectonic Classification, SPE Basin Analysis Standards

attributes.name: trap_style
attributes.description: Predominant hydrocarbon trap mechanism in the basin (e.g., structural anticline, stratigraphic pinchout, combination trap, fault-bounded). Influences exploration strategy.
attributes.references: AAPG Trap Classification, SPE Play Analysis Guidelines

attributes.name: water_depth_max_ft
attributes.description: Maximum water depth in feet for offshore portions of the basin. Null for purely onshore basins. Critical for technology selection and FPSO feasibility.

attributes.name: water_depth_min_ft
attributes.description: Minimum water depth in feet for offshore portions of the basin. Null for purely onshore basins. Used for drilling complexity and cost estimation.

attributes.name: well_count
attributes.description: Total number of exploration and appraisal wells drilled in the basin to date. Includes both company-operated and non-operated wells. Reflects exploration intensity.
attributes.references: Internal Well Database, State Oil and Gas Commission Records

products.name: play
products.description: Master record for petroleum plays within a basin. Defines the play concept including reservoir type, trap style, seal integrity, source rock maturity, migration pathway, charge risk, and play-level risked resource estimates. Aligned with SPE-PRMS play-based exploration methodology. Links to basin and supports portfolio-level play fairway mapping in Landmark DecisionSpace.

attributes.name: play_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the petroleum play. Primary key for the play master record.

attributes.name: basin_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sedimentary basin in which this play is located. Links to basin master data for regional geological context.

attributes.name: reservoir_formation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.formation. Business justification: Plays are defined by their reservoir formations. Currently play has reservoir_formation (STRING) and reservoir_age (STRING); these should be replaced with a FK to the formation master to ensure consis

attributes.name: analogue_play_reference
attributes.description: Reference to analogous plays in other basins or regions used for benchmarking resource estimates, well performance, and geological risk. Supports play fairway mapping and probabilistic assessment.

attributes.name: area_sq_miles
attributes.description: Areal extent of the play fairway in square miles. Represents the geographic footprint where the play concept is valid and prospective.

attributes.name: average_net_pay_thickness_ft
attributes.description: Play-level average thickness of productive reservoir interval in feet. Excludes non-reservoir intervals and water-bearing zones.

attributes.name: average_permeability_md
attributes.description: Play-level average permeability in millidarcies. Conventional reservoirs typically >1 mD; tight gas <0.1 mD; shale <0.001 mD.

attributes.name: average_porosity_percent
attributes.description: Play-level average porosity expressed as a percentage of total rock volume. Typical ranges: excellent >20%, good 15-20%, fair 10-15%, poor <10%.

attributes.name: charge_risk
attributes.description: Assessment of the risk that the play may not have received adequate hydrocarbon charge from the source rock. Low risk indicates proven charge; high risk indicates uncertain or inadequate charge.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the play record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: depth_range_base_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Depth Range Base Feet (ft) True Vertical Depth (TVD)
attributes.description: Deepest true vertical depth (TVD) at which the play reservoir is encountered across the basin, measured in feet subsea or below surface.

attributes.name: depth_range_top_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Depth Range Top Feet (ft) True Vertical Depth (TVD)
attributes.description: Shallowest true vertical depth (TVD) at which the play reservoir is encountered across the basin, measured in feet subsea or below surface.

attributes.name: discovery_count
attributes.description: Number of commercial hydrocarbon discoveries made within the play to date. Used to assess play maturity and success rate.

attributes.name: dry_hole_count
attributes.description: Number of unsuccessful exploration wells drilled in the play. Used to calculate exploration success rate and refine geological models.

attributes.name: exploration_success_rate_percent
attributes.description: Historical success rate for exploration wells in the play, calculated as discoveries divided by total wells drilled, expressed as a percentage.

attributes.name: geological_chance_of_success_percent
attributes.description: Probability that the play contains commercial hydrocarbons, expressed as a percentage. Calculated as the product of individual risk factors (trap, seal, source, reservoir, charge). Typical exploration plays range 10-40%.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_type
attributes.description: Primary hydrocarbon phase expected in the play. Oil plays target liquid petroleum; gas plays target natural gas; condensate plays target gas with liquid dropout; mixed plays contain both oil and gas zones.

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: Date when the play concept was first identified and entered into the exploration portfolio. Used for tracking play lifecycle and portfolio vintage analysis.

attributes.name: last_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent technical and resource assessment of the play. Plays should be reassessed periodically as new data becomes available.

attributes.name: migration_pathway
attributes.description: Description of the route hydrocarbons traveled from source rock to reservoir (e.g., 'vertical migration along fault planes', 'lateral migration through carrier beds'). Critical for understanding charge risk.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the play record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal review and update of the play assessment. Ensures plays remain current in the exploration portfolio.

attributes.name: play_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code for the play used in Landmark DecisionSpace and internal exploration systems for consistent identification across G&G workflows.

attributes.name: play_name
attributes.description: Business name of the petroleum play, typically reflecting the reservoir formation and trap style (e.g., 'Wolfcamp Shale Unconventional', 'Norphlet Sandstone Structural').

attributes.name: play_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the play. Active plays are under active exploration or development; mature plays have established production; emerging plays are newly identified; dormant plays are on hold; abandoned plays are no longer pursued.

attributes.name: play_type
attributes.description: Classification of the play based on reservoir characteristics and production mechanism. Conventional plays rely on natural permeability; unconventional plays require stimulation (hydraulic fracturing, horizontal drilling).

attributes.name: prms_maturity_subclass
attributes.business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Maturity Subclass
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS maturity subclass. Lead is early-stage; prospect is drill-ready; 1P/2P/3P are proved/probable/possible reserves categories.

attributes.name: prms_resource_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Resource Class
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS resource classification. Prospective resources are undiscovered; contingent resources are discovered but not yet commercial; reserves are discovered and commercial.

attributes.name: reservoir_lithology
attributes.description: Dominant rock type of the reservoir. Sandstone and carbonate reservoirs typically have higher permeability; shale reservoirs require hydraulic fracturing.

attributes.name: reservoir_quality
attributes.description: Overall assessment of reservoir porosity and permeability. Excellent quality reservoirs have high porosity and permeability; poor quality reservoirs require stimulation or enhanced recovery.

attributes.name: risked_resource_estimate_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Risked Resource Estimate Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent (MMBOE)
attributes.description: Play-level risked resource estimate in million barrels of oil equivalent (MMBOE). Incorporates geological chance of success and expected recoverable volumes. Aligned with SPE-PRMS probabilistic resource assessment methodology.

attributes.name: seal_integrity
attributes.description: Assessment of the seals effectiveness in retaining hydrocarbons. Proven seals have demonstrated retention in producing fields; uncertain seals carry higher exploration risk.

attributes.name: seal_type
attributes.description: Type of impermeable rock that prevents hydrocarbon migration out of the reservoir. Shale and evaporite seals are most common; fault seals can be effective in some settings.

attributes.name: seismic_coverage_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of the play area covered by 3D seismic surveys. High seismic coverage reduces geological risk and improves prospect definition.

attributes.name: source_rock_formation
attributes.description: Geological formation that generated the hydrocarbons in the play. May be the same as the reservoir formation (self-sourced) or a separate formation (migrated).

attributes.name: source_rock_maturity
attributes.description: Thermal maturity level of the source rock, indicating the stage of hydrocarbon generation. Peak oil window generates liquid petroleum; gas window generates natural gas; overmature rocks have expelled most hydrocarbons.

attributes.name: technical_maturity_level
attributes.description: Assessment of the plays technical understanding and data coverage. Conceptual plays have limited data; mature plays have extensive seismic, well, and production data.

attributes.name: trap_configuration
attributes.description: Detailed description of the trap geometry (e.g., 'four-way dip closure', 'fault-bounded anticline', 'pinchout against unconformity'). Used for prospect mapping and risk assessment.

attributes.name: trap_style
attributes.description: Mechanism by which hydrocarbons are trapped in the play. Structural traps are formed by faulting or folding; stratigraphic traps by depositional or diagenetic changes; combination traps involve both; unconventional plays have no discrete trap.

attributes.name: unrisked_resource_estimate_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Unrisked Resource Estimate Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent (MMBOE)
attributes.description: Play-level unrisked (gross) resource estimate in million barrels of oil equivalent (MMBOE), assuming all geological risks are successful. Used for upside scenario planning.

attributes.name: well_control_density
attributes.description: Assessment of well penetration density within the play. Dense well control provides high confidence in reservoir properties; sparse control increases uncertainty.

products.name: prospect
products.description: Master record for individual drillable prospects identified within a play. Captures prospect name, location (latitude/longitude/block), trap type, structural closure area, gross rock volume (GRV), net-to-gross ratio, porosity, hydrocarbon saturation, formation volume factor, risked and unrisked STOIIP/GIIP estimates, geological chance of success (GCoS), and PRMS resource classification (1P/2P/3P). SSOT for prospect identity and resource potential. Integrates with Schlumberger Petrel 3D modeling.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.formation. Business justification: Prospects target specific reservoir formations. Currently prospect has reservoir_formation (STRING) and reservoir_age (STRING); these should be replaced with a FK to the formation master to ensure con

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Prospects that advance to drilling or detailed evaluation become capital projects tracked via WBS elements for project accounting, cost control, and capitalization decisions. Essential for project eco

attributes.description: Timestamp when the prospect record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: estimated_drill_cost_usd
attributes.description: Estimated cost to drill and complete the prospect well in US dollars. Used for AFE preparation and capital allocation decisions. Business-confidential financial data.

attributes.name: eur_p10_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) P10 Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent
attributes.description: P10 (high case) estimate of recoverable hydrocarbon volume in million barrels of oil equivalent. Represents optimistic reserves scenario.

attributes.name: eur_p50_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) P50 Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent
attributes.description: P50 (median) estimate of recoverable hydrocarbon volume in million barrels of oil equivalent. Represents 2P (proved plus probable) reserves classification.

attributes.name: eur_p90_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) P90 Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent
attributes.description: P90 (low case) estimate of recoverable hydrocarbon volume in million barrels of oil equivalent. Represents conservative reserves scenario.

attributes.name: formation_volume_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of reservoir volume to surface volume for the hydrocarbon phase. Estimated from PVT correlations and analog field data. Used to convert STOIIP to recoverable reserves.

attributes.name: geological_chance_of_success_pct
attributes.description: Probability that all geological risk factors (trap, reservoir, seal, source, timing/migration) are present and effective. Expressed as percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Used to calculate risked resource estimates.

attributes.name: geophysicist_name
attributes.description: Name of the lead geophysicist responsible for seismic interpretation and depth conversion. Used for accountability and technical review.

attributes.name: giip_unrisked_bcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas Initially in Place (GIIP) Unrisked Billion Cubic Feet
attributes.description: Unrisked estimate of original gas in place in billion cubic feet. Calculated from volumetric parameters before applying geological chance of success.

attributes.name: gross_rock_volume_mmcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Rock Volume (GRV) Million Cubic Feet
attributes.description: Total rock volume within the structural closure in million cubic feet. Calculated from seismic interpretation and depth structure maps in Petrel.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Average hydrocarbon saturation (1 minus water saturation) as a fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Estimated from analog well logs and petrophysical models.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_type
attributes.description: Expected hydrocarbon phase in the prospect: oil, gas, condensate, or mixed. Drives economic evaluation and facility design assumptions.

attributes.name: interpretation_date
attributes.description: Date when the G&G interpretation and prospect evaluation were completed. Used for tracking prospect vintage and re-evaluation cycles.

attributes.name: maturity_level
attributes.description: Maturity classification: lead (early stage, low confidence), prospect (G&G analysis complete), or drillable prospect (AFE approved, ready to drill).

attributes.name: net_to_gross_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of net reservoir thickness to gross interval thickness. Derived from analog well log analysis and petrophysical modeling. Range 0.0 to 1.0.

attributes.name: porosity_fraction
attributes.description: Average reservoir porosity as a fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Estimated from seismic inversion, analog wells, and core data. Key input for STOIIP/GIIP calculation.

attributes.name: prms_resource_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Resource Classification
attributes.description: SPE PRMS classification of the prospect resource: 1P (proved), 2P (proved plus probable), 3P (proved plus probable plus possible), contingent, prospective, or unrecoverable. Used for SEC reserves disclosure.

attributes.name: prospect_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the prospect for tracking across Landmark DecisionSpace and Schlumberger Petrel systems. Used in AFE and JIB documentation.

attributes.name: prospect_name
attributes.description: Business name assigned to the prospect for identification and communication purposes. Human-readable label used in exploration planning and AFE documentation.

attributes.name: prospect_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the prospect: identified (initial screening), evaluated (G&G analysis complete), matured (ready for drilling decision), drilled (well spudded), or abandoned (dropped from portfolio).

attributes.name: reservoir_risk_factor
attributes.description: Probability that reservoir quality (porosity, permeability) is adequate for commercial production (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

attributes.name: seal_risk_factor
attributes.description: Probability that an effective seal (cap rock) is present to prevent hydrocarbon migration (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

attributes.name: source_risk_factor
attributes.description: Probability that mature source rock is present and has generated sufficient hydrocarbons (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

attributes.name: stoiip_unrisked_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially in Place (STOIIP) Unrisked Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent
attributes.description: Unrisked estimate of original oil in place in million barrels of oil equivalent. Calculated from volumetric parameters before applying geological chance of success.

attributes.name: structural_closure_area_acres
attributes.description: Areal extent of the structural closure at the spill point in acres. Key input for volumetric resource calculation and STOIIP/GIIP estimation.

attributes.name: surface_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the prospect surface location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and regulatory filing.

attributes.name: surface_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the prospect surface location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping and regulatory filing.

attributes.name: target_depth_tvd_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Target Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD) Feet
attributes.description: True vertical depth to the top of the reservoir target in feet below surface or seabed. Used for drilling cost estimation and well planning.

attributes.name: timing_migration_risk_factor
attributes.description: Probability that hydrocarbon generation, migration, and trap formation occurred in the correct sequence (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

attributes.name: trap_risk_factor
attributes.description: Probability that a valid hydrocarbon trap exists (0.0 to 1.0). Component of geological chance of success calculation.

attributes.name: trap_type
attributes.description: Classification of the hydrocarbon trapping mechanism: structural (anticline, fault block), stratigraphic (pinchout, unconformity), combination, or hydrodynamic.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the prospect record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: water_depth_ft
attributes.description: Water depth at the prospect surface location in feet. Applicable for offshore prospects. Used for drilling cost estimation and rig selection.

products.name: lead
products.description: Master record for exploration leads — early-stage hydrocarbon accumulation concepts not yet matured to drillable prospect status. Captures lead name, play association, maturation stage (identified/screened/evaluated), data requirements for promotion to prospect, risked resource range (low/mid/high), lead-level geological risk factors, and screening-level economic indicators. Supports the lead-to-prospect maturation workflow, portfolio funnel management, and new ventures screening. Leads that mature are promoted to prospect records; leads that fail screening are archived with reason codes.

attributes.name: lead_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the exploration lead record. Primary key.

attributes.name: basin_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sedimentary basin in which the lead is located.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the geologist or geoscientist responsible for generating and evaluating the lead.

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Leads are identified on specific leased acreage. Land position (lease expiry, working interest, royalty burden) directly impacts lead screening economics, promotion decisions, and drilling rights. Ess

attributes.name: license_block_id
attributes.description: Reference to the exploration license or lease block in which the lead is located.

attributes.name: play_id
attributes.description: Reference to the geological play or petroleum system to which this lead belongs.

attributes.name: target_petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Leads identify expected hydrocarbon product type early in exploration workflow. Drives screening economics using product-specific price assumptions and play fairway analysis. Real business process: le

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Leads that advance to evaluation stage (screening NPV/IRR tracked) become capital projects with WBS elements for cost tracking and investment decision support. Required for project accounting and capi

attributes.name: archive_reason_code
attributes.description: Reason code for archiving the lead if it fails screening or evaluation. Below Threshold: resource size too small; High Risk: GCoS below acceptable level; No Data: insufficient data to evaluate; Strategic Misfit: does not align with portfolio strategy; Regulatory Constraint: permitting or access issues; Other: other reasons.

attributes.name: archive_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the lead was archived, including technical, commercial, or strategic rationale.

attributes.name: archived_date
attributes.description: Date when the lead was archived and removed from active portfolio.

attributes.name: charge_risk_probability
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that hydrocarbons have been generated, migrated, and charged into the trap.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code where the lead is geographically located.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the lead record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: data_requirement_description
attributes.description: Description of additional seismic, well, or geological data required to mature the lead to prospect status. May include 3D seismic acquisition, reprocessing, or analog well data.

attributes.name: depth_subsea_m
attributes.description: Estimated depth of the target reservoir below sea level in meters. Negative values indicate above sea level.

attributes.name: estimated_capex_mm_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Capital Expenditure (Million United States Dollars)
attributes.description: Preliminary estimate of total capital expenditure required to develop the lead if promoted to prospect and drilled, in million USD.

attributes.name: estimated_opex_mm_usd_per_year
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Operating Expenditure (Million United States Dollars per Year)
attributes.description: Preliminary estimate of annual operating expenditure in million USD per year if the lead is developed.

attributes.name: evaluated_date
attributes.description: Date when detailed evaluation of the lead was completed.

attributes.name: geological_chance_of_success
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that all geological risk factors are favorable and the lead contains moveable hydrocarbons. Product of trap, reservoir, seal, and charge probabilities.

attributes.name: gross_rock_volume_mm3
attributes.description: Estimated total rock volume of the lead structure in million cubic meters.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Estimated average hydrocarbon saturation in the reservoir pore space as a fraction (0 to 1). One minus water saturation.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_type
attributes.description: Expected hydrocarbon phase in the lead accumulation. Oil: liquid petroleum; Gas: natural gas; Condensate: gas condensate; Mixed: oil and gas.

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: Date when the lead was first identified and entered into the exploration portfolio.

attributes.name: lead_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned to the lead for tracking and reference in exploration systems and reports.

attributes.name: lead_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation assigned to the exploration lead for identification and communication purposes.

attributes.name: lead_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the lead. Active: under active evaluation; On Hold: evaluation paused pending data or strategic decision; Archived: no longer being pursued; Promoted: matured to prospect.

attributes.name: lead_type
attributes.description: Geological classification of the lead based on trap mechanism. Structural: fault or fold trap; Stratigraphic: depositional or diagenetic trap; Combination: both structural and stratigraphic elements; Unconventional: shale, tight gas, or coalbed methane.

attributes.name: maturation_stage
attributes.description: Current stage in the lead-to-prospect maturation workflow. Identified: initial concept captured; Screened: passed preliminary technical and commercial filters; Evaluated: detailed subsurface and economic analysis completed; Promoted: advanced to prospect status; Archived: failed screening or evaluation.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the lead record was last modified.

attributes.name: net_to_gross_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio (0 to 1) of net reservoir thickness to gross interval thickness. Represents proportion of pay zone within the total interval.

attributes.name: porosity_fraction
attributes.description: Estimated average porosity of the reservoir rock as a fraction (0 to 1). Represents pore volume as percentage of total rock volume.

attributes.name: promoted_date
attributes.description: Date when the lead was promoted to prospect status and became a drillable candidate.

attributes.name: promotion_criteria
attributes.description: Business and technical criteria that must be met for the lead to be promoted to drillable prospect status. May include minimum resource size, GCoS threshold, NPV hurdle, or strategic fit.

attributes.name: recovery_factor
attributes.description: Estimated fraction (0 to 1) of in-place hydrocarbons that can be economically recovered using primary and secondary recovery methods.

attributes.name: reservoir_risk_probability
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that reservoir rock with adequate porosity and permeability is present.

attributes.name: resource_high_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimate High Case (Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: High-case (P10) risked resource estimate for the lead in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents optimistic scenario.

attributes.name: resource_low_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimate Low Case (Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: Low-case (P90) risked resource estimate for the lead in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents conservative scenario.

attributes.name: resource_mid_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Resource Estimate Mid Case (Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: Mid-case (P50) risked resource estimate for the lead in barrels of oil equivalent. Represents most likely scenario.

attributes.name: screened_date
attributes.description: Date when the lead passed preliminary screening and was advanced to evaluation stage.

attributes.name: screening_irr_percent
attributes.description: Preliminary internal rate of return estimate as a percentage based on screening-level economic assumptions.

attributes.name: screening_npv_mm_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Screening Net Present Value (Million United States Dollars)
attributes.description: Preliminary net present value estimate in million USD based on screening-level economic assumptions. Used for portfolio ranking and prioritization.

attributes.name: seal_risk_probability
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that an effective seal (cap rock) is present to prevent hydrocarbon migration.

attributes.name: timing_risk_probability
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that trap formation occurred before or during hydrocarbon migration.

attributes.name: trap_risk_probability
attributes.description: Probability (0 to 1) that a viable trap structure exists at the time of hydrocarbon migration.

attributes.name: water_depth_m
attributes.description: Water depth at the lead location in meters. Zero for onshore leads.

products.name: seismic_survey
products.description: Master record for seismic acquisition surveys (2D, 3D, 4D) including survey-level and line-level detail. Survey attributes: survey name, type, acquisition method (towed streamer, OBC, OBN, land vibroseis), survey area (sq km), vintage year, acquisition contractor, processing status, data quality rating, dominant frequency, fold coverage, and licensing terms. Line-level attributes: line name/number, shot point range, line length (km), azimuth, acquisition parameters (record length, sample interval, source type, receiver spacing), processing sequence, and interpretation status. SSOT for seismic survey identity, line inventory, and data management. Integrates with Landmark DecisionSpace seismic interpretation workflows.

attributes.name: seismic_survey_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the seismic survey record. Primary key for the seismic survey entity.
attributes.references: API RP 2A - Recommended Practice for Planning, Designing and Constructing Fixed Offshore Platforms

attributes.name: acquisition_contractor_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Seismic acquisition contractors (CGG, PGS, WesternGeco) are vendors providing specialized geophysical services - major procurement category requiring vendor qualification, contracts, and performance t

attributes.name: afe_budget_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.afe_budget. Business justification: Seismic acquisition requires AFE authorization - major capital expenditure requiring partner approval and budget tracking. Survey costs are AFE line items for JIB billing and cost recovery. No existin

attributes.name: asset_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.facility. Business justification: Seismic acquisition operations staged from production facilities (onshore bases, offshore platforms) for logistics, cost allocation, HSE coordination, and vessel/equipment mobilization planning. Role

attributes.name: basin_id
attributes.description: FK to exploration.basin

attributes.name: finance_afe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.finance_afe. Business justification: Seismic surveys are major capital expenditures requiring AFE authorization; each survey is approved via an AFE for budget control, cost tracking, and JV partner approval. Critical for capital expendit

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Seismic surveys are acquired over leased acreage. Surface access rights, environmental permits, and data ownership are tied to lease agreements. Required for cost allocation, regulatory compliance, an

attributes.name: permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.permit. Business justification: Seismic operations require environmental permits (marine mammal protection, NEPA clearances) and regulatory approvals before acquisition. Standard HSE compliance requirement. Links survey to its envir

attributes.name: acquisition_end_date
attributes.description: Date when field acquisition operations were completed for this seismic survey. Used to calculate acquisition duration and assess data currency.

attributes.name: acquisition_method
attributes.description: Physical method used to acquire seismic data. Towed streamer for marine surveys with hydrophone cables, OBC (Ocean Bottom Cable) for seabed cable systems, OBN (Ocean Bottom Node) for autonomous seabed nodes, land vibroseis for truck-mounted vibrator sources, land dynamite for explosive sources, transition zone for shallow water/marsh environments, borehole for VSP and crosswell surveys. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: towed_streamer|OBC|OBN|land_vibroseis|land_dynamite|transition_zone|borehole — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Seismic Acquisition Methods

attributes.name: acquisition_start_date
attributes.description: Date when field acquisition operations commenced for this seismic survey. Marks the beginning of the survey lifecycle and is used for project tracking and data vintage assessment.

attributes.name: bin_size_m
attributes.description: Spatial grid cell size for 3D seismic data binning measured in meters. Defines the horizontal resolution of the processed seismic volume. Common values: 12.5 m x 12.5 m for high-resolution surveys, 25 m x 25 m for standard surveys.

attributes.name: coordinate_system
attributes.description: Spatial reference system used for survey positioning and navigation (e.g., WGS84, NAD83, UTM Zone 15N, State Plane). Critical for integration with well data, lease boundaries, and GIS workflows.
attributes.references: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset - Coordinate Reference Systems

attributes.name: cost_usd
attributes.description: Total capital expenditure for seismic survey acquisition, processing, and interpretation measured in United States Dollars. Used for AFE (Authorization for Expenditure) tracking, joint venture billing, and economic analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this seismic survey record was first created in the data management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_format
attributes.description: Digital file format standard used for seismic data storage and exchange. SEG-Y for Society of Exploration Geophysicists Y-format (industry standard), SEG-D for field recording format, SEG-2 for legacy format, SEGY_Rev1/Rev2 for specific revisions, proprietary for vendor-specific formats.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - SEG-Y Rev 2.0 Data Exchange Format

attributes.name: data_quality_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of overall seismic data quality based on signal-to-noise ratio, imaging clarity, structural resolution, and interpretability. Used by geophysicists to determine fitness for prospect evaluation and reserves booking.

attributes.name: data_volume_tb
attributes.description: Total size of seismic data volume measured in terabytes. Includes raw field data, processed volumes, and interpretation products. Used for storage planning and data transfer logistics.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Data Volume Metrics

attributes.name: datum_elevation_m
attributes.description: Vertical reference elevation for seismic time-depth conversion measured in meters relative to mean sea level. Used to tie seismic data to well logs and subsurface geological models.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Vertical Datum Specifications

attributes.name: dominant_frequency_hz
attributes.description: Peak frequency content of the seismic wavelet measured in Hertz. Determines vertical resolution capability and is critical for thin bed detection and reservoir characterization. Typical ranges: 15-40 Hz for deep targets, 40-80 Hz for shallow reservoirs.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Seismic Resolution Metrics

attributes.name: environmental_clearance_date
attributes.description: Date when environmental impact assessment and regulatory clearances were obtained for seismic acquisition operations. Required for HSE compliance and permitting workflows.
attributes.references: EPA National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) Compliance

attributes.name: fold_coverage
attributes.description: Number of times each subsurface point is sampled during seismic acquisition, representing the redundancy and stacking power of the survey. Higher fold improves signal-to-noise ratio. Typical values: 30-60 fold for 3D surveys, 6-12 fold for 2D surveys.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Acquisition Design Parameters

attributes.name: interpretation_status
attributes.description: Current stage of geological and geophysical interpretation workflow. Not_started for uninterpreted data, in_progress for active interpretation, preliminary for initial interpretation results, final for completed interpretation, peer_reviewed for QC-validated interpretation ready for prospect generation.

attributes.name: licensing_terms
attributes.description: Commercial ownership and usage rights model for the seismic data. Proprietary for company-owned exclusive data, multi-client for shared-cost industry surveys, open_file for publicly available data, licensed for third-party data under license agreement, exclusive for sole access rights, non-exclusive for shared access with other licensees.
attributes.references: BOEM Data and Information Management Requirements

attributes.name: migration_type
attributes.description: Seismic imaging algorithm applied to position reflectors to their true subsurface locations. None for unmigrated data, post-stack_time for stacked time migration, pre-stack_time for PSTM, post-stack_depth for stacked depth migration, pre-stack_depth for PSDM, RTM for reverse-time migration, Kirchhoff for Kirchhoff migration, beam for beam migration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|post-stack_time|pre-stack_time|post-stack_depth|pre-stack_depth|RTM|Kirchhoff|beam — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this seismic survey record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data governance workflows.

attributes.name: play_type
attributes.description: Geological play classification targeted by the seismic survey (e.g., structural trap, stratigraphic trap, unconventional shale, deepwater turbidite, carbonate reef). Aligns survey data with exploration strategy and prospect generation workflows.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Play and Prospect Classification

attributes.name: processing_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when final seismic data processing was completed and deliverable products were generated. Indicates when data became available for interpretation and prospect evaluation.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Data Delivery Requirements

attributes.name: processing_contractor
attributes.description: Name of the seismic processing contractor or service company that performed data processing workflows (e.g., WesternGeco, CGG, PGS, ION Geophysical). May differ from acquisition contractor.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Processing Vendor Requirements

attributes.name: processing_sequence
attributes.description: Summary description of the seismic processing workflow and key algorithms applied (e.g., demultiple, velocity analysis, migration type, noise attenuation methods). Used for data quality assessment and reprocessing decisions.

attributes.name: processing_status
attributes.description: Current stage of seismic data processing. Raw for unprocessed field data, pre-stack for data before stack, post-stack for stacked data, PSDM (Pre-Stack Depth Migration) for advanced depth imaging, PSTM (Pre-Stack Time Migration) for time-domain migration, final for deliverable product, reprocessed for data that has undergone modern reprocessing workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: raw|pre-stack|post-stack|PSDM|PSTM|final|reprocessed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Seismic Data Processing Workflows

attributes.name: receiver_spacing_m
attributes.description: Distance between adjacent receiver stations or hydrophone groups measured in meters. Determines spatial sampling density and horizontal resolution. Typical values: 12.5-25 m for 3D surveys, 50-100 m for 2D surveys.

attributes.name: record_length_ms
attributes.description: Total recording time for each seismic trace measured in milliseconds. Determines the maximum depth of investigation. Typical values: 6000-12000 ms for deep exploration targets, 3000-6000 ms for shallow development surveys.

attributes.name: sample_interval_ms
attributes.description: Time sampling rate for seismic data recording measured in milliseconds. Determines temporal resolution and Nyquist frequency. Standard values: 2 ms or 4 ms for conventional surveys, 1 ms for high-resolution surveys.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Digital Sampling Requirements

attributes.name: shot_point_interval_m
attributes.description: Distance between successive seismic source activation points measured in meters. Controls subsurface sampling density and fold coverage. Typical values: 25-50 m for 3D surveys, 50-100 m for 2D surveys.

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: Type of seismic energy source used for signal generation. Airgun for marine compressed air sources, vibroseis for truck-mounted vibrators, dynamite for explosive sources, weight_drop for accelerated weight impact, sparker for high-resolution marine surveys, boomer for shallow water surveys.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Seismic Source Specifications

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Physical or cloud storage location where seismic data volumes are archived (e.g., tape library, disk array, cloud object storage path). Used for data management and retrieval workflows.

attributes.name: survey_area_sq_km
attributes.description: Total geographic area covered by the seismic survey measured in square kilometers. For 2D surveys, represents the bounding box area; for 3D surveys, represents the actual acquisition footprint.

attributes.name: survey_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation assigned to the seismic survey for identification and reference purposes.

attributes.name: survey_type
attributes.description: Classification of the seismic survey based on dimensionality and acquisition geometry. 2D for two-dimensional line surveys, 3D for three-dimensional volume surveys, 4D for time-lapse repeat surveys, VSP for vertical seismic profile, multi-component for shear wave acquisition, ocean_bottom for OBC/OBN surveys.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards Committee - Seismic Data Acquisition Standards

attributes.name: total_line_count
attributes.description: Total number of seismic lines acquired in the survey. For 2D surveys, represents the number of individual lines; for 3D surveys, represents the number of inline and crossline directions combined.

attributes.name: total_line_km
attributes.description: Cumulative length of all seismic lines in the survey measured in kilometers. Used for project scope quantification, cost estimation, and acquisition progress tracking.

attributes.name: velocity_model_type
attributes.description: Type of velocity model used for seismic imaging and depth conversion. Constant for simple single-velocity model, layered for interval velocity model, tomography for tomographic inversion, FWI (Full Waveform Inversion) for advanced velocity building, anisotropic for VTI/TTI models, isotropic for standard velocity models.
attributes.references: SEG Technical Standards - Velocity Model Building

attributes.name: vintage_year
attributes.description: Calendar year when the seismic survey was acquired in the field. Used to assess data currency and technology generation for interpretation and prospect evaluation.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Data Quality and Vintage Requirements

attributes.name: water_depth_m
attributes.description: Average water depth in meters for marine seismic surveys. Critical parameter for acquisition planning, processing velocity models, and operational feasibility assessment. Null for land surveys.

products.name: seismic_line

attributes.name: seismic_line_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the seismic line record. Primary key for the seismic line entity.

attributes.name: acquisition_cost_usd

attributes.name: acquisition_end_date

attributes.name: acquisition_status

attributes.name: azimuth_degrees

attributes.name: data_storage_location

attributes.name: end_longitude
