attributes.name: actual_fluid_loss_ml_per_30min
attributes.description: Actual API fluid loss measured during drilling operations in milliliters per 30 minutes. Captured from daily mud checks and lab analysis.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_mud_weight_ppg
attributes.description: Actual mud weight (density) measured during drilling operations in pounds per gallon (ppg). Captured from daily drilling reports and mud checks.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_oil_water_ratio
attributes.description: Actual ratio of oil phase to water phase measured during drilling operations for invert emulsion muds. Captured from retort analysis.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_ph
attributes.description: Actual pH measured during drilling operations. Captured from daily mud checks and lab analysis.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_plastic_viscosity_cp
attributes.description: Actual plastic viscosity (PV) measured during drilling operations in centipoise. Calculated from 600 RPM and 300 RPM viscometer readings.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_solids_content_percent
attributes.description: Actual total solids content measured during drilling operations as a percentage by volume. Captured from retort analysis.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_viscosity_seconds
attributes.description: Actual viscosity measured during drilling operations in Marsh funnel seconds. Captured from daily mud checks and lab analysis.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: actual_yield_point_lb_per_100sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Yield Point (Pounds Per 100 Square Feet)
attributes.description: Actual yield point (YP) measured during drilling operations in pounds per 100 square feet. Calculated from viscometer readings (300 RPM reading minus PV).
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the mud program was formally approved by the drilling engineer, operations manager, or regulatory authority. Required before implementation.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name and title of the person who approved the mud program. Typically the drilling engineer, operations manager, or well site leader.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: co2_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether carbon dioxide gas is expected in the formations to be drilled. True if CO2 is present, which can cause carbonic acid formation and pH reduction in water-based muds.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: completion_date
attributes.description: Date when drilling of this hole section was completed and the mud program was no longer active. Typically when casing is set or total depth is reached.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this mud program record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: design_chloride_content_mg_per_l
attributes.description: Target chloride ion concentration in milligrams per liter. Critical for saltwater muds and inhibitive systems. High chloride content indicates salt contamination or intentional salt addition for shale inhibition.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_date
attributes.description: Date when the mud program was designed and documented. Typically completed during the well planning phase before spud.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_fluid_loss_ml_per_30min
attributes.description: Target API fluid loss (filtrate volume) in milliliters per 30 minutes at 100 psi differential pressure. Controls formation damage and filter cake quality. Lower values indicate better filtration control.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_gel_strength_10min_lb_per_100sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Gel Strength 10-Minute (Pounds Per 100 Square Feet)
attributes.description: Target gel strength measured after 10 minutes of static conditions in pounds per 100 square feet. Higher values indicate progressive gelation which can cause circulation problems.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_gel_strength_10sec_lb_per_100sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Gel Strength 10-Second (Pounds Per 100 Square Feet)
attributes.description: Target gel strength measured after 10 seconds of static conditions in pounds per 100 square feet. Indicates the mud's ability to suspend cuttings when circulation stops.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_mud_weight_max_ppg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Mud Weight Maximum (Pounds Per Gallon)
attributes.description: Maximum planned mud weight (density) for this hole section in pounds per gallon (ppg). Must not exceed fracture gradient to prevent lost circulation.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_mud_weight_min_ppg
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Mud Weight Minimum (Pounds Per Gallon)
attributes.description: Minimum planned mud weight (density) for this hole section in pounds per gallon (ppg). Must be sufficient to provide hydrostatic pressure to control formation fluids and prevent kicks.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_oil_water_ratio
attributes.description: Target ratio of oil phase to water phase for invert emulsion muds (oil-based and synthetic-based). Expressed as oil:water (e.g., 80:20, 75:25). Higher oil content provides better shale inhibition but increases cost and environmental impact.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_ph_max
attributes.description: Maximum target pH level for the mud system. Excessive pH can cause formation damage and chemical instability.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_ph_min
attributes.description: Minimum target pH level for the mud system. Controls corrosion, chemical stability, and solubility of additives. Typical range 8.5-10.5 for water-based muds.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_plastic_viscosity_cp
attributes.description: Target plastic viscosity (PV) in centipoise, representing the viscosity of the mud when extrapolated to infinite shear rate. Part of the Bingham plastic rheological model.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_solids_content_percent
attributes.description: Target total solids content as a percentage by volume. Includes both low-gravity solids (drilled cuttings) and high-gravity solids (barite, hematite). Excessive solids reduce drilling efficiency.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_viscosity_target_seconds
attributes.description: Target viscosity for the mud system measured in Marsh funnel seconds. Controls the mud's ability to suspend cuttings and transport them to surface.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: design_yield_point_lb_per_100sqft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Design Yield Point (Pounds Per 100 Square Feet)
attributes.description: Target yield point (YP) in pounds per 100 square feet, representing the stress required to initiate flow. Part of the Bingham plastic rheological model. Critical for hole cleaning and cuttings suspension.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: environmental_disposal_classification
attributes.description: Approved method for disposal of spent drilling fluid and cuttings. Overboard discharge is permitted for water-based muds in offshore operations meeting EPA and BSEE toxicity limits. Oil-based and synthetic-based muds require onshore disposal, re-injection, or thermal treatment.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 435 Oil and Gas Extraction Point Source Category; BSEE NTL 2012-G05

attributes.name: h2s_concentration_ppm
attributes.description: Expected concentration of hydrogen sulfide in formation gas in parts per million (ppm). Concentrations above 10 ppm require H2S scavengers in the mud system. Concentrations above 100 ppm require enhanced safety protocols.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000

attributes.name: h2s_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether hydrogen sulfide gas is expected in the formations to be drilled. True if H2S is present, requiring specialized mud additives (H2S scavengers) and safety procedures.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000

attributes.name: hole_section_code
attributes.description: Reference to the specific hole section (e.g., surface, intermediate, production) for which this mud program applies. Links to the hole section master record.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: hpht_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the well environment based on pressure and temperature conditions. HPHT wells (>10,000 psi and >300°F) require specialized mud formulations with thermal stability and pressure resistance. Extreme HPHT exceeds 15,000 psi or 400°F.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: implementation_date
attributes.description: Date when the mud program was put into active use during drilling operations. Marks the transition from design to execution.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this mud program record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: max_anticipated_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Anticipated Pressure (Pounds Per Square Inch)
attributes.description: Maximum formation pressure expected in this hole section in pounds per square inch (psi). Used to design mud weight window and well control procedures.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: max_anticipated_temperature_f
attributes.description: Maximum bottomhole temperature expected in this hole section in degrees Fahrenheit. High temperatures can degrade mud additives and affect rheological properties.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: mud_subtype
attributes.description: Detailed classification of the mud system within the primary type (e.g., freshwater gel, saltwater polymer, low-toxicity oil-based, ester-based synthetic, potassium chloride polymer).
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: mud_system_type
attributes.description: Primary classification of the drilling fluid system. Water-based mud (WBM) uses water as the continuous phase; oil-based mud (OBM) uses diesel or mineral oil; synthetic-based mud (SBM) uses synthetic hydrocarbons; pneumatic uses air or gas; foam uses aerated fluids.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: offshore_discharge_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the mud system is approved for overboard discharge in offshore operations. True if the mud meets EPA toxicity limits (96-hour LC50 >30,000 ppm) and BSEE discharge requirements. False if onshore disposal is required.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 435 Subpart A; BSEE NTL 2012-G05

attributes.name: program_revision_number
attributes.description: Version number of the mud program. Incremented each time the program is revised due to changes in formation conditions, well control requirements, or operational adjustments.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the mud program. Tracks progression from design through execution to completion.
attributes.references: API RP 13B-1 Recommended Practice for Field Testing of Drilling Fluids

attributes.name: wellbore_code
attributes.description: Reference to the specific wellbore (original, sidetrack, or re-entry) for this mud program. Links to the wellbore master record.

products.name: well_permit
products.description: Regulatory drilling permit record tracking all permits required to drill, complete, and operate a well. Captures permit type (APD - Application for Permit to Drill, sundry notice, workover permit, P&A permit), issuing regulatory body (BSEE, state oil and gas commission, EPA), permit number, application date, approval date, expiration date, permit conditions, bond amount, and permit status. Manages the regulatory approval lifecycle from initial APD submission through final well abandonment permit. Mandatory for BSEE offshore and state onshore compliance.
products.reference: BSEE APD Process / API RP 100-1 / State Oil and Gas Commission Regulations

attributes.name: well_permit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the well permit record. Primary key for the well permit entity.

attributes.name: block_id
attributes.description: FK to exploration.block

attributes.name: compliance_permit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.permit. Business justification: Drilling well permits should reference master compliance permit record for unified regulatory tracking. Enables consolidated permit management across drilling and compliance domains for audit and repo

attributes.name: designated_agent_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Well permits require designated agent employee for regulatory liaison with BSEE/state agencies, permit condition compliance, and inspection coordination. Replaces denormalized designated_agent text fi

attributes.name: drilling_well_id
attributes.description: Reference to the well for which this permit was issued. Links to the well master record in the drilling domain.

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: FK to drilling.field

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Drilling permits issued for specific leases. Permit applications require lease documentation, lessor consent verification, and lease term validation. Regulatory agencies require lease identification i

attributes.name: operator_customer_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_counterparty. Business justification: Well permits designate operator of record as legal entity. Required for: regulatory compliance (BSEE/state agency filings), operator designation changes, permit transfer workflows, bonding requirement

attributes.name: operator_id
attributes.description: FK to drilling.operator

attributes.name: well_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.well_asset. Business justification: Permits are regulatory documents tied to well asset for compliance tracking. Required for: regulatory audits, permit renewal tracking, compliance reporting, demonstrating authorization for well operat

attributes.name: well_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to drilling.well_program. Business justification: Well permit authorizes execution of a specific well program. The permit references the planned program details for regulatory approval. One permit authorizes one program. Removing attributes that are

attributes.name: actual_completion_date
attributes.description: Actual date when drilling and completion operations were finished. Must be reported to regulatory authority for permit closure.
attributes.references: BSEE Completion Reporting Requirements, State Well Completion Standards

attributes.name: actual_spud_date
attributes.description: Actual date when drilling operations commenced. Must be reported to regulatory authority and must fall within the permit validity period.
attributes.references: BSEE Drilling Notification Requirements, State Spud Reporting Standards

attributes.name: application_date
attributes.description: Date when the permit application was formally submitted to the regulatory authority. Used to track regulatory review timelines and compliance with submission deadlines.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Application Process, State Regulatory Filing Requirements

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the regulatory authority officially approved the permit. This is the effective start date for permit validity and the date from which operations may legally commence.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Approval Standards, State Regulatory Approval Process

attributes.name: approval_notes
attributes.description: Notes and comments from the regulatory authority regarding the permit approval, including any special instructions or clarifications.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Documentation Standards, State Regulatory Filing Requirements

attributes.name: bond_amount_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bond Amount in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Financial bond amount required by the regulatory authority to ensure proper well plugging and abandonment. Protects against environmental liability and ensures funds are available for proper well closure.
attributes.references: BSEE Bonding Requirements 30 CFR 556, State Oil and Gas Commission Bonding Standards

attributes.name: bond_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the financial bond instrument securing this permit. Used for tracking and verification of financial assurance.
attributes.references: BSEE Bond Management System, State Bond Tracking Standards

attributes.name: bond_type
attributes.description: Type of financial bond securing the permit. Individual Well Bond covers a single well, Blanket Bond covers multiple wells, Area-Wide Bond covers all wells in a geographic area, and Supplemental Bond provides additional coverage for high-risk wells.
attributes.value_regex: Individual Well Bond|Blanket Bond|Area-Wide Bond|Supplemental Bond
attributes.references: BSEE Bonding Requirements 30 CFR 556, State Bonding Classification Standards

attributes.name: bop_pressure_rating_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blowout Preventer (BOP) Pressure Rating in Pounds per Square Inch (psi)
attributes.description: Required pressure rating for the blowout preventer stack in pounds per square inch. Must meet or exceed maximum anticipated wellbore pressure for regulatory approval.
attributes.references: API Spec 16A BOP Standards, BSEE BOP Requirements 30 CFR 250

attributes.name: cancellation_date
attributes.description: Date when the permit was cancelled by either the operator or the regulatory authority. Used for permit lifecycle tracking and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Cancellation Process, State Regulatory Cancellation Standards

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the permit was cancelled. May include project abandonment, economic factors, or regulatory non-compliance.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Cancellation Documentation, State Regulatory Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standards, SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: denial_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the permit was denied by the regulatory authority. Used for resubmission planning and compliance improvement.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Denial Process, State Regulatory Appeal Standards

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the permit becomes legally effective and operations may begin. May differ from approval date if the permit has a delayed effective date specified by the regulatory authority.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Effective Date Guidelines, State Regulatory Standards

attributes.name: environmental_assessment_date
attributes.description: Date when the environmental assessment or environmental impact statement was completed and approved. Required before permit can be issued for environmentally sensitive areas.
attributes.references: NEPA Environmental Review Timeline, BSEE Environmental Approval Process

attributes.name: environmental_assessment_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an environmental assessment or environmental impact statement was required as part of the permit application process. True if environmental review was mandatory.
attributes.references: NEPA Environmental Assessment Requirements, BSEE Environmental Review Process

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the permit expires and is no longer valid for operations. Operations must be completed or a permit extension must be obtained before this date to maintain regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Duration Standards, State Regulatory Expiration Rules

attributes.name: extension_count
attributes.description: Number of times the permit has been extended beyond its original expiration date. Tracks regulatory accommodation history and potential compliance risk.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Extension Guidelines, State Regulatory Extension Policies

attributes.name: h2s_concentration_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Concentration in Parts Per Million (ppm)
attributes.description: Expected concentration of hydrogen sulfide in parts per million. Used to determine safety equipment requirements and emergency response planning.
attributes.references: API RP 49 H2S Concentration Standards, OSHA PEL Limits

attributes.name: h2s_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether hydrogen sulfide gas is expected to be present in the well. True if H2S is anticipated, requiring special safety equipment and procedures.
attributes.references: API RP 49 Safe Drilling of Wells Containing H2S, OSHA H2S Safety Standards

attributes.name: hpht_classification_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT) Classification Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the well is classified as High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT). True if the well meets HPHT criteria, requiring specialized equipment and procedures.
attributes.references: API HPHT Well Classification Standards, BSEE HPHT Requirements

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory body that issued or is reviewing the permit. Examples include BSEE (Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement) for offshore federal waters, state oil and gas commissions for onshore operations, or EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) for environmental permits.
attributes.references: BSEE Organizational Structure, State Oil and Gas Commission Directory

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The regulatory jurisdiction under which the permit falls. Determines which regulatory body has authority and which rules apply.
attributes.value_regex: Federal Offshore|State Onshore|State Offshore|Tribal Lands|Private Lands
attributes.references: BSEE Jurisdiction Guidelines, State Oil and Gas Commission Jurisdiction Maps

attributes.name: last_extension_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent permit extension approval. Used to track extension history and calculate current expiration date.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Extension Process, State Regulatory Extension Standards

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this permit record was last updated in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standards, SOX Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: offshore_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the well is located offshore (true) or onshore (false). Determines applicable regulatory framework and safety requirements.
attributes.references: BSEE Offshore vs Onshore Classification, State Jurisdiction Standards

attributes.name: permit_conditions
attributes.description: Specific conditions, restrictions, or stipulations imposed by the regulatory authority as part of the permit approval. May include environmental protections, operational restrictions, monitoring requirements, or seasonal limitations.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Conditions Standards, State Regulatory Stipulation Guidelines

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Official permit number assigned by the regulatory authority. This is the externally-known unique identifier for the permit used in all regulatory correspondence and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Numbering Standard, State Oil and Gas Commission Standards

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the permit. Tracks the permit from initial draft through regulatory approval, active operations, and final closure. Critical for compliance tracking and operational planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Draft|Submitted|Under Review|Approved|Denied|Expired|Suspended|Cancelled|Closed — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Lifecycle Management, State Regulatory Standards

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the permit based on the type of drilling or well operation activity. APD (Application for Permit to Drill) is for new wells, Sundry Notice for modifications, Workover Permit for well intervention, P&A (Plug and Abandonment) Permit for well closure, Sidetrack Permit for directional drilling from existing wellbore, and Recompletion Permit for changing production zones.
attributes.value_regex: APD|Sundry Notice|Workover Permit|P&A Permit|Sidetrack Permit|Recompletion Permit
attributes.references: BSEE NTL 2010-N06, State Regulatory Permit Classification Standards

attributes.name: planned_completion_date
attributes.description: Planned date to complete drilling and completion operations as stated in the permit application. Used for regulatory timeline compliance tracking.
attributes.references: BSEE Drilling Program Timeline Requirements, State Completion Standards

attributes.name: planned_spud_date
attributes.description: Planned date to spud (commence drilling) the well as stated in the permit application. Used for regulatory planning and rig scheduling coordination.
attributes.references: BSEE APD Requirements, State Drilling Plan Standards

attributes.name: reviewer_name
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory agency staff member assigned to review the permit application. Used for tracking and correspondence.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Review Process, State Regulatory Review Standards

attributes.name: surety_company
attributes.description: Name of the surety company or financial institution providing the bond. Must be an approved surety on the U.S. Department of Treasury list.
attributes.references: BSEE Approved Surety List, U.S. Department of Treasury Circular 570

attributes.name: surface_location_latitude
attributes.description: Latitude coordinate of the well surface location in decimal degrees. Used for geographic identification and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: API Well Location Standards, BSEE Geographic Coordinate Requirements

attributes.name: surface_location_longitude
attributes.description: Longitude coordinate of the well surface location in decimal degrees. Used for geographic identification and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: API Well Location Standards, BSEE Geographic Coordinate Requirements

attributes.name: suspension_reason
attributes.description: Reason why the permit was suspended by the regulatory authority. May include safety violations, environmental concerns, or administrative issues.
attributes.references: BSEE Permit Suspension Authority, State Regulatory Enforcement Standards

attributes.name: water_depth_ft
attributes.description: Water depth at the well location in feet for offshore wells. Critical for rig selection, BOP requirements, and regulatory classification (shallow water vs deepwater).
attributes.references: BSEE Water Depth Classification Standards, API Offshore Drilling Standards

products.name: dc_program
products.description: Drilling and Completion (D&C) program master record representing a portfolio-level grouping of wells planned and executed under a single capital program or development campaign. Captures program name, program type (exploration, appraisal, development, infill), field or block name, planned well count, approved total CAPEX, program start and end dates, program manager, and overall program status (planning, active, complete, deferred). Serves as the top-level organizing entity for rig schedules, AFEs, and well programs within a capital investment cycle. Enables portfolio-level D&C performance benchmarking and capital allocation reporting.

attributes.name: dc_program_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the drilling and completion program. Primary key for the D&C program master record.

attributes.name: compliance_regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Multi-well drilling programs require regulatory approval and reporting (development plans, environmental assessments). Program-level filings are common for field development and BSEE exploration plan

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Drilling campaigns are major capital programs tracked in cost centers for budget management and multi-well cost aggregation. New attribute needed; no existing candidate. Standard oil & gas practice.

attributes.name: dc_manager_person_employee_id
attributes.description: FK to workforce.employee

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Multi-well drilling campaigns in joint ventures require JOA governance. Operating committees approve programs, budget follows JOA terms, non-consent can apply at program level. Essential for tracking

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Multi-well drilling campaigns planned to fulfill lease development obligations and acreage retention requirements. Program budgets allocated per lease for working interest accounting. Standard practic

attributes.name: operator_customer_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_counterparty. Business justification: Drilling campaigns have designated operator entities for program-level governance. Required for: master service agreements, program-level JV agreements, regulatory program approvals, consolidated prog

attributes.name: primary_dc_employee_id
attributes.description: System identifier linking to the employee or contractor record of the program manager.

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Drilling campaigns map to WBS elements for multi-well project accounting and capital tracking. New attribute needed; no existing candidate. Standard oil & gas project accounting practice.

attributes.name: actual_duration_days
attributes.description: Actual total duration of the D&C program from start to completion, expressed in calendar days. Updated upon program completion.

attributes.name: actual_total_capex_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Actual Total Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Cumulative actual capital expenditure incurred to date across all wells and activities in the program. Updated from AFE actuals and JIB postings.

attributes.name: actual_well_count
attributes.description: Actual number of wells spudded or completed under this program to date. Updated as wells are drilled.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the D&C program and associated CAPEX budget were formally approved by the appropriate authority (management committee, board, or JV partners).

attributes.name: approved_total_capex_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Approved Total Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total capital expenditure budget approved for the D&C program, including all AFEs, rig costs, completion costs, and contingencies. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: authorization_basis
attributes.description: Business justification or strategic rationale for the D&C program (e.g., 'FY2024 Capital Plan', 'Board Resolution 2024-03', 'JV Development Agreement Commitment'). Links to governance and approval documentation.

attributes.name: average_planned_td_md_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Planned Total Depth (TD) Measured Depth (MD) in Feet
attributes.description: Average planned total depth (measured depth) across all wells in the program, expressed in feet. Used for program-level drilling performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: average_planned_td_tvd_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Planned Total Depth (TD) True Vertical Depth (TVD) in Feet
attributes.description: Average planned total depth (true vertical depth) across all wells in the program, expressed in feet. Used for subsurface planning and reserves estimation.

attributes.name: average_rig_day_rate_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Rig Day Rate in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Average daily rig rate across all rigs used in the program, expressed in USD. Used for cost benchmarking and budget variance analysis.

attributes.name: basin_name
attributes.description: Name of the geological basin or play where the program is located (e.g., 'Permian Basin', 'Gulf of Mexico', 'Williston Basin'). Used for portfolio-level basin analytics.

attributes.name: block_name
attributes.description: Lease block or concession area identifier where the program wells are located. Particularly relevant for offshore programs (e.g., 'Green Canyon Block 123', 'Mississippi Canyon 252').

attributes.name: budget_variance_percentage
attributes.description: Budget variance expressed as a percentage of approved CAPEX. Calculated as (actual - approved) / approved * 100.

attributes.name: budget_variance_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Budget Variance in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Variance between approved CAPEX and actual CAPEX (actual minus approved). Positive values indicate over-budget, negative values indicate under-budget.

attributes.name: contingency_percentage
attributes.description: Contingency reserve as a percentage of approved CAPEX, allocated for unforeseen costs, NPT, or scope changes. Typically ranges from 5% to 20% based on risk category.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the D&C program record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the program budget. Typically USD for international operations, but may vary by jurisdiction.

attributes.name: environmental_sensitivity_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the program area based on environmental sensitivity: standard (routine operations), sensitive (near protected areas), protected (within designated zones), or critical (endangered species habitat or cultural sites).

attributes.name: field_name
attributes.description: Name of the oil or gas field where the D&C program is being executed. For exploration programs, may reference the prospect or block name.

attributes.name: h2s_present_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether hydrogen sulfide (sour gas) is anticipated in the program wells. Drives HSE protocols, BOP specifications, and personnel safety requirements.

attributes.name: hpht_classification
attributes.description: Classification of the program based on anticipated downhole pressure and temperature conditions: standard (normal), HPHT (>10,000 psi or >300°F), extreme HPHT (>15,000 psi or >400°F), or not applicable.

attributes.name: joint_venture_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the joint venture or partnership under which the D&C program is being executed. Links to the JOA and partner working interest structure.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the D&C program record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: offshore_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the D&C program is offshore (true) or onshore (false). Drives regulatory reporting requirements and HSE protocols.

attributes.name: operator_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the operating company responsible for executing the D&C program. References the legal entity serving as operator under the JOA.

attributes.name: planned_duration_days
attributes.description: Planned total duration of the D&C program from start to completion, expressed in calendar days. Used for rig contract planning and schedule optimization.

attributes.name: planned_well_count
attributes.description: Total number of wells planned for drilling and completion under this program at the time of AFE approval. Used for portfolio planning and rig scheduling.

attributes.name: primary_rig_contractor
attributes.description: Name of the primary drilling contractor providing rig services for the program (e.g., 'Nabors', 'Helmerich & Payne', 'Transocean'). Used for vendor performance tracking.

attributes.name: program_end_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual end date of the D&C program, typically aligned with the last well TD and rig release or demobilization.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the drilling and completion program, typically reflecting the field, block, or development area (e.g., 'Eagle Ford 2024 Development Campaign', 'Offshore Block 15 Appraisal Program').

attributes.name: program_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the D&C program, typically used in external communications, AFE references, and capital planning documents. Unique across the organization.

attributes.name: program_start_date
attributes.description: Planned or actual start date of the D&C program, typically aligned with the first well spud date or rig mobilization.

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the D&C program: planning (pre-AFE), approved (AFE authorized), active (drilling in progress), suspended (temporarily halted), complete (all wells TD and released), cancelled (terminated before completion), or deferred (postponed to future period). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planning|approved|active|suspended|complete|cancelled|deferred — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Classification of the D&C program based on its strategic purpose: exploration (wildcat/new play), appraisal (delineation), development (field development), infill (incremental wells in producing field), workover (re-entry), or sidetrack (directional deviation from existing wellbore).

attributes.name: risk_category
attributes.description: Overall risk classification for the D&C program based on technical complexity, HSE exposure, regulatory environment, and geological uncertainty: low, medium, high, or critical.

attributes.name: target_formation
attributes.description: Primary geological formation or reservoir target for the D&C program (e.g., 'Wolfcamp A', 'Tuscaloosa Marine Shale', 'Niobrara'). Used for reserves classification and technical planning.

attributes.name: water_depth_ft
attributes.description: Average water depth for offshore programs, expressed in feet. Null for onshore programs. Used for rig selection and cost estimation.

attributes.name: well_trajectory_type
attributes.description: Predominant well trajectory type planned for the program: vertical (straight hole), directional (deviated), horizontal (lateral section), or multilateral (multiple laterals from single wellbore).

products.name: rig_contract
products.description: This association product represents the contractual relationship between a drilling rig and a vendor (drilling contractor or service provider). It captures the commercial terms, performance metrics, and temporal scope of each rig contracting agreement. Each record links one rig to one vendor for a specific contract period with attributes that exist only in the context of this contractual relationship, including day rates, mobilization fees, contract duration, and performance ratings.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas drilling operations, rigs are contracted from multiple vendors over the lifecycle of drilling programs, and vendors (drilling contractors) provide multiple rigs to operators under separate contractual agreements. Each rig-vendor relationship is governed by a distinct contract with specific commercial terms (day rates, standby rates, mobilization fees), temporal scope (contract start/end dates), and performance metrics. The business actively manages these contracts as operational entities, tracking costs, performance, and contract status.

attributes.name: rig_contract_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the rig_contract association

attributes.name: rig_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the drilling rig master record

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor master record (drilling contractor or service provider)

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: Scheduled end date of the rig contract period, after which terms may be renegotiated or the contract may be renewed

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the rig contract agreement, used for reference in procurement and drilling operations systems

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Effective start date of the rig contract period when the vendor begins providing the rig under the agreed terms

attributes.name: contract_status
attributes.description: Current status of the rig contract indicating whether it is currently in force, completed, prematurely terminated, or temporarily suspended

attributes.name: contract_type
attributes.description: Classification of the contractual arrangement defining the basis of payment and risk allocation between operator and contractor

attributes.name: day_rate_usd
attributes.description: Daily operating rate in USD charged by the vendor for the rig while actively drilling, representing the primary cost component of rig contracting

attributes.name: mobilization_fee_usd
attributes.description: One-time fee in USD charged by the vendor for mobilizing the rig to the drilling location at the start of the contract

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the vendor's performance in delivering rig services under this specific contract, used for future vendor selection and contract negotiations

attributes.name: standby_rate_usd
attributes.description: Daily rate in USD charged by the vendor when the rig is on standby (not actively drilling but available), typically lower than the operating day rate

products.name: afe_vendor_spend
products.description: This association product represents the financial relationship between an Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) and the vendors engaged to deliver services or materials for that AFE. It captures the contracted amounts, actual expenditures, purchase order activity, invoicing, and payment status for each vendor working on a specific AFE. Each record links one AFE to one vendor with financial tracking attributes that exist only in the context of this AFE-vendor engagement.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas drilling operations, a single AFE (Authorization for Expenditure) engages multiple vendors simultaneously—drilling contractors, completion service providers, equipment suppliers, cementing companies, directional drilling firms, logging services, and material suppliers. Conversely, each vendor serves multiple AFEs across different wells and projects. The business actively manages the financial relationship between each AFE and each vendor, tracking contracted amounts, actual spend, purchase orders, invoices, and payment status per AFE-vendor combination.

attributes.name: afe_vendor_spend_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Afe Vendor Spend - Afe Vendor Spend Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the afe_vendor_spend association

attributes.name: drilling_afe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the Authorization for Expenditure record for which this vendor provided services or materials.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor master record for the supplier or service provider engaged on this AFE.

attributes.name: actual_spend_usd
attributes.description: The cumulative actual expenditure in USD for this vendor on this AFE, aggregated from invoices and cost postings. Updated as invoices are received and processed. Used for variance analysis and budget control.

attributes.name: contracted_amount_usd
attributes.description: The total contracted or estimated amount in USD for this vendor's services or materials on this AFE, as specified in the purchase order or service agreement. Used for budget allocation and vendor commitment tracking.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this AFE-vendor spend record was created in the system, typically when the vendor was first engaged or a purchase order was issued for this AFE.

attributes.name: first_invoice_date
attributes.description: Date of the first invoice received from this vendor for this AFE. Marks the start of the financial relationship for this AFE-vendor engagement.

attributes.name: invoice_count
attributes.description: The number of invoices received from this vendor for this AFE. Used for accounts payable tracking and vendor payment processing.

attributes.name: last_invoice_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent invoice received from this vendor for this AFE. Used to track recency of vendor activity and billing cycles.

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current payment status for this vendor on this AFE: pending (no invoices yet), in progress (invoices received, payment processing), paid (all invoices settled), disputed (invoice or payment dispute), on hold (payment suspended). Used for cash flow management and vendor relations.

attributes.name: purchase_order_count
attributes.description: The number of purchase orders issued to this vendor for this AFE. Tracks procurement activity and vendor engagement complexity.

attributes.name: service_category
attributes.description: Classification of the type of service or material provided by this vendor for this AFE, aligned with AFE cost categories such as drilling services, completion services, oilfield equipment, cementing, directional services, logging, casing and tubing, mud and chemicals, bits, fuel, catering, or other.

attributes.name: updated_date
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this AFE-vendor spend record, reflecting changes to spend amounts, invoice counts, or payment status.

attributes.name: variance_amount_usd
attributes.description: Calculated variance between contracted amount and actual spend for this vendor on this AFE (actual_spend_usd - contracted_amount_usd). Positive values indicate overruns, negative values indicate underruns. Used for cost control and vendor performance analysis.

products.name: well_zone_completion
products.description: This association product represents the completion interval between a drilling well and a reservoir zone. It captures the physical connection established when a wellbore is perforated or completed to produce from a specific zone. Each record links one drilling well to one zone with attributes that describe the perforation interval, production contribution, and zone-specific performance metrics. This is a fundamental operational entity in reservoir management, production allocation, and reserves reporting.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas operations, wells routinely produce from multiple reservoir zones simultaneously (commingled production), and each zone is accessed by multiple wells as part of field development strategy. The well-zone completion is a fundamental operational entity that captures the physical perforation interval, production allocation percentages, zone-specific performance, and completion status. This relationship is actively managed by completion engineers and reservoir engineers for production optimization, reserves reporting, and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: well_zone_completion_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for this well-zone completion record. Primary key.

attributes.name: drilling_well_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Well Zone Completion - Drilling Well Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the drilling well that was completed in this zone

attributes.name: reservoir_zone_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Well Zone Completion - Reservoir Zone Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the reservoir zone accessed by this completion

attributes.name: completion_type
attributes.description: Type of completion method used to establish production from this zone. Determines flow characteristics and sand control approach.

attributes.name: cumulative_production_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Production Barrels of Oil Equivalent
attributes.description: Total cumulative production from this zone completion measured in barrels of oil equivalent (BOE). Tracks zone-specific production performance over the life of the completion.

attributes.name: first_production_date
attributes.description: Date when production from this specific zone completion first began. May differ from well completion date if zones were brought online sequentially or if this is a workover/recompletion.

attributes.name: last_production_date
attributes.description: Most recent date when production was recorded from this zone completion. Used to identify inactive or shut-in zones.

attributes.name: perforation_interval_bottom_md
attributes.description: Measured depth in feet to the bottom of the perforated interval for this zone completion. Defines the lower boundary of the physical connection between wellbore and zone.

attributes.name: perforation_interval_top_md
attributes.description: Measured depth in feet to the top of the perforated interval for this zone completion. Defines the upper boundary of the physical connection between wellbore and zone.

attributes.name: stimulation_method
attributes.description: Stimulation treatment applied to this zone completion (e.g., hydraulic fracturing, acidizing, none). Impacts productivity and EUR.

attributes.name: zone_contribution_fraction
attributes.description: Estimated fraction of total well production attributable to this zone, expressed as a decimal (0.0 to 1.0). Used for production allocation and reserves attribution when wells produce from multiple zones simultaneously (commingled production).

attributes.name: zone_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this specific zone completion. Tracks lifecycle from planned through active production to shut-in or abandonment. A well may have multiple zones with different statuses.

products.name: well_service_engagement
products.description: This association product represents the service engagement contract between a drilling well and a vendor. It captures the specific services provided by each vendor to each well throughout the drilling, completion, and workover lifecycle. Each record links one drilling well to one vendor with attributes that exist only in the context of this service relationship, including service type, contract reference, service period, costs, and performance metrics.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas drilling operations, each well engages multiple specialized vendors throughout its lifecycle (drilling contractor, cementing services, directional drilling, wireline, mud services, completion services, etc.), and each vendor serves multiple wells across the operator's portfolio. The business actively manages these service engagements as operational contracts, tracking service type, contract reference, service period, costs, and performance ratings for each well-vendor combination.

attributes.name: well_service_engagement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this well-vendor service engagement record. Primary key.

attributes.name: drilling_well_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Well Service Engagement - Drilling Well Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the drilling well receiving the service

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the vendor providing the service

attributes.name: contract_number
attributes.description: Reference to the master service agreement or purchase order number governing this specific well-vendor engagement. Links to procurement contract management systems.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this well service engagement record was created in the system.

attributes.name: drilling_contractor
attributes.description: Name of the drilling contractor company that provided the rig and drilling crew for this wellbore. Used for contractor performance tracking and Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract management. [Moved from drilling_well: The drilling_contractor attribute in drilling_well is a STRING field containing the contractor company name. This represents ONE specific vendor relationship (the drilling contractor) but should be modeled as a well_service_engagement record with service_type='drilling contractor'. This allows proper referential integrity to the vendor master, tracks contract details, service period, costs, and performance rating. The current STRING field prevents proper vendor analytics and violates normalization principles.]

attributes.name: performance_rating
attributes.description: Post-service performance evaluation of the vendor's service delivery on this well. Used for vendor qualification, future bid evaluations, and continuous improvement. Ratings typically assess HSE performance, quality, schedule adherence, and cost management.

attributes.name: service_end_date
attributes.description: Date when the vendor completed or demobilized from service delivery for this well. For drilling contractors, typically aligns with rig release date. May be null for ongoing services.

attributes.name: service_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the vendor commenced service delivery for this well. For drilling contractors, typically aligns with spud date or rig mobilization. For other services, represents the date service operations began.

attributes.name: service_type
attributes.description: Classification of the service provided by the vendor to the well. Examples include drilling contractor, cementing, completion services, mud services, directional drilling, wireline, coiled tubing, stimulation, workover, and P&A services. A single well typically engages multiple vendors for different service types.

attributes.name: total_service_value_usd
attributes.description: Total cost incurred for this vendor's services on this specific well, expressed in USD. Represents actual costs invoiced and paid, used for well cost accounting and AFE reconciliation.

attributes.name: updated_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this well service engagement record was last modified.

products.name: afe_election
products.description: This association product represents the participation decision and cost allocation between an AFE and a working interest owner. It captures the consent/non-consent election, participating percentage, cost allocation, and billing status for each working interest owner's participation in a specific AFE. Each record links one AFE to one working interest owner with attributes that exist only in the context of this AFE-WI relationship.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas joint venture operations, a single AFE authorizes expenditures that multiple working interest owners must elect to participate in (consent or non-consent), and each working interest owner participates in multiple AFEs over time across different wells and projects. The AFE Election is a recognized operational business process governed by Joint Operating Agreements (JOA) and COPAS standards, where operators must track each WI owner's consent decision, participating percentage, cost allocation, and billing status for every AFE issued.

attributes.name: afe_election_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this AFE election record. Primary key.

attributes.name: drilling_afe_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the AFE for which this election applies

attributes.name: land_working_interest_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the working interest owner making the election

attributes.name: actual_cost_to_date
attributes.description: Cumulative actual costs incurred and allocated to this working interest owner for this AFE as of the current date. Updated as AFE costs are posted.

attributes.name: afe_election_status
attributes.description: Current status of the working interest owner's election decision for this AFE. Tracks whether the owner has consented to participate, elected non-consent, or been forced pooled.

attributes.name: billing_status
attributes.description: Current billing and payment status for this working interest owner's share of AFE costs. Tracks JIB invoice lifecycle.

attributes.name: consent_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the working interest owner consented to participate in this AFE. True = consented (cost-bearing), False = non-consented (may forfeit interest or be penalized per JOA terms).

attributes.name: cost_allocation_amount
attributes.description: The total dollar amount of AFE costs allocated to this working interest owner based on their participating percentage and the AFE approved budget. Used for JIB billing.

attributes.name: election_date
attributes.description: Date on which the working interest owner submitted their consent or non-consent election for this AFE. Used to enforce JOA election deadlines.

attributes.name: election_received_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the operator representative who received and recorded the working interest owner's election.

attributes.name: forced_pooling_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this working interest owner's participation is the result of forced pooling or compulsory integration by regulatory authority rather than voluntary election.

attributes.name: jib_invoice_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the Joint Interest Billing invoice issued to this working interest owner for their share of AFE costs.

attributes.name: non_consent_penalty_rate
attributes.description: Penalty multiplier applied to non-consenting working interest owners per JOA terms (e.g., 300% = 3.0). Non-consenting parties may pay a penalty to regain their interest after payout.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes regarding special conditions, disputes, or clarifications related to this working interest owner's AFE election.

attributes.name: participating_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of AFE costs this working interest owner has elected to bear. May differ from their WI decimal if they elect partial participation or non-consent provisions apply.

attributes.name: payment_due_date
attributes.description: Date by which the working interest owner must pay their allocated share of AFE costs per JOA payment terms.

products.name: program_reservoir_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the capital allocation and drilling plan between a D&C program and a target reservoir. It captures the per-reservoir well count, allocated budget, target reserves, development priority, and drilling sequence within a multi-reservoir drilling campaign. Each record links one dc_program to one reservoir with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific program-reservoir development plan.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas capital planning, D&C programs routinely target multiple reservoirs across a field or basin (e.g., a Permian development program drilling into Wolfcamp A, Wolfcamp B, and Bone Spring reservoirs), and individual reservoirs are developed through multiple drilling campaigns over time (e.g., initial exploration program, appraisal program, full-field development program, infill program). The business actively manages per-reservoir allocations within each program, tracking planned well counts, allocated budgets, target reserves, development priorities, and drilling sequences.

attributes.name: program_reservoir_allocation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this program-reservoir allocation record. Primary key.

attributes.name: dc_program_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Program Reservoir Allocation - Dc Program Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the D&C program under which this reservoir is being developed

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the target reservoir being developed under this program

attributes.name: actual_capex_usd
attributes.description: Actual capital expenditure incurred for drilling and completing wells in this reservoir under this program to date.

attributes.name: actual_well_count_for_reservoir
attributes.description: Actual number of wells drilled into this reservoir under this program to date. Updated as wells are spudded.

attributes.name: allocated_capex_usd
attributes.description: Capital expenditure budget allocated to drilling and completing wells in this reservoir under this program. Subset of the program's total approved CAPEX.

attributes.name: allocation_date
attributes.description: Date when this reservoir was added to the D&C program and budget allocation was made.

attributes.name: allocation_status
attributes.description: Current status of this program-reservoir allocation: planned (pre-AFE), approved (AFE approved), active (drilling underway), complete (all wells drilled), cancelled (allocation removed).

attributes.name: development_priority
attributes.description: Priority ranking for developing this reservoir within the program: high (drill first), medium (drill mid-program), low (drill if budget allows), deferred (postponed to future program).

attributes.name: drilling_sequence
attributes.description: Planned sequence order for drilling wells into this reservoir within the program. Used for rig scheduling and logistics planning.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing rationale for allocation, geological considerations, or operational constraints specific to developing this reservoir under this program.

attributes.name: planned_well_count_for_reservoir
attributes.description: Number of wells planned to be drilled into this specific reservoir under this D&C program. Subset of the program's total planned well count.

attributes.name: target_completion_date
attributes.description: Planned date for completing the last well into this reservoir under this program.

attributes.name: target_eur_mmboe
attributes.description: Target estimated ultimate recovery in million barrels of oil equivalent expected from wells drilled into this reservoir under this program. Used for capital allocation and portfolio optimization.

attributes.name: target_start_date
attributes.description: Planned date for spudding the first well into this reservoir under this program.

products.name: well_unit_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation relationship between a drilling well and a pooling unit in oil and gas operations. It captures the allocation of production, costs, and revenues when a well participates in one or more pooling units, or when a pooling unit contains multiple wells. Each record links one drilling well to one pooling unit with attributes that govern cost-bearing obligations, revenue allocation, and participating acreage specific to that well-unit combination. This is a core operational record required for regulatory compliance, royalty calculation, and joint interest billing.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas operations, a single drilling well can participate in multiple pooling units when it produces from multiple formations or zones that are subject to different unitization agreements (multi-zone completions), and a single pooling unit typically contains multiple wells drilled to develop the pooled acreage. The business actively manages well-unit participation records to track allocation percentages, cost-bearing obligations, revenue distribution methods, and participating acreage for each well-unit combination, which are essential for regulatory compliance, joint interest billing, and royalty calculations.

attributes.name: well_unit_participation_id
attributes.description: Unique system identifier for this well-unit participation record. Primary key.

attributes.name: drilling_well_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Well Unit Participation - Drilling Well Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the drilling well participating in this pooling unit

attributes.name: pooling_unit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Well Unit Participation - Pooling Unit Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the pooling unit in which this well participates

attributes.name: allocation_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of production, costs, or revenues allocated to this well within the pooling unit. Used for proportional allocation calculations in joint interest billing and regulatory reporting. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: cost_bearing_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this well-unit participation bears drilling and completion costs under the unit agreement. Used in joint interest billing calculations. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: System timestamp when this participation record was created.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this well-unit participation relationship became effective, typically aligned with regulatory approval or unit agreement execution. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: formation_allocation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this participation is specific to a particular formation or zone within a multi-zone pooling unit. True for formation-specific allocations in multi-zone completions.

attributes.name: net_revenue_interest_percent
attributes.description: Company's net revenue interest percentage specific to this well-unit participation after royalty and overriding royalty burdens.

attributes.name: participating_area_acres
attributes.description: Acreage attributed to this specific well within the pooling unit for allocation purposes. May differ from gross unit acres when multiple wells participate. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: participation_status
attributes.description: Current status of this well-unit participation relationship. Active participations are used in allocation calculations; suspended or terminated participations are historical.

attributes.name: regulatory_approval_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory order or approval document authorizing this well to participate in the pooling unit, if required by state regulations.

attributes.name: revenue_allocation_method
attributes.description: Method used to allocate production revenues for this well-unit participation. Common methods include surface acreage, subsurface acreage, well count, production-based, or custom formulas defined in the unit agreement. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which this well-unit participation relationship terminated, if applicable. Null for active participations.

attributes.name: updated_date
attributes.description: System timestamp when this participation record was last updated.

attributes.name: working_interest_percent
attributes.description: Company's working interest percentage specific to this well-unit participation, which may differ from the overall unit working interest if participation varies by well.

domains.name: reservoir
domains.description: Serves as the SSOT for subsurface reservoir characterization, simulation models, PVT data, OOIP/OGIP estimates, STOIIP calculations, EUR estimation, material balance data, and recovery factor optimization. Tracks EOR/IOR programs including WAG, SAGD, and CSS schemes. Supports SEC and SPE-PRMS reserves classification (PDP, PUD, PDNP) and production forecast modeling. Integrates with Schlumberger Petrel reservoir simulation.

products.name: reservoir
products.description: Core master entity representing a subsurface reservoir unit — the SSOT for reservoir identity, geometry, fluid type, drive mechanism, and classification. Captures reservoir name, field association, formation, depth range (TVD/MD), areal extent, net pay thickness, porosity, permeability, fluid type (oil/gas/condensate), drive mechanism (solution gas, water drive, gas cap), initial reservoir pressure, temperature, datum depth, API gravity, GOR, WOR, H2S/CO2 content, and PRMS resource classification. Serves as the parent entity for all zone-level, volumetric, simulation, and reserves data in the domain.

products.name: zone
products.description: Defines stratigraphic zones and pay intervals within a reservoir, serving as the SSOT for zone-level characterization. Captures zone name, formation, top and bottom depth (TVD/MD), net pay, gross pay, net-to-gross ratio, porosity type (matrix/fracture/vuggy), permeability range, fluid contact depths (OWC, GOC, GWC), zone status (active/depleted/undeveloped), and lithology description. Supports multi-zone reservoir management and production allocation by zone.

attributes.name: zone_id
attributes.description: Primary key for zone

attributes.description: Reference to the parent reservoir containing this zone. Links zone to its reservoir context for multi-zone reservoir management.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: average_permeability_md
attributes.description: Arithmetic or geometric mean permeability of the net pay interval measured in millidarcies. Critical for flow rate estimation and well spacing decisions.

attributes.name: bottom_depth_md_ft

attributes.name: drive_mechanism

attributes.name: eor_method

attributes.name: gas_water_contact_tvd_ft

attributes.name: initial_reservoir_pressure_psi

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
