attributes.name: top_depth_md_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Top Depth Measured Depth (MD) in Feet
attributes.description: Measured depth along the wellbore to the top of the zone in feet. Relevant for deviated and horizontal wells where MD differs from TVD.
attributes.references: API RP 2A - Recommended Practice for Planning, Designing and Constructing Fixed Offshore Platforms

attributes.name: top_depth_tvd_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Top Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD) in Feet
attributes.description: True vertical depth to the top of the zone measured in feet from a reference datum (typically mean sea level or kelly bushing). Critical for volumetric calculations and STOIIP estimation.
attributes.references: API RP 2A - Recommended Practice for Planning, Designing and Constructing Fixed Offshore Platforms

attributes.name: zone_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code for the zone used in reservoir simulation models and production allocation systems. Unique within the reservoir context.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: zone_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation of the stratigraphic zone or pay interval. Human-readable identifier used in operational communications and reporting.
attributes.references: API RP 40 - Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: zone_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the zone in terms of production activity. Tracks lifecycle state for production optimization and reserves classification.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: zone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the zone based on its hydrocarbon content and production potential. Distinguishes productive pay zones from non-productive intervals.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

products.name: pvt_analysis
products.description: Stores Pressure-Volume-Temperature (PVT) laboratory analysis results for reservoir fluid characterization. Captures sample ID, sample source (DST/wellbore), fluid type, bubble point pressure, dew point pressure, oil formation volume factor (Bo), gas formation volume factor (Bg), solution GOR (Rs), oil viscosity, gas viscosity, oil density, gas gravity, compressibility, Z-factor, shrinkage factor, separator conditions, EOS model parameters, and lab analysis date. Critical input for reservoir simulation and material balance calculations.
products.reference: API RP 44 — Sampling of Petroleum Reservoir Fluids

attributes.name: pvt_analysis_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the PVT analysis record. Primary key for the PVT analysis data product.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - PVT data standards

attributes.name: actual_cost_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.actual_cost. Business justification: PVT laboratory analysis is a direct cost charged to wells/reservoirs. Business process: cost allocation for lab services, AFE tracking, and working interest billing for joint venture operations.

attributes.name: asset_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.facility. Business justification: PVT samples are processed at specific lab facilities; results drive facility design (separator sizing, pipeline specs). Facility design basis, separator optimization, and pipeline flow assurance requi

attributes.name: exploration_well_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.exploration_well. Business justification: PVT samples collected during exploration/appraisal drilling (DST, wireline sampling). Links fluid properties to discovery wells for initial reservoir characterization. Critical for early-stage reserve

attributes.name: hazardous_substance_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.hazardous_substance. Business justification: PVT fluid samples contain hazardous substances (H2S, NORM, aromatic hydrocarbons, mercury) requiring HSE characterization for laboratory handling, transportation (DOT/IATA), disposal, and personnel ex

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the reservoir zone from which the sample was obtained.

attributes.name: sample_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the reservoir fluid sample collected for laboratory analysis. Links to sample collection records.
attributes.references: API RP 44 - Recommended Practice for Sampling Petroleum Reservoir Fluids

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: PVT analysis is procured from qualified laboratories (Core Lab, Weatherford, etc.). Links fluid analysis to vendor qualification, performance tracking, and invoice reconciliation. Removes denormalized

attributes.name: well_asset_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the well from which the reservoir fluid sample was collected.

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: Date when the PVT laboratory analysis was completed.

attributes.name: analysis_status
attributes.description: Current status of the PVT analysis in the data quality and approval workflow. Draft = preliminary results, validated = QC complete, approved = ready for simulation use, superseded = replaced by newer analysis.

attributes.name: bubble_point_pressure
attributes.description: Pressure at which the first gas bubble appears when pressure is reduced on a liquid hydrocarbon system at constant temperature, measured in psia. Critical parameter for oil reservoirs.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments and notes regarding the PVT analysis, including sample quality observations, laboratory procedures, data anomalies, and recommendations for use.

attributes.name: composition_c1
attributes.description: Mole fraction of methane (C1) in the reservoir fluid composition, expressed as a decimal fraction. Part of the compositional analysis used for EOS modeling.

attributes.name: composition_c2_c6
attributes.description: Combined mole fraction of ethane, propane, butanes, pentanes, and hexanes in the reservoir fluid, expressed as a decimal fraction.

attributes.name: composition_c7_plus
attributes.description: Mole fraction of heptane and heavier hydrocarbons in the reservoir fluid, expressed as a decimal fraction. C7+ characterization is critical for black oil and volatile oil systems.

attributes.name: composition_co2
attributes.description: Mole fraction of carbon dioxide in the reservoir fluid, expressed as a decimal fraction. Important for corrosion assessment and EOR design.

attributes.name: composition_h2s
attributes.description: Mole fraction of hydrogen sulfide in the reservoir fluid, expressed as a decimal fraction. Critical for HSE risk assessment and materials selection in sour service.
attributes.references: API RP 44 - Compositional analysis, NACE MR0175 - Sour service standards

attributes.name: composition_n2
attributes.description: Mole fraction of nitrogen in the reservoir fluid, expressed as a decimal fraction. Affects gas heating value and processing requirements.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the PVT analysis record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: dew_point_pressure
attributes.description: Pressure at which the first liquid droplet appears when pressure is reduced on a gas system at constant temperature, measured in psia. Critical parameter for gas condensate reservoirs.

attributes.name: eos_model_type
attributes.description: Type of thermodynamic equation of state model used to match the PVT data for reservoir simulation. Peng-Robinson and Soave-Redlich-Kwong are common cubic EOS models.

attributes.name: eos_parameters
attributes.description: Tuned parameters for the EOS model including binary interaction coefficients, critical properties, and acentric factors. Stored as JSON or delimited string for use in reservoir simulators.

attributes.name: fluid_type
attributes.description: Classification of the reservoir fluid based on phase behavior and composition. Black oil = low shrinkage crude, volatile oil = high shrinkage crude, gas condensate = retrograde condensate, dry gas = lean gas, wet gas = rich gas with NGLs.

attributes.name: gas_compressibility
attributes.description: Change in gas volume per unit change in pressure, measured in reciprocal psi (1/psi). Critical for gas reservoir material balance.

attributes.name: gas_formation_volume_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of gas volume at reservoir conditions to gas volume at standard conditions, measured in reservoir barrels per standard cubic foot (RB/SCF). Bg parameter used in gas material balance.

attributes.name: gas_gravity
attributes.description: Ratio of gas density to air density at standard conditions, dimensionless. Used to characterize gas composition and heating value.

attributes.name: gas_viscosity
attributes.description: Resistance of gas to flow at reservoir conditions, measured in centipoise (cp). Used in gas well deliverability calculations.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the PVT analysis record was last modified in the system.

attributes.name: oil_api_gravity
attributes.description: Measure of how heavy or light crude oil is compared to water, expressed in API degrees. Higher API gravity indicates lighter, more valuable crude oil.

attributes.name: oil_compressibility
attributes.description: Change in oil volume per unit change in pressure, measured in reciprocal psi (1/psi). Used in material balance and pressure transient analysis.

attributes.name: oil_density
attributes.description: Mass per unit volume of oil at reservoir conditions, measured in grams per cubic centimeter (g/cc) or pounds per cubic foot.

attributes.name: oil_formation_volume_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of oil volume at reservoir conditions to oil volume at standard conditions, dimensionless. Bo parameter critical for reserves calculations and material balance.

attributes.name: oil_viscosity
attributes.description: Resistance of oil to flow at reservoir conditions, measured in centipoise (cp). Critical for production forecasting and EOR design.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Assessment of the overall quality and reliability of the PVT analysis based on sample quality, laboratory procedures, and data consistency checks.

attributes.name: reservoir_pressure
attributes.description: Initial reservoir pressure at the sample depth, measured in pounds per square inch absolute (psia).

attributes.name: reservoir_temperature
attributes.description: Temperature of the reservoir at the sample depth, measured in degrees Fahrenheit.

attributes.name: sample_date
attributes.description: Date when the reservoir fluid sample was collected from the well or facility.

attributes.name: sample_source_type
attributes.description: Type of source from which the reservoir fluid sample was collected. DST = Drill Stem Test, wellbore = downhole sampling, separator = surface separator sampling, production_test = production test sampling, recombined = laboratory recombined sample.

attributes.name: separator_pressure
attributes.description: Operating pressure of the production separator used in the PVT analysis, measured in pounds per square inch gauge (psig).

attributes.name: separator_temperature
attributes.description: Operating temperature of the production separator used in the PVT analysis, measured in degrees Fahrenheit.

attributes.name: shrinkage_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of stock tank oil volume to separator oil volume, dimensionless. Accounts for gas liberation and liquid shrinkage from separator to stock tank conditions.

attributes.name: solution_gor
attributes.description: Volume of gas dissolved in oil at reservoir conditions, measured in standard cubic feet per stock tank barrel (SCF/STB). Rs parameter used in material balance calculations.
attributes.references: SPE - Material balance and reservoir simulation standards

attributes.name: stock_tank_pressure
attributes.description: Atmospheric pressure at the stock tank, typically 14.7 psia at standard conditions.

attributes.name: stock_tank_temperature
attributes.description: Temperature at the stock tank, typically 60 degrees Fahrenheit at standard conditions.

attributes.name: z_factor
attributes.description: Gas deviation factor accounting for non-ideal gas behavior at reservoir conditions, dimensionless. Z-factor is critical for gas reserves calculations and material balance.

products.name: volumetric_estimate
products.description: Manages Original Oil In Place (OOIP) and Original Gas In Place (OGIP) volumetric estimates for each reservoir or reservoir zone. Captures estimation method (volumetric/material balance/simulation), gross rock volume (GRV), net rock volume (NRV), net-to-gross ratio, porosity, water saturation, formation volume factor, OOIP low/mid/high (P90/P50/P10), OGIP low/mid/high, STOIIP, estimation date, revision number, and approving geoscientist. Supports SEC and SPE-PRMS reserves disclosure requirements.

attributes.name: volumetric_estimate_id
attributes.description: Primary key for volumetric_estimate

attributes.name: actual_cost_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.actual_cost. Business justification: Volumetric studies are engineering work with associated costs. Business process: cost tracking for reserves evaluation work, AFE variance analysis, and working interest billing.

attributes.name: approving_geoscientist_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Volumetric OOIP estimates are foundation for reserves booking and require licensed geoscientist approval. Links estimate to employee for competency verification (professional geoscientist license), au

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reservoir or reservoir zone for which this volumetric estimate applies.

attributes.name: reservoir_zone_id
attributes.description: FK to reservoir.zone

attributes.name: simulation_model_id
attributes.description: FK to reservoir.simulation_model

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: API gravity of the crude oil in the reservoir, a measure of oil density. Higher API gravity indicates lighter, more valuable crude oil. Typical range is 10 to 50 degrees API.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the volumetric estimate was formally approved by the qualified geoscientist or reserves committee.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of confidence in the volumetric estimate based on data quality, reservoir understanding, and estimation method reliability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this volumetric estimate record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Numerical score (1-10) representing the quality and completeness of input data used for the estimate. Higher scores indicate more reliable data (seismic, well logs, core, production history).

attributes.name: estimate_type
attributes.description: Type of volumetric estimate: OOIP (Original Oil In Place), OGIP (Original Gas In Place), STOIIP (Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place), or GIIP (Gas Initially In Place).

attributes.name: estimation_date
attributes.description: Date when this volumetric estimate was calculated or finalized. Used for tracking estimate vintage and regulatory reporting cutoff dates.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200 - Reserves Disclosure

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Method used to calculate the volumetric estimate. Volumetric uses GRV and petrophysical properties; material balance uses production and pressure data; simulation uses reservoir modeling software.

attributes.name: eur_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) in Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent (MMBOE)
attributes.description: Total volume of hydrocarbons expected to be recovered from the reservoir over its entire productive life, measured in million barrels of oil equivalent. Calculated as OOIP/OGIP multiplied by recovery factor.

attributes.name: formation_volume_factor_gas
attributes.description: Ratio of gas volume at reservoir conditions to gas volume at standard conditions. Used to convert reservoir volumes to standard cubic feet.

attributes.name: formation_volume_factor_oil
attributes.description: Ratio of oil volume at reservoir conditions to oil volume at stock tank conditions. Used to convert reservoir barrels to stock tank barrels. Typically ranges from 1.0 to 2.5.

attributes.name: gas_oil_ratio_scf_bbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas-Oil Ratio (GOR) in Standard Cubic Feet per Barrel (SCF/BBL)
attributes.description: Ratio of gas volume to oil volume produced from the reservoir, measured in standard cubic feet per barrel. Used to characterize reservoir fluid type and drive mechanism.

attributes.name: gross_rock_volume_acre_ft
attributes.description: Total volume of the reservoir rock including both reservoir and non-reservoir rock, measured in acre-feet. Used in volumetric calculations.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this volumetric estimate record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: net_rock_volume_acre_ft
attributes.description: Volume of reservoir rock that contains hydrocarbons, excluding non-reservoir intervals, measured in acre-feet. Calculated as GRV multiplied by net-to-gross ratio.

attributes.name: net_to_gross_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of net reservoir rock to gross rock volume, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. Represents the proportion of the reservoir that is productive.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional comments, assumptions, or qualifications related to this volumetric estimate. May include data limitations, methodology notes, or special considerations.

attributes.name: ogip_high_p10_bcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Gas In Place (OGIP) High Estimate P10 in Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
attributes.description: High estimate (P10 - 10% probability of exceeding) of original gas in place, measured in billion cubic feet. Optimistic estimate for gas reservoirs.

attributes.name: ogip_low_p90_bcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Gas In Place (OGIP) Low Estimate P90 in Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
attributes.description: Low estimate (P90 - 90% probability of exceeding) of original gas in place, measured in billion cubic feet. Conservative estimate for gas reservoirs.

attributes.name: ogip_mid_p50_bcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Gas In Place (OGIP) Mid Estimate P50 in Billion Cubic Feet (BCF)
attributes.description: Best estimate (P50 - 50% probability of exceeding) of original gas in place, measured in billion cubic feet. Most likely estimate for gas reservoirs.

attributes.name: ooip_high_p10_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Oil In Place (OOIP) High Estimate P10 in Million Barrels (MMBBL)
attributes.description: High estimate (P10 - 10% probability of exceeding) of original oil in place, measured in million barrels. Optimistic estimate used for upside scenarios.

attributes.name: ooip_low_p90_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Oil In Place (OOIP) Low Estimate P90 in Million Barrels (MMBBL)
attributes.description: Low estimate (P90 - 90% probability of exceeding) of original oil in place, measured in million barrels. Conservative estimate used for reserves classification.

attributes.name: ooip_mid_p50_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Original Oil In Place (OOIP) Mid Estimate P50 in Million Barrels (MMBBL)
attributes.description: Best estimate (P50 - 50% probability of exceeding) of original oil in place, measured in million barrels. Most likely estimate used for planning.

attributes.name: porosity_fraction
attributes.description: Average porosity of the reservoir rock expressed as a fraction (0 to 1). Represents the pore space available to hold fluids.

attributes.name: recovery_factor_fraction
attributes.description: Estimated fraction of OOIP or OGIP that can be economically recovered, expressed as a decimal (0 to 1). Used to calculate recoverable reserves from in-place volumes.

attributes.name: reserves_category
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS reserves classification category associated with this volumetric estimate: 1P (Proved), 2P (Proved + Probable), 3P (Proved + Probable + Possible), PDP (Proved Developed Producing), PUD (Proved Undeveloped), PDNP (Proved Developed Non-Producing). attributes.name: reservoir_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reservoir Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Average reservoir pressure at the time of the estimate, measured in pounds per square inch. Critical input for material balance calculations and PVT analysis.

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential version number of this estimate. Incremented each time the estimate is revised due to new data, updated models, or methodology changes.

attributes.name: revision_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why this estimate was revised from the previous version (e.g., new well data, updated seismic interpretation, production performance review).

attributes.name: simulation_software
attributes.description: Name and version of the reservoir simulation software used (e.g., Schlumberger Petrel 2023, Eclipse 100, CMG IMEX). Applicable when estimation method is simulation.

attributes.name: stoiip_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place (STOIIP) in Million Barrels (MMBBL)
attributes.description: Volume of oil initially in place at stock tank conditions (surface conditions), measured in million barrels. Calculated by dividing OOIP by formation volume factor.

attributes.name: uncertainty_assessment_method
attributes.description: Method used to quantify uncertainty in the volumetric estimate: Monte Carlo simulation, deterministic sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, or expert judgment.

attributes.name: volumetric_estimate_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the volumetric estimate: draft (under review), approved (finalized), superseded (replaced by newer estimate), archived (historical record).

attributes.name: water_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Average water saturation in the reservoir pore space expressed as a fraction (0 to 1). Hydrocarbon saturation equals 1 minus water saturation.

attributes.description: The business scenario or case name for this forecast (e.g., base case, upside, downside, accelerated development, infill drilling). Used for sensitivity analysis and decision support.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the production forecast: draft (in preparation), under review (pending approval), approved (validated by reservoir engineer), active (currently used for planning), superseded (replaced by newer forecast), or archived (historical record).
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: forecast_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecasting methodology used: deterministic (single outcome), probabilistic (P10/P50/P90 distribution), simulation-based (reservoir simulator output), analogy-based (type curve), or hybrid approach.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: gor_scf_per_bbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas-Oil Ratio (GOR) Standard Cubic Feet (SCF) Per Barrel (BBL)
attributes.description: The Gas-Oil Ratio (GOR) representing the volume of gas produced per barrel of oil, measured in Standard Cubic Feet per Barrel (SCF/BBL). Critical for reservoir characterization, facility design, and production optimization.

attributes.name: initial_production_rate_gas_mcfd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production (IP) Rate Gas Thousand Cubic Feet per Day (MCFD)
attributes.description: The initial gas production rate at the start of the forecast period, measured in Thousand Cubic Feet per Day (MCFD). Used for gas reserves estimation and decline curve modeling.

attributes.name: initial_production_rate_oil_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production (IP) Rate Oil Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: The initial oil production rate at the start of the forecast period, measured in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD). Key parameter for decline curve analysis and EUR estimation.

attributes.name: initial_production_rate_water_bwpd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production Rate Water Barrels of Water Per Day (BWPD)
attributes.description: The initial water production rate at the start of the forecast period, measured in Barrels of Water Per Day (BWPD). Important for Water-Oil Ratio (WOR) tracking and facility design.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this production forecast record was last modified. Tracks changes for version control and audit purposes.

attributes.name: recovery_factor_percent
attributes.description: The percentage of Original Oil in Place (OOIP) or Original Gas in Place (OGIP) that is expected to be recovered over the life of the reservoir. Calculated as EUR divided by OOIP/OGIP. Key indicator of reservoir performance and Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) effectiveness.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: reserves_category
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS and SEC reserves classification: PDP (Proved Developed Producing), PDNP (Proved Developed Non-Producing), PUD (Proved Undeveloped), Probable (2P), or Possible (3P). Critical for SEC reserves disclosure and financial reporting.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System, SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10

attributes.name: simulation_model_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the reservoir simulation model (e.g., Schlumberger Petrel, Eclipse) used to generate this production forecast. Provides traceability to the technical basis for the forecast.

attributes.name: wor_bbl_per_bbl
attributes.description: The Water-Oil Ratio (WOR) representing the volume of water produced per barrel of oil, measured in Barrels per Barrel (BBL/BBL). Important for waterflood monitoring, artificial lift design, and facility capacity planning.

products.name: eor_scheme

Parent entity for all injection events and EOR performance tracking.

attributes.description: Planned daily injection rate in barrels per day (BPD) for water, steam, gas, or chemical injectant as specified in the EOR scheme design.

attributes.description: Internal rate of return for the EOR scheme expressed as a percentage, used for investment decision-making and portfolio optimization.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this EOR scheme record was last updated, reflecting changes to status, performance data, or scheme parameters.

attributes.name: npv_usd
attributes.description: Net present value of the EOR scheme in US dollars, calculated using discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis at the corporate discount rate.

attributes.name: number_of_injection_wells
attributes.description: Total count of active injection wells dedicated to this EOR scheme.

attributes.name: number_of_production_wells
attributes.description: Total count of production wells associated with this EOR scheme that are expected to benefit from the enhanced recovery process.

attributes.name: pattern_type

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: five_spot|seven_spot|nine_spot|line_drive|peripheral|inverted|custom — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: planned_end_date
attributes.description: Forecasted date for completion or termination of the EOR scheme based on reservoir simulation and economic modeling.

attributes.name: reserves_category
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS reserves classification for incremental oil attributed to the EOR scheme: PDP (Proved Developed Producing), PUD (Proved Undeveloped), PDNP (Proved Developed Non-Producing), probable, or possible.

attributes.name: scheme_code
attributes.description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned to the EOR scheme for system identification and cross-referencing with AFE and JIB records.

attributes.name: scheme_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation of the Enhanced Oil Recovery scheme for operational reference and reporting.

attributes.name: scheme_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the EOR scheme: design (planning phase), pilot (small-scale test), active (full-field implementation), suspended (temporarily halted), abandoned (permanently discontinued), or completed (objectives achieved and closed).

attributes.name: sec_reporting_eligible
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the incremental reserves from this EOR scheme are eligible for SEC reserves disclosure under Regulation S-K Item 1200.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when the EOR scheme commenced injection operations or pilot testing.

attributes.name: steam_oil_ratio_sor
attributes.description: Ratio of steam injected (in barrels of cold water equivalent) to oil produced (in barrels) for thermal EOR schemes (SAGD, CSS, steam flood). Key performance indicator for thermal efficiency.

attributes.name: target_incremental_oil_boe
attributes.description: Target incremental oil production in barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) for schemes that also produce associated gas.

attributes.name: target_incremental_oil_mstb
attributes.description: Target incremental oil production in thousands of stock tank barrels (MSTB) expected from the EOR scheme over its lifetime.

attributes.name: target_incremental_recovery_factor
attributes.description: Projected increase in recovery factor (as a decimal fraction) expected from the EOR scheme beyond primary and secondary recovery. Used for EUR estimation and reserves booking.

attributes.name: wag_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of water to gas injection volumes for WAG schemes. Expressed as water volume divided by gas volume. Null for non-WAG schemes.

products.name: injection_event
products.description: Captures individual injection events within EOR/IOR schemes including WAG cycles, steam injection cycles (SAGD/CSS), CO2 injection slugs, and polymer injection batches. Records injection date, injection well, EOR scheme reference, injected fluid type, injected volume (BBL or MCF), injection pressure, injection temperature, injection rate (BOPD/MCFD), cycle number (for cyclic processes), cumulative injection to date, and operational status. Enables EOR performance monitoring and optimization against simulation predictions.
products.reference: SPE EOR Monitoring and Surveillance Standards

attributes.name: cumulative_injection_bbl

attributes.name: cumulative_injection_mcf

attributes.name: cycle_number

attributes.name: cycle_phase
attributes.description: The phase within a cyclic EOR process during which this injection event occurred. Applicable to CSS and other cyclic methods.

attributes.name: data_quality_score
attributes.description: Automated data quality score for this injection event record, ranging from 0 to 100. Based on completeness, accuracy, and consistency checks.

attributes.name: data_source_system

attributes.name: downtime_hours

attributes.name: downtime_reason
attributes.description: Description of the cause of any downtime during the injection event. Supports root cause analysis and continuous improvement.

attributes.name: hse_incident_flag

attributes.name: injected_volume_bbl
attributes.description: Total volume of liquid injected during this event, measured in barrels. Used for water, steam, and liquid chemical injections.

attributes.name: injected_volume_mcf

attributes.description: Total volume of gas injected during this event, measured in thousand cubic feet. Used for CO2, natural gas, and nitrogen injections.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) - Gas measurement standards

attributes.name: injection_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total cost incurred for this injection event, including fluid costs, energy, labor, and equipment. Used for OPEX (Operating Expenditure) tracking and economic analysis.
attributes.references: COPAS (Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies) - Joint interest billing standards

attributes.name: injection_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the injection event occurred. Primary business event timestamp for production reporting and performance tracking.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Production data standards

attributes.name: injection_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total duration of the injection event in hours. Calculated from start and end timestamps or recorded directly from operational systems.

attributes.name: injection_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the injection event concluded. Used to calculate injection duration and operational efficiency.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System - Real-time data historian standards

attributes.name: injection_event_number
attributes.description: Business-assigned unique identifier or tracking number for the injection event, used for operational reporting and cross-system reference.

attributes.name: injection_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Average wellhead injection pressure during the event, measured in pounds per square inch. Critical for reservoir pressure maintenance and fracture risk management.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) - Pressure measurement standards

attributes.name: injection_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the injected fluid. Flags deviations from specification that may impact EOR performance or reservoir integrity.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) - Fluid quality standards

attributes.name: injection_rate_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Rate in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Average injection rate for liquid fluids during this event, expressed in barrels per day. Key operational parameter for EOR optimization.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Production operations standards

attributes.name: injection_rate_mcfd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Rate in Thousand Cubic Feet per Day (MCFD)
attributes.description: Average injection rate for gas fluids during this event, expressed in thousand cubic feet per day. Critical for gas injection EOR schemes.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Production operations standards

attributes.name: injection_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the injection event began. Used for detailed operational analysis and SCADA integration.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI System - Real-time data historian standards

attributes.name: injection_temperature_f
attributes.description: Temperature of the injected fluid at the wellhead, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Particularly important for thermal EOR methods like SAGD and CSS.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) - Temperature measurement standards

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the injection event. Tracks the lifecycle state from planning through completion or termination.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this injection event record was first created in the data system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: record_updated_by
attributes.description: User or system identifier that last modified this injection event record. Supports audit trail and data stewardship accountability.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) - Internal controls and audit trail requirements

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this injection event record was last modified. Audit trail for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, observations, or special conditions related to this injection event. Supports operational knowledge capture.

attributes.name: simulated_injection_volume_bbl
attributes.description: Predicted injection volume from reservoir simulation model (e.g., Schlumberger Petrel). Used for variance analysis between actual and simulated performance.

attributes.name: variance_to_simulation_pct
attributes.description: Percentage variance between actual injection volume and simulated prediction. Key metric for reservoir model calibration and EOR optimization.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir simulation validation standards

products.name: aquifer_model
products.description: Stores aquifer characterization and influx model parameters for water-drive reservoirs. Captures aquifer model type (Schilthuis/van Everdingen-Hurst/Carter-Tracy/Fetkovich), aquifer geometry (radial/linear/bottom), aquifer outer radius, aquifer thickness, aquifer permeability, aquifer porosity, aquifer compressibility, water influx constant (B), aquifer productivity index, cumulative water influx (We), aquifer strength classification (strong/moderate/weak/negligible), calibration date, and model engineer. Feeds material balance and simulation models.
products.reference: van Everdingen-Hurst Aquifer Model; Carter-Tracy Method

attributes.name: aquifer_model_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the aquifer characterization and influx model record. Primary key for the aquifer model entity.

attributes.name: model_engineer_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Aquifer models impact reserves estimates and waterflood design; require qualified reservoir engineer accountability. Links model to engineer for technical peer review, competency verification, and suc

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the parent reservoir that this aquifer model supports. Links aquifer characterization to the reservoir entity.

attributes.name: aquifer_compressibility
attributes.description: Total compressibility of the aquifer system in 1/psi or 1/bar, including rock and water compressibility. Critical parameter for unsteady-state aquifer models.

attributes.name: aquifer_compressibility_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for aquifer compressibility. Typically reciprocal pressure units.

attributes.name: aquifer_encroachment_angle
attributes.description: Angle in degrees representing the fraction of the reservoir perimeter in contact with the aquifer. 360 degrees indicates full radial aquifer, smaller angles indicate partial aquifer contact.

attributes.name: aquifer_geometry
attributes.description: Geometric configuration of the aquifer relative to the reservoir. Radial indicates aquifer surrounds reservoir, linear indicates aquifer extends along one edge, bottom indicates aquifer underlies reservoir, edge/peripheral indicates aquifer contacts reservoir along specific boundaries.

attributes.name: aquifer_initial_pressure
attributes.description: Initial pressure of the aquifer at the aquifer-reservoir contact depth, expressed in psi or bar. Typically equals or slightly exceeds initial reservoir pressure.

attributes.name: aquifer_model_type
attributes.description: Mathematical model type used to characterize aquifer behavior and water influx. Schilthuis for steady-state, van Everdingen-Hurst for unsteady-state radial flow, Carter-Tracy for modified unsteady-state, Fetkovich for pseudo-steady-state, or numerical simulation approaches.

attributes.name: aquifer_name
attributes.description: Business name or designation for the aquifer model, typically referencing the geological formation or field location.

attributes.name: aquifer_outer_radius
attributes.description: Outer boundary radius of the aquifer in feet or meters, representing the extent of the water-bearing formation. Critical parameter for radial aquifer models.

attributes.name: aquifer_permeability
attributes.description: Average horizontal permeability of the aquifer rock in millidarcies (mD). Controls the rate at which water can flow from the aquifer into the reservoir.

attributes.name: aquifer_permeability_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for aquifer permeability. Typically millidarcies (mD) or darcies (D).

attributes.name: aquifer_porosity
attributes.description: Average porosity of the aquifer rock expressed as a fraction (0-1) or percentage. Represents the pore volume available for water storage in the aquifer.

attributes.name: aquifer_pressure_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for aquifer pressure. Typically pounds per square inch (psi), bar, or kilopascals (kPa).

attributes.name: aquifer_productivity_index
attributes.description: Productivity index of the aquifer in barrels per day per psi (bbl/day/psi), representing the rate of water influx per unit pressure differential. Used in Fetkovich aquifer models.

attributes.name: aquifer_radius_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for aquifer radius dimensions. Typically feet (ft) in US operations or meters (m) in international operations.

attributes.name: aquifer_strength_classification
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of aquifer drive strength based on water influx rate relative to reservoir production. Strong aquifers maintain reservoir pressure, weak aquifers provide minimal pressure support.

attributes.name: aquifer_thickness
attributes.description: Average vertical thickness of the aquifer formation in feet or meters. Used to calculate aquifer pore volume and storage capacity.

attributes.name: aquifer_thickness_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for aquifer thickness. Typically feet (ft) in US operations or meters (m) in international operations.

attributes.name: aquifer_water_formation_volume_factor
attributes.description: Formation volume factor for aquifer water (Bw), representing the ratio of water volume at reservoir conditions to volume at standard conditions. Dimensionless or RB/STB.
attributes.references: SPE PVT and Phase Behavior Monograph

attributes.name: aquifer_water_viscosity
attributes.description: Viscosity of aquifer water at reservoir conditions, expressed in centipoise (cP). Used in flow calculations for aquifer influx models.
attributes.references: SPE PVT and Phase Behavior Monograph

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, assumptions, limitations, or special considerations related to the aquifer model.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aquifer model record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: cumulative_water_influx
attributes.description: Total cumulative volume of water that has entered the reservoir from the aquifer since production began, expressed in reservoir barrels (RB) or stock tank barrels (STB). Key parameter for material balance calculations.

attributes.name: cumulative_water_influx_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Water Influx Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for cumulative water influx volume. Reservoir barrels (RB), stock tank barrels (STB), or cubic meters (m3).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this aquifer model record was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: material_balance_integration_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this aquifer model is integrated into the reservoir material balance calculations for reserves estimation and production forecasting.

attributes.name: model_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the aquifer model was formally approved for use in reserves estimation, production forecasting, or development planning. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: model_calibration_date
attributes.description: Date when the aquifer model parameters were last calibrated against historical production and pressure data. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: model_calibration_method
attributes.description: Description of the methodology used to calibrate the aquifer model, such as history matching against pressure decline data, material balance analysis, or numerical simulation.

attributes.name: model_confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of confidence in the aquifer model parameters and predictions based on data quality, calibration fit, and geological understanding.

attributes.name: model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the aquifer model. Active models are used in current forecasts, Under Review models are being updated, Superseded models have been replaced by newer versions, Archived models are retained for historical reference.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for the aquifer model, tracking iterations and updates over time (e.g., v1.0, v2.1).

attributes.name: simulation_software
attributes.description: Name and version of the reservoir simulation or aquifer modeling software used to develop this model (e.g., Schlumberger Petrel, Eclipse, CMG).

attributes.name: water_influx_constant
attributes.description: Aquifer influx constant (B) used in Schilthuis steady-state model, relating cumulative water influx to pressure drop. Expressed in reservoir barrels per psi (RB/psi).

products.name: petrophysical_interp
products.description: Stores petrophysical log interpretation results for wells within a reservoir, providing the subsurface property inputs for volumetric calculations. Captures well identifier, interpreted interval top/bottom depth, gross pay, net pay, net-to-gross ratio, average porosity (total/effective), average water saturation (Sw), average permeability (horizontal/vertical), shale volume (Vsh), hydrocarbon pore volume (HCPV), interpretation method, cutoff criteria applied (porosity/Sw/Vsh cutoffs), software used (Landmark DecisionSpace), and interpretation date.
products.reference: Landmark DecisionSpace Petrophysical Analysis; API RP 40

attributes.name: petrophysical_interp_id
attributes.description: Primary key for petrophysical_interp

attributes.name: exploration_well_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to exploration.exploration_well. Business justification: Petrophysical interpretations from exploration/appraisal well logs quantify reservoir quality and hydrocarbon volumes. Essential for discovery evaluation, reserves booking, and static model population

attributes.name: interpreter_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Petrophysical interpretations feed OOIP calculations and reserves estimates; require certified petrophysicist or geoscientist. Links interpretation to employee for competency verification (petrophysic

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reservoir or formation being interpreted. Links to the reservoir master data.

attributes.name: reservoir_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.zone. Business justification: Petrophysical log interpretations are performed on specific reservoir zones. Currently has reservoir_id but not zone_id. The interpreted_zone field is a STRING - this should be normalized to FK. Petro

attributes.name: well_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the well for which this petrophysical interpretation was performed. Links to the well asset in the asset domain.

attributes.name: average_hydrocarbon_saturation
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average hydrocarbon saturation across the net pay interval, calculated as 1 minus water saturation, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1).

attributes.name: average_permeability_horizontal
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average horizontal (lateral) permeability across the net pay interval in millidarcies (mD), representing the ability of rock to transmit fluids parallel to bedding.
attributes.references: API RP 40 Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: average_permeability_vertical
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average vertical permeability across the net pay interval in millidarcies (mD), representing the ability of rock to transmit fluids perpendicular to bedding.
attributes.references: API RP 40 Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: average_porosity_effective
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average effective porosity across the net pay interval, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1), representing interconnected pore space available for fluid flow.
attributes.references: API RP 40 Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: average_porosity_total
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average total porosity across the net pay interval, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1), representing all pore space including isolated pores.
attributes.references: API RP 40 Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: average_shale_volume
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average shale volume across the interpreted interval, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1), representing the proportion of non-reservoir rock (clay and shale).
attributes.references: Gamma Ray Log Interpretation - API Standard

attributes.name: average_water_saturation
attributes.description: Arithmetic or weighted average water saturation across the net pay interval, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1), representing the fraction of pore space occupied by formation water.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for interpreter notes, assumptions, data quality issues, or special considerations relevant to this petrophysical interpretation.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this petrophysical interpretation record was first created in the system, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.

attributes.name: depth_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for all depth values in this interpretation record (feet or meters).

attributes.name: gross_thickness
attributes.description: Total thickness of the interpreted interval in feet or meters, calculated as bottom depth minus top depth.

attributes.name: hcpv_unit_of_measure
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hydrocarbon Pore Volume (HCPV) Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for hydrocarbon pore volume: acre-feet, cubic meters, or barrels.

attributes.name: hydrocarbon_pore_volume
attributes.description: Total hydrocarbon-filled pore volume for this interpreted interval, calculated as net pay thickness × effective porosity × hydrocarbon saturation × area, typically in acre-feet or cubic meters.

attributes.name: interpretation_date
attributes.description: Date when this petrophysical interpretation was completed and finalized, in yyyy-MM-dd format.

attributes.name: interpretation_method
attributes.description: Petrophysical interpretation method or model used to calculate water saturation and reservoir properties (e.g., Archie, Simandoux, Waxman-Smits for shaly sands).

attributes.name: interpretation_name
attributes.description: Business-friendly name or label for this petrophysical interpretation run, typically including well name, zone, and date for identification purposes.

attributes.name: interpretation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this petrophysical interpretation indicating its approval state and usability for reserves calculations and production forecasting.

attributes.name: interval_bottom_depth_md
attributes.description: Measured depth in feet or meters to the bottom of the interpreted interval along the wellbore trajectory.
attributes.references: API RP 7G Recommended Practice for Drill Stem Design and Operating Limits

attributes.name: interval_bottom_depth_tvd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Interval Bottom Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD)
attributes.description: True vertical depth in feet or meters to the bottom of the interpreted interval, corrected for wellbore deviation.
attributes.references: API RP 7G Recommended Practice for Drill Stem Design and Operating Limits

attributes.name: interval_top_depth_md
attributes.description: Measured depth in feet or meters to the top of the interpreted interval along the wellbore trajectory.
attributes.references: API RP 7G Recommended Practice for Drill Stem Design and Operating Limits

attributes.name: interval_top_depth_tvd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Interval Top Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD)
attributes.description: True vertical depth in feet or meters to the top of the interpreted interval, corrected for wellbore deviation.
attributes.references: API RP 7G Recommended Practice for Drill Stem Design and Operating Limits

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this petrophysical interpretation record was last updated or modified, in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.

attributes.name: net_pay_thickness
attributes.description: Cumulative thickness of reservoir rock within the interval that meets cutoff criteria for porosity, water saturation, and shale volume, representing producible hydrocarbon-bearing rock.

attributes.name: net_to_gross_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of net pay thickness to gross thickness, expressed as a decimal fraction (0 to 1), indicating the proportion of the interval that is productive reservoir rock.

attributes.name: permeability_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for permeability values: millidarcies (mD), darcies (D), or nanodarcies (nD).
attributes.references: API RP 40 Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: porosity_cutoff
attributes.description: Minimum effective porosity threshold applied to define net pay, expressed as a decimal fraction. Rock below this porosity is excluded from net pay calculations.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the interpretation quality based on log quality, data availability, and confidence in the results.

attributes.name: shale_volume_cutoff
attributes.description: Maximum shale volume threshold applied to define net pay, expressed as a decimal fraction. Rock above this shale volume is excluded from net pay calculations.
attributes.references: Gamma Ray Log Interpretation - API Standard

attributes.name: software_used
attributes.description: Name and version of the petrophysical interpretation software application used to perform this analysis (e.g., Landmark DecisionSpace Geosciences, Schlumberger Techlog, Paradigm Geolog).

attributes.name: water_saturation_cutoff
attributes.description: Maximum water saturation threshold applied to define net pay, expressed as a decimal fraction. Rock above this water saturation is excluded from net pay calculations.

products.name: pressure_history
products.description: Time-series record of average reservoir pressure decline over the producing life of a reservoir, aggregated from individual well pressure surveys and simulation history matching. Captures reporting period (monthly/quarterly/annual), average reservoir pressure (psia), datum-corrected pressure, pressure source (measured/simulated/interpolated), cumulative production at reporting date (oil/gas/water in BOE), pressure support mechanism active, depletion rate, and data quality flag. Essential for material balance, reserves revisions, and EOR timing decisions.
products.reference: SPE Reservoir Surveillance and Monitoring Standards

attributes.name: pressure_history_id
attributes.description: Primary key for pressure_history

attributes.name: analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pressure history analysis drives reservoir management decisions and reserves revisions; requires qualified reservoir engineer. Links analysis to employee for approval workflow (approved_by references

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the reservoir for which pressure history is recorded. Links this pressure observation to the specific subsurface reservoir being monitored.

attributes.name: simulation_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.simulation_model. Business justification: Pressure history records reference simulation_model_name as a STRING attribute, but lack the FK relationship. Pressure history is used to validate simulation model history match quality. The model nam

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: The date on which the pressure history analysis was performed or the record was created in the system.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the pressure history record was formally approved for use in reserves estimation and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The current approval workflow status of the pressure history record. Indicates whether the data is in draft, has been submitted for review, approved for use in reserves estimation, or rejected.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the senior reservoir engineer or technical authority who approved this pressure history record for use in reserves reporting and production forecasting.

attributes.name: average_reservoir_pressure_psia
attributes.business_glossary_term: Average Reservoir Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch Absolute - PSIA)
attributes.description: The volumetric average reservoir pressure for the reporting period, measured in pounds per square inch absolute. This is the primary pressure metric used for material balance calculations and reserves estimation.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or explanations regarding the pressure measurement, data quality issues, or special circumstances affecting the pressure history.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: The level of confidence in the accuracy and representativeness of the reported reservoir pressure. Based on measurement quality, number of data points, and consistency with material balance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this pressure history record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: cumulative_gas_production_mcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Gas Production (Thousand Cubic Feet - MCF)
attributes.description: Total cumulative gas production from the reservoir as of the reporting period end date, measured in thousand cubic feet. Essential for gas reservoir material balance and pressure depletion modeling.

attributes.name: cumulative_injection_bbl
attributes.description: Total cumulative volume of fluids injected into the reservoir for pressure maintenance or enhanced oil recovery as of the reporting period end date, measured in barrels.

attributes.name: cumulative_oil_production_bbl
attributes.description: Total cumulative oil production from the reservoir as of the reporting period end date, measured in barrels. Used for material balance calculations and pressure decline analysis.

attributes.name: cumulative_production_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Production (Barrel of Oil Equivalent - BOE)
attributes.description: Total cumulative hydrocarbon production from the reservoir expressed in barrels of oil equivalent, combining oil, gas, and natural gas liquids using standard conversion factors.

attributes.name: cumulative_water_production_bbl
attributes.description: Total cumulative water production from the reservoir as of the reporting period end date, measured in barrels. Important for aquifer influx analysis and pressure support evaluation.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of the quality and validation status of the pressure data. Flags data that has been verified, is suspect due to measurement issues, or is provisional pending further review.

attributes.name: datum_corrected_pressure_psia
attributes.business_glossary_term: Datum Corrected Pressure (Pounds per Square Inch Absolute - PSIA)
attributes.description: Reservoir pressure corrected to a standard datum depth to enable consistent comparison across wells and time periods. Accounts for hydrostatic pressure differences due to elevation.

attributes.name: datum_depth_ft
attributes.description: The reference depth in feet to which reservoir pressure measurements are corrected. Typically set at the top of the reservoir or a mid-point for consistent pressure comparison.

attributes.name: depletion_rate_psi_per_month
attributes.business_glossary_term: Depletion Rate (Pounds per Square Inch per Month - PSI/Month)
attributes.description: The rate of reservoir pressure decline per month during the reporting period. Calculated as the change in average reservoir pressure divided by the time interval. Critical for forecasting and reserves estimation.

attributes.name: eor_program_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether an enhanced oil recovery or improved oil recovery program was active during this reporting period. True if EOR/IOR operations were ongoing.

attributes.name: eor_scheme_type
attributes.description: The specific type of enhanced oil recovery scheme in operation during the reporting period. Includes water alternating gas, steam-assisted gravity drainage, cyclic steam stimulation, polymer flooding, and other tertiary recovery methods. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wag|sagd|css|polymer|surfactant|co2_flood|steam_flood|microbial|not_applicable — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: history_match_quality
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of how well the simulated pressure data matches observed field measurements. Used to evaluate the reliability of simulation-based pressure forecasts.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this pressure history record was most recently updated or modified. Essential for change tracking and audit compliance.

attributes.name: material_balance_error_percent
attributes.description: The percentage error between observed pressure decline and material balance predicted pressure decline. A key quality metric for reservoir characterization and reserves estimation.

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: The specific method or tool used to obtain the pressure measurement. Includes bottom hole pressure gauges, wireline surveys, memory gauges, permanent downhole monitoring systems, or pressure transient tests. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: bottom_hole_gauge|wireline|memory_gauge|permanent_downhole_gauge|buildup_test|falloff_test|material_balance — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: number_of_wells_measured
attributes.description: The count of individual wells from which pressure measurements were obtained and averaged to calculate the reservoir average pressure for this reporting period.

attributes.name: pressure_gradient_psi_per_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pressure Gradient (Pounds per Square Inch per Foot - PSI/FT)
attributes.description: The vertical pressure gradient in the reservoir at the time of measurement, expressed as pressure change per unit depth. Used to correct pressures to datum and assess fluid contacts.

attributes.name: pressure_source_type
attributes.description: Indicates the origin of the pressure data: measured from well surveys, simulated from reservoir model, interpolated between measurements, extrapolated from trends, history matched from simulation, or estimated using material balance.

attributes.name: pressure_support_mechanism
attributes.description: The primary drive mechanism or pressure support system active in the reservoir during this reporting period. Includes natural depletion, aquifer support, gas cap expansion, water injection, gas injection, water alternating gas, steam injection, or chemical enhanced oil recovery. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_depletion|water_drive|gas_cap_drive|solution_gas_drive|water_injection|gas_injection|wag|steam_injection|polymer_flood — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: pressure_uncertainty_psia
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pressure Uncertainty (Pounds per Square Inch Absolute - PSIA)
attributes.description: The estimated uncertainty or error range in the reported average reservoir pressure measurement, expressed in psia. Reflects measurement precision and spatial variability.

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which reservoir pressure is reported for this record. Indicates whether the measurement represents a daily, monthly, quarterly, or annual average.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the reporting period for which this average reservoir pressure measurement applies.

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the reporting period for which this average reservoir pressure measurement applies. Typically monthly, quarterly, or annual intervals.

attributes.name: reserves_category
attributes.description: The SPE-PRMS reserves classification category applicable to the reservoir at the time of this pressure measurement. Includes proved developed producing, proved developed non-producing, proved undeveloped, probable, and possible reserves.

attributes.name: simulation_run_date
attributes.description: The date on which the reservoir simulation was executed to generate or validate this pressure history record. Relevant for simulated or history-matched pressure data.

products.name: decline_curve
products.description: Stores Decline Curve Analysis (DCA) parameters for individual wells and reservoir aggregates used in EUR estimation and production forecasting. Captures well or reservoir identifier, decline type (exponential/hyperbolic/harmonic), initial production rate (IP), initial decline rate (Di), hyperbolic exponent (b-factor), terminal decline rate, EUR oil (MSTB), EUR gas (MMCF), EUR NGL (MSTB), forecast start date, forecast end date, economic limit rate, DCA software used, analyst name, and approval status. Feeds reserves booking and production planning.
products.reference: Arps Decline Curve Analysis; SPE-PRMS EUR Estimation

attributes.name: decline_curve_id
attributes.description: Primary key for decline_curve

attributes.name: actual_cost_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.actual_cost. Business justification: Decline curve analysis is engineering cost for reserves evaluation. Business process: cost allocation for reserves evaluation, AFE tracking, and SEC reserves certification cost tracking.

attributes.name: analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Decline curve analysis is primary method for reserves estimation and SEC reporting; requires certified petroleum engineer. Links DCA to analyst for competency verification (reserves certification), la

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reservoir being analyzed. Links to the reservoir master data for subsurface characterization context.

attributes.name: well_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the well for which this decline curve analysis was performed. Links to the well asset master data.

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: Date on which the decline curve analysis was completed and results were finalized.

attributes.name: analysis_name
attributes.description: Business name or label assigned to this decline curve analysis for identification and reference purposes.

attributes.name: analysis_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the decline curve analysis is for an individual well or an aggregate of multiple wells at reservoir, field, or zone level.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the decline curve analysis was formally approved by the technical authority.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of the decline curve analysis in the technical review and approval workflow. Approved analyses feed reserves booking and production planning.

attributes.name: approver_name
attributes.description: Name of the senior reservoir engineer or technical authority who approved the decline curve analysis for use in reserves booking and forecasting.

attributes.name: b_factor_hyperbolic_exponent
attributes.description: Hyperbolic decline exponent used in Arps hyperbolic decline equation. Value ranges from 0 (exponential) to 1 (harmonic). Typical shale values are 0.5-2.0. Only applicable for hyperbolic and modified hyperbolic decline types.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for analyst comments, assumptions, limitations, and special considerations related to the decline curve analysis.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of confidence in the decline curve forecast based on data quality, production history length, and reservoir understanding.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this decline curve analysis record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: cumulative_production_gas_mmcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Production Gas in Million Cubic Feet (MMCF)
attributes.description: Total gas produced from the well or reservoir aggregate up to the forecast start date, measured in million cubic feet.

attributes.name: cumulative_production_ngl_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Production Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Total natural gas liquids produced from the well or reservoir aggregate up to the forecast start date, measured in thousand stock tank barrels.

attributes.name: cumulative_production_oil_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Production Oil in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Total oil produced from the well or reservoir aggregate up to the forecast start date, measured in thousand stock tank barrels. Used to calculate remaining reserves.

attributes.name: dca_software_name
attributes.description: Name of the software application used to perform the decline curve analysis, such as Schlumberger Petrel, IHS Harmony, or Aries.

attributes.name: dca_software_version
attributes.description: Version number of the software application used for the decline curve analysis, important for audit trail and reproducibility.

attributes.name: decline_type
attributes.description: Mathematical model used for the decline curve analysis. Exponential assumes constant percentage decline, hyperbolic uses variable decline rate with b-factor, harmonic is special case where b=1, and modified hyperbolic transitions from hyperbolic to exponential.

attributes.name: di_initial_decline_rate
attributes.description: Initial decline rate parameter used in Arps decline curve equations, expressed as a decimal fraction per time unit (typically per year). Represents the rate of production decline at the start of the forecast.

attributes.name: economic_limit_rate_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Economic Limit Rate in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Minimum production rate at which the well or reservoir remains economically viable. Production below this rate results in negative cash flow and triggers abandonment consideration.

attributes.name: eur_boe_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) in Thousand Barrels of Oil Equivalent (MBOE)
attributes.description: Total estimated ultimate recovery expressed in thousand barrels of oil equivalent, combining oil, gas (converted at 6:1 ratio), and NGL volumes for unified reporting.

attributes.name: eur_gas_mmcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Gas in Million Cubic Feet (MMCF)
attributes.description: Estimated ultimate recovery of natural gas from the well or reservoir aggregate over its entire economic life, measured in million cubic feet.

attributes.name: eur_ngl_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Estimated ultimate recovery of natural gas liquids from the well or reservoir aggregate over its entire economic life, measured in thousand stock tank barrels.

attributes.name: eur_oil_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) Oil in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Estimated ultimate recovery of oil from the well or reservoir aggregate over its entire economic life, measured in thousand stock tank barrels. Key output of decline curve analysis used for reserves booking.

attributes.name: forecast_end_date
attributes.description: The date at which the decline curve forecast terminates, typically when production reaches the economic limit rate or the well reaches its abandonment date.

attributes.name: forecast_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which the decline curve forecast begins. Typically the first production date or the date of the most recent production data used to calibrate the curve.

attributes.name: ip_gas_mcfd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production (IP) Gas Rate in Thousand Cubic Feet per Day (MCFD)
attributes.description: Initial gas production rate at the start of the decline curve forecast period, measured in thousand cubic feet per day.

attributes.name: ip_ngl_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production (IP) Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) Rate in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Initial natural gas liquids production rate at the start of the decline curve forecast period, measured in barrels per day.

attributes.name: ip_oil_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Initial Production (IP) Oil Rate in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Initial oil production rate at the start of the decline curve forecast period, measured in barrels of oil per day. Critical parameter for EUR estimation.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this decline curve analysis record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: prms_reserves_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Petroleum Resources Management System (PRMS) Reserves Category
attributes.description: SPE-PRMS reserves classification category. 1P represents proved reserves, 2P represents proved plus probable, and 3P represents proved plus probable plus possible reserves.

attributes.name: production_history_months
attributes.description: Number of months of historical production data used to calibrate the decline curve model. Longer history typically improves forecast reliability.

attributes.name: r_squared_fit_quality
attributes.description: Statistical measure of how well the decline curve model fits the historical production data, ranging from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate better fit quality.

attributes.name: remaining_reserves_gas_mmcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Remaining Reserves Gas in Million Cubic Feet (MMCF)
attributes.description: Remaining gas reserves calculated as EUR minus cumulative production, measured in million cubic feet.

attributes.name: remaining_reserves_ngl_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Remaining Reserves Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Remaining natural gas liquids reserves calculated as EUR minus cumulative production, measured in thousand stock tank barrels.

attributes.name: remaining_reserves_oil_mstb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Remaining Reserves Oil in Thousand Stock Tank Barrels (MSTB)
attributes.description: Remaining oil reserves calculated as EUR minus cumulative production, measured in thousand stock tank barrels. Used for SEC and SPE-PRMS reserves classification.

attributes.name: sec_reserves_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Reserves Category
attributes.description: SEC reserves classification. PDP is Proved Developed Producing, PDNP is Proved Developed Non-Producing, and PUD is Proved Undeveloped. Used for financial reporting and disclosure.

attributes.name: terminal_decline_rate
attributes.description: Final decline rate at which the well or reservoir is assumed to decline for the remainder of its economic life. Used in modified hyperbolic models to transition from hyperbolic to exponential decline.

attributes.name: cumulative_injection_volume_mcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Cumulative Injection Volume in Thousand Cubic Feet (MCF)
attributes.description: Total cumulative volume of gas injected since the start of the injection program, measured in thousand cubic feet. Tracks lifetime gas injection for reservoir voidage management.

attributes.name: gas_quality_co2_percent

attributes.name: gross_injection_volume_mcf

attributes.description: Total volume of gas injected during the measurement period, measured in thousand cubic feet. Applies to natural gas, CO2, and other gaseous injectants.

attributes.name: injected_fluid_type
attributes.description: Type of fluid being injected into the reservoir for pressure maintenance or Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR).
