attributes.name: injection_availability_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of time the injection well was available for injection during the measurement period. Calculated as (injection uptime hours / total period hours) * 100. Key performance indicator for injection well reliability.

attributes.name: injection_downtime_hours
attributes.description: Total number of hours the injection well was not injecting during the measurement period due to planned or unplanned downtime. Supports Non-Productive Time (NPT) analysis and operational performance tracking.

attributes.name: injection_efficiency_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of injected fluid that remains in the target reservoir zone versus fluid lost to other zones or formations. Calculated from injection profile logs and tracer studies. High efficiency indicates good conformance; low efficiency signals channeling or thief zones.

attributes.name: injection_period_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the injection performance measurement period. Typically the last day of the reporting month for monthly injection tracking.

attributes.name: injection_period_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the injection performance measurement period. Typically the first day of the reporting month for monthly injection tracking.

attributes.name: injection_pressure_margin_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Pressure Margin in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Difference between formation fracture pressure and current bottomhole injection pressure, measured in pounds per square inch. Positive margin indicates safe injection; negative margin indicates risk of formation fracturing.
attributes.references: API RP 33 - Standard Procedure for Evaluation of Hydraulic Fracturing Fluids

attributes.name: injection_profile_zone_1_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total injection volume entering reservoir zone 1, determined from injection profile logs or flow meters. Supports conformance monitoring and identifies preferential flow paths.
attributes.references: API RP 33 - Standard Procedure for Evaluation of Hydraulic Fracturing Fluids

attributes.name: injection_profile_zone_2_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total injection volume entering reservoir zone 2, determined from injection profile logs or flow meters. Supports conformance monitoring and identifies preferential flow paths.
attributes.references: API RP 33 - Standard Procedure for Evaluation of Hydraulic Fracturing Fluids

attributes.name: injection_profile_zone_3_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of total injection volume entering reservoir zone 3, determined from injection profile logs or flow meters. Supports conformance monitoring and identifies preferential flow paths.
attributes.references: API RP 33 - Standard Procedure for Evaluation of Hydraulic Fracturing Fluids

attributes.name: injection_rate_bpd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Rate in Barrels Per Day (BPD)
attributes.description: Average daily injection rate of liquid during the measurement period, measured in barrels per day. Key metric for monitoring injection well performance and conformance to injection plan.
attributes.references: API RP 11V8 - Recommended Practice for Progressing Cavity Pump (PCP) Installations

attributes.name: injection_rate_mcfd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injection Rate in Thousand Cubic Feet Per Day (MCFD)
attributes.description: Average daily injection rate of gas during the measurement period, measured in thousand cubic feet per day. Monitors gas injection performance for pressure maintenance and EOR schemes.
attributes.references: API RP 14E - Recommended Practice for Design and Installation of Offshore Production Platform Piping Systems

attributes.name: injection_scheme_type
attributes.description: Classification of the injection program type. Includes pressure maintenance, waterflood, gas injection, Water Alternating Gas (WAG), Steam-Assisted Gravity Drainage (SAGD), Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS), polymer flood, surfactant flood, and Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pressure_maintenance|waterflood|gas_injection|wag|sagd|css|polymer_flood|surfactant_flood|ccs — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: injection_temperature_f
attributes.description: Temperature of injected fluid at the wellhead, measured in degrees Fahrenheit. Critical for thermal EOR programs (SAGD, CSS) and monitoring thermal efficiency.

attributes.name: injection_uptime_hours
attributes.description: Total number of hours the injection well was actively injecting during the measurement period. Used to calculate injection availability and operational efficiency.

attributes.name: injectivity_index_bpd_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Injectivity Index in Barrels Per Day per Pounds per Square Inch (BPD/PSI)
attributes.description: Ratio of injection rate to pressure differential (bottomhole injection pressure minus reservoir pressure), measured in barrels per day per psi. Indicates the ease of fluid injection and formation acceptance. Declining injectivity index may signal formation damage, plugging, or conformance issues.

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the injection performance measurement was recorded. Captured from SCADA or PI System historian.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the injection well during the measurement period. Indicates whether the well is actively injecting, shut in for reservoir management, suspended due to mechanical issues, under maintenance, undergoing testing, or offline.
attributes.references: API RP 11V8 - Recommended Practice for Progressing Cavity Pump (PCP) Installations

attributes.name: polymer_concentration_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Polymer Concentration in Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: Concentration of polymer in injected water for polymer flood EOR programs, measured in parts per million. Monitors chemical injection conformance to design specifications.

attributes.name: reservoir_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reservoir Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Current reservoir pressure at the injection zone datum depth, measured in pounds per square inch. Tracks reservoir pressure response to injection for voidage replacement and pressure maintenance effectiveness.

attributes.name: steam_quality_percent
attributes.description: Steam quality (dryness fraction) of injected steam for SAGD or CSS thermal EOR programs, expressed as percentage. 100% indicates dry steam; lower values indicate wet steam with liquid water content.

attributes.name: sweep_efficiency_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of reservoir volume contacted by the injected fluid. Combines areal sweep (horizontal coverage) and vertical sweep (layer coverage). Key metric for waterflood and EOR performance evaluation.

attributes.name: voidage_replacement_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of total injection volume to total production volume on a reservoir-equivalent basis. A VRR of 1.0 indicates perfect voidage replacement; values above 1.0 indicate pressure support exceeding production voidage. Critical metric for reservoir pressure maintenance strategy.

attributes.name: water_quality_suspended_solids_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Water Quality Suspended Solids in Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: Suspended solids concentration in injected water, measured in parts per million. Critical for monitoring filtration effectiveness and preventing formation plugging.
attributes.references: API RP 45 - Recommended Practice for Analysis of Oilfield Waters

attributes.name: water_quality_tds_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Water Quality Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) in Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: Total dissolved solids concentration in injected water, measured in parts per million. Monitors water quality for formation compatibility and scale/plugging risk assessment.
attributes.references: API RP 45 - Recommended Practice for Analysis of Oilfield Waters

attributes.name: wellhead_injection_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Wellhead Injection Pressure in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Injection pressure measured at the wellhead surface, in pounds per square inch. Monitors surface injection pressure for operational control and equipment integrity.
attributes.references: API Spec 6A - Wellhead and Christmas Tree Equipment

products.name: connectivity
products.description: Characterizes the degree of pressure and fluid communication between reservoir zones, fault blocks, and well pairs. Captures connectivity type (pressure/fluid/both), connected reservoir zones or fault blocks, connectivity evidence (pressure equalization/tracer breakthrough/production response), connectivity strength (strong/moderate/weak/none), fault transmissibility multiplier, barrier description, supporting data references, interpretation date, and geoscientist. Critical for development planning, well spacing, and EOR design.

attributes.name: connectivity_id
attributes.description: Primary key for connectivity

attributes.name: connectivity_well_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the source well in a well-pair connectivity analysis. Used when evaluating connectivity between two specific wells.

attributes.name: connectivity_well_pair_target_well_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the target well in a well-pair connectivity analysis. Used when evaluating connectivity between two specific wells.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee or contractor record of the geoscientist who performed the connectivity analysis.

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the field containing the reservoir zones being evaluated for connectivity.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: interference_test_id
attributes.description: Reference to the interference or pulse test record if well testing was used to establish connectivity.

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary reservoir being analyzed for connectivity. Links to the reservoir master data product.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: simulation_model_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reservoir simulation model that incorporates or validates this connectivity interpretation.

attributes.name: source_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the first reservoir zone in the connectivity pair. Represents the zone from which connectivity is being evaluated.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: target_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the second reservoir zone in the connectivity pair. Represents the zone to which connectivity is being evaluated.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: tracer_test_id
attributes.description: Reference to the tracer test record if tracer breakthrough was used as evidence for connectivity.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the connectivity interpretation was formally approved by technical authority or peer review committee.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name of the technical authority or committee that approved the connectivity interpretation for use in development planning and reserves estimation.

attributes.name: barrier_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the geological barrier affecting connectivity, including its nature, extent, and impact on fluid flow.

attributes.name: barrier_type
attributes.description: Type of geological feature acting as a flow barrier between zones. Sealing fault indicates complete fault seal, partial fault indicates leaky fault, shale barrier indicates impermeable shale layer, tight zone indicates low permeability rock, stratigraphic pinchout indicates depositional termination, diagenetic barrier indicates post-depositional cementation or alteration.
attributes.references: SPE Structural and Stratigraphic Geology Standards

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional notes, observations, or context regarding the connectivity interpretation, including uncertainties, alternative interpretations, or recommendations for further investigation.

attributes.name: confidence_level
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of confidence in the connectivity interpretation based on quality and quantity of supporting evidence. High indicates strong multiple lines of evidence, medium indicates reasonable evidence with some uncertainty, low indicates limited or indirect evidence.

attributes.name: connectivity_name
attributes.description: Business name or label assigned to this connectivity analysis for identification and reference purposes.

attributes.name: connectivity_status
attributes.description: Current status of the connectivity interpretation. Confirmed indicates strong evidence, probable indicates likely but not certain, possible indicates weak evidence, uncertain indicates conflicting evidence, disproven indicates evidence of isolation.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS - Petroleum Resources Management System

attributes.name: connectivity_type
attributes.description: Type of connectivity observed between reservoir zones or fault blocks. Pressure connectivity indicates pressure equilibration, fluid connectivity indicates fluid movement, both indicates complete communication, none indicates isolation.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Date when the connectivity record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: evidence_type
attributes.description: Primary type of evidence supporting the connectivity interpretation. Pressure equalization indicates synchronized pressure behavior, tracer breakthrough indicates fluid movement detection, production response indicates rate or pressure response to nearby activity, interference test indicates controlled well testing, seismic attribute indicates geophysical evidence, geological model indicates structural or stratigraphic interpretation.

attributes.name: fault_transmissibility_multiplier
attributes.description: Dimensionless multiplier applied to reservoir simulation grid cells across faults to represent the degree of flow communication. Values range from 0 (complete barrier) to 1 (no barrier). Used in reservoir simulation models to honor observed connectivity behavior.

attributes.name: geoscientist_name
attributes.description: Name of the geoscientist or reservoir engineer responsible for the connectivity interpretation and analysis.

attributes.name: impact_on_development
attributes.description: Description of how this connectivity interpretation impacts field development planning, well spacing decisions, Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) design, or production optimization strategies.

attributes.name: impact_on_eor
attributes.description: Description of how this connectivity interpretation affects Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) or Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) program design, including injection patterns, sweep efficiency, and recovery factor expectations.

attributes.name: interpretation_date
attributes.description: Date when the connectivity interpretation was completed by the geoscientist or reservoir engineer.

attributes.name: interpretation_method
attributes.description: Methodology or technique used to determine connectivity, such as pressure transient analysis, tracer testing, production data analysis, seismic interpretation, or reservoir simulation history matching.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Date when the connectivity record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent technical review or update of the connectivity interpretation based on new data or production performance.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next technical review of the connectivity interpretation to incorporate new surveillance data or production history.

attributes.name: pressure_equalization_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether pressure equalization between zones or fault blocks has been observed through pressure monitoring or well testing.

attributes.name: production_response_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether production rate or pressure changes in one well have been observed in response to activity in another well, suggesting connectivity.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Data quality indicator for the connectivity record. Verified indicates peer-reviewed and approved, unverified indicates preliminary interpretation, under review indicates active quality control, rejected indicates interpretation has been superseded or invalidated.

attributes.name: source_fault_block
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the source fault block being evaluated for connectivity. Fault blocks are reservoir compartments separated by geological faults.

attributes.name: strength
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the degree of communication between connected zones. Strong indicates high transmissibility, moderate indicates partial communication, weak indicates limited communication, none indicates complete isolation.

attributes.name: supporting_data_reference
attributes.description: Reference to supporting data sources used in the connectivity analysis, such as well test reports, tracer study results, pressure survey data, seismic volumes, or simulation model runs. May include document identifiers, file paths, or database references.

attributes.name: target_fault_block
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the target fault block being evaluated for connectivity. Fault blocks are reservoir compartments separated by geological faults.

attributes.name: tracer_breakthrough_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether tracer material injected in one zone or well has been detected in another, confirming fluid connectivity.

attributes.name: well_spacing_recommendation
attributes.description: Recommended well spacing or infill drilling strategy based on the connectivity interpretation. Includes guidance on optimal well placement to maximize reservoir contact while avoiding interference.

products.name: reservoir_sec_reserves_disclosure
products.description: Manages the formal SEC-compliant reserves disclosure records submitted in annual 10-K filings and supplemental oil and gas disclosures. Captures disclosure year, SEC pricing (12-month average first-day-of-month price), proved reserves by category (PDP/PDNP/PUD) and product type (oil/gas/NGL), standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows (SMDFNCF), changes in standardized measure, reserve quantity information table, independent engineer certification reference, filing date, and SEC submission reference. Governed by SEC Rule 4-10(a) and ASC 932.
products.reference: SEC Rule 4-10(a); ASC 932 Extractive Activities — Oil and Gas

attributes.name: reservoir_sec_reserves_disclosure_id

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SEC reserves disclosure record. Primary key for the entity.

attributes.name: asset_facility_id

attributes.name: compliance_regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: SEC reserves disclosures are submitted via regulatory filings (10-K, 20-F, 6-K). Links reservoir-level SEC disclosure data to the formal filing submission for tracking filing status, acknowledgment da

attributes.name: lease_id

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: PSA reserves are disclosed to SEC under specific fiscal terms; cost recovery limits, profit oil entitlements, and contractor shares depend on certified reserves under PSA framework. Required for SEC 1

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reservoir for which reserves are being disclosed.

attributes.name: responsible_engineer_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: SEC reserves disclosure requires named responsible engineer per Regulation S-K Item 1200. Links disclosure to employee for competency verification (qualified reserves evaluator), professional liabilit

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the reserves disclosure was approved by management for inclusion in the SEC filing.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or title of the executive who approved the reserves disclosure for SEC filing.

attributes.name: boe_reserves_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: BOE (Barrel of Oil Equivalent) Reserves MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The total proved reserves expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent, using standard conversion factors for gas and NGL.

attributes.name: certification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the independent engineer certified the reserves estimates.

attributes.name: certification_reference
attributes.description: The reference number or identifier for the independent engineer certification report.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Additional notes, explanations, or qualifications related to the reserves disclosure, including any material assumptions or limitations.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO country code for the country where the reserves are located.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this reserves disclosure record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: disclosure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the SEC reserves disclosure record.

attributes.name: disclosure_year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which the reserves disclosure is being reported, typically aligned with the fiscal year-end for annual 10-K filings.

attributes.name: discount_rate_percent
attributes.description: The annual discount rate applied to future net cash flows to calculate the standardized measure, typically 10% as prescribed by SEC guidelines.

attributes.name: field_code
attributes.description: Reference to the field containing the reservoir for which reserves are disclosed.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date on which the SEC reserves disclosure was officially filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

attributes.name: future_cash_inflows_usd_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Future Cash Inflows USD (United States Dollars) MM (Million)
attributes.description: The undiscounted future gross revenue from proved reserves based on SEC pricing assumptions, expressed in millions of US dollars.

attributes.name: future_development_costs_usd_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Future Development Costs USD (United States Dollars) MM (Million)
attributes.description: The estimated future capital expenditures required to develop proved undeveloped reserves, expressed in millions of US dollars.

attributes.name: future_income_tax_expense_usd_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Future Income Tax Expense USD (United States Dollars) MM (Million)
attributes.description: The estimated future income tax expense associated with the future net cash flows from proved reserves, expressed in millions of US dollars.

attributes.name: future_production_costs_usd_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Future Production Costs USD (United States Dollars) MM (Million)
attributes.description: The estimated future costs to produce the proved reserves, including lease operating expenses and production taxes, expressed in millions of US dollars.

attributes.name: gas_price_usd_per_mcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas Price USD (United States Dollars) per MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet)
attributes.description: The SEC pricing assumption for natural gas used in reserves valuation, expressed in US dollars per thousand cubic feet.

attributes.name: gas_reserves_bcf
attributes.description: The quantity of proved natural gas reserves for this disclosure record, expressed in billion cubic feet.

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: The geographic region or basin where the reserves are located, used for segment reporting in SEC disclosures.

attributes.name: independent_engineer_firm
attributes.description: The name of the independent petroleum engineering firm that certified or audited the reserves estimates for this disclosure.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this reserves disclosure record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: ngl_price_usd_per_bbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: NGL (Natural Gas Liquids) Price USD (United States Dollars) per BBL (Barrel)
attributes.description: The SEC pricing assumption for natural gas liquids used in reserves valuation, expressed in US dollars per barrel.

attributes.name: ngl_reserves_mmbbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: NGL (Natural Gas Liquids) Reserves MMBBL (Million Barrels)
attributes.description: The quantity of proved natural gas liquids reserves for this disclosure record, expressed in million barrels.

attributes.name: oil_price_usd_per_bbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Oil Price USD (United States Dollars) per BBL (Barrel)
attributes.description: The SEC pricing assumption for crude oil used in reserves valuation, expressed in US dollars per barrel.

attributes.name: oil_reserves_mmbbl
attributes.description: The quantity of proved oil reserves for this disclosure record, expressed in million barrels.

attributes.name: prior_year_reserves_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Prior Year Reserves MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The total proved reserves reported in the prior year disclosure, expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent, used for reconciliation purposes.

attributes.name: prms_classification
attributes.description: The SPE-PRMS classification level: 1P (Proved), 2P (Proved plus Probable), or 3P (Proved plus Probable plus Possible). SEC disclosures typically report only 1P (Proved) reserves.

attributes.name: proved_reserves_category
attributes.description: The classification of proved reserves: PDP (Proved Developed Producing), PDNP (Proved Developed Non-Producing), or PUD (Proved Undeveloped).

attributes.name: reporting_entity_name
attributes.description: The legal name of the entity reporting the reserves disclosure, typically the parent company or operating subsidiary.

attributes.name: reserves_additions_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reserves Additions MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The total additions to proved reserves during the disclosure year from extensions, discoveries, improved recovery, and purchases, expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent.

attributes.name: reserves_change_reason
attributes.description: The primary reason for changes in proved reserves from the prior year disclosure, such as revisions of previous estimates, extensions and discoveries, purchases of reserves in place, sales of reserves, or production.

attributes.name: reserves_production_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reserves Production MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The total production from proved reserves during the disclosure year, expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent.

attributes.name: reserves_revisions_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reserves Revisions MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The net revisions to proved reserves during the disclosure year due to changes in technical or economic factors, expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent.

attributes.name: reserves_sales_mmboe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reserves Sales MMBOE (Million Barrels of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: The total proved reserves sold or divested during the disclosure year, expressed in million barrels of oil equivalent.

attributes.name: sec_pricing_method
attributes.business_glossary_term: SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) Pricing Method
attributes.description: The pricing methodology used for reserves valuation, typically the 12-month average first-day-of-month price as required by SEC guidelines.

attributes.name: sec_submission_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) Submission Reference
attributes.description: The official SEC submission identifier or accession number for the 10-K filing containing this reserves disclosure.

attributes.name: smdfncf_usd_mm
attributes.business_glossary_term: SMDFNCF (Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows) USD (United States Dollars) MM (Million)
attributes.description: The standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows from proved reserves, calculated using SEC-prescribed discount rate (10%) and pricing assumptions, expressed in millions of US dollars.

products.name: core_analysis
products.description: Stores laboratory core analysis results from conventional and special core analysis (SCAL) programs. Captures core sample identifier, well identifier, sample depth (MD/TVD), core type (conventional/sidewall/rotary sidewall), analysis type (routine/SCAL), measured porosity, measured permeability (horizontal/vertical), grain density, bulk density, fluid saturations (So/Sw/Sg), capillary pressure data, relative permeability (Kro/Krw/Krg), wettability index, formation resistivity factor, cementation exponent (m), saturation exponent (n), lab name, and analysis date. Calibrates petrophysical log interpretations.
products.reference: API RP 40 — Recommended Practices for Core Analysis

attributes.name: core_analysis_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the core analysis record. Primary key for the core analysis data product.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Data Standards

attributes.name: actual_cost_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.actual_cost. Business justification: Core analysis laboratory work is a direct cost charged to projects. Business process: cost allocation for core programs, AFE tracking, and working interest billing.

attributes.name: asset_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.facility. Business justification: Core analysis is performed at lab facilities; results inform facility design (completion design, artificial lift selection). Lab facility capacity planning and facility design basis require this link.

attributes.name: core_sample_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier assigned to the physical core sample in the laboratory inventory system. Links to sample tracking and chain of custody records.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the reservoir being characterized by this core analysis. Links to reservoir master data for formation, field, and hydrocarbon type.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) PRMS (Petroleum Resources Management System)

attributes.name: reservoir_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.zone. Business justification: Core samples are taken from specific stratigraphic zones within a reservoir. Currently core_analysis has reservoir_id but not zone_id. Zone-level attribution is critical for petrophysical characteriza

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Core analysis is procured from qualified laboratories. Links petrophysical analysis to vendor qualification, API certification tracking, and service quality management. Removes denormalized laboratory

attributes.name: well_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the well from which the core sample was extracted. Links to well master data for location, operator, and drilling history.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) Well Numbering System

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: Date when the laboratory core analysis testing program was completed and results were finalized.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: analysis_status
attributes.description: Current workflow status of the core analysis program. Tracks progression from sample receipt through laboratory testing, quality control review, and final approval.

attributes.name: analysis_type
attributes.description: Classification of the core analysis program. Routine analysis includes basic porosity and permeability; SCAL (Special Core Analysis) includes capillary pressure, relative permeability, and wettability studies.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: bulk_density_g_cm3
attributes.business_glossary_term: Bulk Density in Grams per Cubic Centimeter (g/cm³)
attributes.description: Total density of the rock sample including both matrix and pore space, measured in grams per cubic centimeter. Used to calibrate density logs and calculate porosity.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: capillary_pressure_data_available
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether capillary pressure versus saturation curves were measured as part of SCAL (Special Core Analysis). Capillary pressure data is critical for determining fluid contacts and initial saturation distributions.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: cementation_exponent_m
attributes.description: Archie equation cementation exponent relating formation factor to porosity (F = a / φ^m). Typically ranges from 1.8 to 2.2 for consolidated sandstones. Derived from core resistivity measurements and used for log-derived porosity calculations.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Standards

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-form text field for additional observations, interpretations, or contextual information about the core analysis that does not fit in structured fields. May include geologist notes, laboratory technician observations, or data usage recommendations.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: core_type
attributes.description: Classification of the core sample acquisition method. Conventional cores are full-diameter samples cut during drilling; sidewall cores are smaller plugs extracted from the wellbore wall.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this core analysis record was first created in the data management system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: formation_resistivity_factor
attributes.description: Ratio of brine-saturated rock resistivity to brine resistivity. Used to calibrate Archie equation parameters for resistivity log interpretation. Typically ranges from 1 to 1000 depending on porosity and tortuosity.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Standards

attributes.name: gas_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Fraction of pore space occupied by gas at reservoir conditions, expressed as a decimal (0.0 to 1.0). Important for gas reservoir characterization and gas cap modeling.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: grain_density_g_cm3
attributes.business_glossary_term: Grain Density in Grams per Cubic Centimeter (g/cm³)
attributes.description: Density of the solid rock matrix material, measured in grams per cubic centimeter. Used to calibrate density log interpretations and calculate porosity from bulk density measurements.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: irreducible_water_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Minimum water saturation that cannot be displaced by hydrocarbons, expressed as a decimal fraction. Determined from capillary pressure curves. Defines the maximum hydrocarbon saturation achievable in the reservoir.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Standards

attributes.name: laboratory_location
attributes.description: Geographic location or city where the core analysis laboratory is situated. Important for logistics, sample transport, and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this core analysis record was last updated. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and data synchronization across systems.

attributes.name: lithology_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the rock type, mineralogy, texture, and sedimentary structures observed in the core sample. Includes grain size, sorting, cementation, and visible porosity characteristics.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: measured_permeability_horizontal_md
attributes.description: Laboratory-measured permeability in the horizontal direction (parallel to bedding plane), expressed in millidarcies. Indicates the rock's ability to transmit fluids horizontally. Critical for production rate forecasting and well spacing decisions.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: measured_permeability_vertical_md
attributes.description: Laboratory-measured permeability in the vertical direction (perpendicular to bedding plane), expressed in millidarcies. Typically lower than horizontal permeability due to laminations. Important for vertical sweep efficiency in EOR (Enhanced Oil Recovery) programs.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: measured_porosity_fraction
attributes.description: Laboratory-measured porosity of the core sample expressed as a decimal fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Represents the pore volume as a fraction of total rock volume. Critical for OOIP (Original Oil in Place) and STOIIP (Stock Tank Oil Initially in Place) calculations.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this core analysis record. Used for audit trail and accountability in data governance processes.

attributes.name: oil_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Fraction of pore space occupied by oil at reservoir conditions, expressed as a decimal (0.0 to 1.0). Measured using Dean-Stark extraction or retort analysis. Critical for OOIP (Original Oil in Place) calculations.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: permeability_anisotropy_ratio
attributes.description: Ratio of horizontal to vertical permeability (Kh/Kv). Values greater than 1.0 indicate preferential horizontal flow. Critical for reservoir simulation grid design and EOR (Enhanced Oil Recovery) scheme selection.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir Simulation Standards

attributes.name: porosity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the porosity measurement. Total porosity includes all pore space; effective porosity excludes isolated pores; primary porosity is depositional; secondary porosity is from diagenesis or fracturing.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Standards

attributes.name: primary_lithology
attributes.description: Dominant rock type classification of the core sample. Used for petrophysical model selection and reservoir quality assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sandstone|limestone|dolomite|shale|siltstone|conglomerate|chalk|marl|coal|salt — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Geological Standards

attributes.name: qc_notes
attributes.description: Detailed notes from quality control review documenting any anomalies, measurement uncertainties, sample handling issues, or deviations from standard procedures that may affect data reliability.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality control assessment of the core analysis results. Considers sample preservation, measurement precision, data consistency, and adherence to laboratory protocols. Poor quality data may be excluded from reservoir modeling.

attributes.name: relative_permeability_gas_endpoint
attributes.description: Maximum relative permeability to gas at irreducible water saturation, expressed as a decimal fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Endpoint value from relative permeability curves used in gas reservoir simulation.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir Simulation Standards

attributes.name: relative_permeability_oil_endpoint
attributes.description: Maximum relative permeability to oil at irreducible water saturation, expressed as a decimal fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Endpoint value from relative permeability curves used in reservoir simulation.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir Simulation Standards

attributes.name: relative_permeability_water_endpoint
attributes.description: Maximum relative permeability to water at residual oil saturation, expressed as a decimal fraction (0.0 to 1.0). Endpoint value from relative permeability curves used in waterflood simulation.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir Simulation Standards

attributes.name: residual_oil_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Oil saturation remaining after waterflooding or primary depletion, expressed as a decimal fraction. Represents the target for EOR (Enhanced Oil Recovery) programs such as WAG (Water Alternating Gas) or chemical flooding.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - EOR (Enhanced Oil Recovery) Standards

attributes.name: sample_date
attributes.description: Date when the core sample was physically extracted from the wellbore during drilling or sidewall coring operations.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: sample_depth_md_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Sample Depth Measured Depth (MD) in Feet
attributes.description: Measured depth along the wellbore trajectory where the core sample was extracted, measured in feet from the surface reference point.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: sample_depth_tvd_ft
attributes.business_glossary_term: Sample Depth True Vertical Depth (TVD) in Feet
attributes.description: True vertical depth of the core sample measured perpendicular to the surface, in feet. Used for pressure gradient calculations and reservoir modeling.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Reservoir Engineering Standards

attributes.name: saturation_exponent_n
attributes.description: Archie equation saturation exponent relating resistivity index to water saturation (Sw^-n). Typically close to 2.0 for water-wet rocks. Derived from core resistivity measurements at varying saturations and used for log-derived water saturation calculations.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - Petrophysical Standards

attributes.name: water_saturation_fraction
attributes.description: Fraction of pore space occupied by water at reservoir conditions, expressed as a decimal (0.0 to 1.0). Used to calibrate resistivity log interpretations and validate Archie equation parameters.
attributes.references: API (American Petroleum Institute) RP 40 - Core Analysis Procedures

attributes.name: wettability_index
attributes.description: Quantitative measure of rock wettability ranging from -1.0 (strongly oil-wet) to +1.0 (strongly water-wet). Measured using Amott-Harvey or USBM methods. Critical for selecting appropriate relative permeability curves and EOR (Enhanced Oil Recovery) methods.
attributes.references: SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) - SCAL (Special Core Analysis) Standards

products.name: equity_participation
products.description: This association product represents the equity participation contract between a reservoir and a customer counterparty (equity partner). It captures the working interest, net revenue interest, and profit-sharing arrangements specific to each partner-reservoir combination in Production Sharing Contracts (PSC) and Joint Operating Agreements (JOA). Each record links one reservoir to one equity partner with entitlement terms, cost recovery status, and profit distribution percentages that exist only in the context of this specific partnership arrangement.. Existence Justification: In upstream oil and gas operations, Production Sharing Contracts (PSC) and Joint Operating Agreements (JOA) create genuine many-to-many equity participation arrangements. A single reservoir commonly has multiple equity partners (IOCs, NOCs, independents) each holding different working interest percentages, and each partner typically holds interests across multiple reservoirs within a field or across multiple fields. The business actively manages these participation arrangements as distinct contractual entities with specific entitlement terms, cost recovery tracking, and profit distribution calculations that vary by partner-reservoir combination.

products.name: scheme_well_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the operational assignment of injection wells to Enhanced Oil Recovery schemes. It captures the specific role each injection well plays within an EOR scheme's injection pattern (five-spot, seven-spot, line drive), the well's position in the pattern, injection targets, and performance tracking. Each record links one EOR scheme to one injection well with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas EOR operations, injection wells are strategically assigned to EOR schemes in specific geometric patterns (five-spot, seven-spot, line drive) where each well plays a defined role (peripheral injector, central injector, pattern edge). A single EOR scheme requires multiple injection wells working in coordinated patterns, and injection wells can participate in multiple EOR schemes simultaneously when targeting different reservoir zones or sequentially over time as schemes evolve. The business actively manages these assignments with scheme-specific injection targets, pattern roles, and performance tracking.

attributes.name: eor_scheme_id

products.name: eor_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation agreement between an Enhanced Oil Recovery scheme and a joint venture partner. It captures scheme-specific working interests, cost sharing arrangements, carried interest provisions, non-consent elections, and incremental reserves entitlements that differ from base reservoir development agreements. Each record links one EOR scheme to one partner with participation terms that exist only in the context of this specific EOR project.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas joint ventures, EOR schemes frequently have different partner participation than base reservoir development. Partners can elect to participate or go non-consent on individual EOR projects based on technical risk, capital availability, and strategic priorities. Each EOR scheme-partner combination requires tracking of scheme-specific working interests, cost sharing obligations, carried interest provisions, non-consent elections, back-in rights, and incremental reserves entitlements that differ from the base JOA.

products.name: eor_vendor_supply_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual supply relationship between an Enhanced Oil Recovery scheme and its vendors. It captures procurement agreements for EOR-specific materials and services including chemical suppliers, steam generators, CO2 suppliers, and specialized equipment vendors. Each record links one EOR scheme to one vendor with contract terms, pricing, volumes, and performance guarantees that exist only in the context of this specific scheme-vendor relationship.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas EOR operations, a single Enhanced Oil Recovery scheme requires multiple vendors simultaneously (chemical supplier for polymers, CO2 supplier for gas injection, equipment vendor for pumps, service contractor for steam generation). Conversely, specialized EOR vendors supply multiple schemes across different fields and operators. The business actively manages these supply relationships as procurement contracts with scheme-specific pricing, volumes, delivery terms, and performance guarantees.

products.name: reservoir_working_interest
products.description: This association product represents the ownership and economic participation of venture partners in specific reservoirs. It captures the legal and financial relationship between partners and reservoirs, including working interest percentages, net revenue interest, reserves entitlement, and cost allocation. Each record links one partner to one reservoir with attributes that define the partner's economic stake and obligations in that specific reservoir. This is the SSOT for partner-reservoir participation tracking, AFE cost allocation, and reserves booking by partner.. Existence Justification: In oil and gas joint ventures, multiple partners hold economic interests in multiple reservoirs simultaneously. Each partner-reservoir combination has distinct working interest percentages, net revenue interest, reserves entitlement, and cost allocation that are legally defined in JOAs, PSAs, or assignment agreements. The business actively manages these working interests through AFE approvals, revenue distribution, reserves booking, and partner billing—this is a core operational relationship, not an analytical correlation.

attributes.name: cost_allocation_percentage

attributes.name: interest_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the working interest. Active = partner is currently bearing costs and receiving revenue. Pending = interest assigned but not yet effective. Relinquished = partner has surrendered interest. Farmed_Out = partner has assigned interest to another party. Suspended = interest temporarily inactive due to force majeure or regulatory action.

attributes.name: last_modified_date

attributes.name: net_revenue_interest_percentage

attributes.name: percentage

attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-X Rule 4-10, SPE PRMS

domains.name: production
domains.description: Manages real-time and historical production data including daily production allocation, well test analysis, BOPD/MCFD/MMCFD reporting, GOR/WOR tracking, artificial lift optimization, decline curve analysis, and facility performance. Serves as the SSOT for production volumes and field performance via OSIsoft PI System, Avocet Production Operations, and SCADA/DCS integration. Supports SEC reserves reporting and regulatory production filings to BSEE and state agencies.

products.name: production_well
products.description: Master record for every well in the production domain, including producing, injection, observation, and disposal wells. Captures well identity, API number, wellbore type (oil producer, gas producer, water injector, gas injector, disposal, observation), current status (producing, shut-in, temporarily abandoned, P&A, PDNP), spud date, completion date, artificial lift type, field/reservoir assignment, surface and bottom-hole coordinates, measured depth (MD), true vertical depth (TVD), injection parameters (injection type, UIC permit number, permitted rate) where applicable, and regulatory identifiers for BSEE and state agency filings. Serves as the SSOT for well identity within the production domain and is the primary anchor entity for all production volumes, injection volumes, and well performance data.
