attributes.description: Date when this lifecycle status ended and transitioned to a new status. Null for the current active status record. Used for historical status tracking and audit trail.

attributes.name: financial_impact_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated financial impact of the lifecycle status change in USD, including revenue loss from discontinued sales, inventory write-down costs, contract penalties, and transition costs. Used for EBITDA forecasting and management reporting. Negative values indicate costs or losses.
attributes.references: IFRS/GAAP Accounting Standards, Internal Financial Planning Framework

attributes.name: hse_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Impact Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifecycle status change has health, safety, or environmental implications requiring HSE review and mitigation planning. True for regulatory-withdrawn status or when discontinuation involves hazardous material handling.
attributes.references: OSHA Standards, EPA Environmental Compliance, Internal HSE Management System

attributes.name: hse_review_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Review Reference
attributes.description: Reference number for the HSE impact assessment or Management of Change (MOC) review conducted for this lifecycle status change. Links to HSE management system records for audit and compliance verification.
attributes.references: Internal HSE Management System, MOC Process Standard

attributes.name: inventory_disposition_plan
attributes.description: Description of the strategy for managing existing inventory when product status transitions to phase-out or discontinued. May include sell-through timelines, blending into other products, disposal methods, or transfer to other markets. Critical for OPEX planning and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: Supply Chain Management Standard, Environmental Disposal Regulations

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that last updated this lifecycle status record. Supports change tracking and accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard, SOX Compliance Controls

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this lifecycle status record. Used for data freshness monitoring and audit trail completeness.
attributes.references: ISO 8601 Timestamp Standard, SOX Audit Requirements

attributes.name: lifecycle_status_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle stage of the petroleum product. Development indicates product formulation and testing phase; pilot indicates limited market trial; active indicates full commercial availability; phase-out indicates planned discontinuation with existing commitments honored; discontinued indicates no longer available for new orders; regulatory-withdrawn indicates removal from market due to regulatory action or compliance failure.

attributes.name: market_applicability
attributes.description: Geographic markets or jurisdictions where this lifecycle status applies. May be global or restricted to specific regions due to regulatory differences, supply chain constraints, or strategic market positioning. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or regional identifiers.

attributes.name: notification_lead_time_days
attributes.description: Number of days advance notice required before the status effective date per contractual terms or regulatory requirements. Typically 30-180 days for phase-out or discontinuation to allow customer planning and inventory management.
attributes.references: Contract Terms Standard, FERC Tariff Requirements

attributes.name: notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when downstream system notifications were successfully transmitted. Used for audit trail and to verify compliance with notification lead time requirements.

attributes.name: production_cutoff_date
attributes.description: Date when refining or manufacturing operations will cease production of this petroleum product. Applies to phase-out and discontinued statuses. Used for refinery scheduling, feedstock planning, and capacity reallocation decisions.
attributes.references: Refinery Operations Standard, Production Planning Framework

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory body or government agency that governs this product lifecycle status change. Examples include EPA for environmental compliance, FERC for natural gas products, BSEE for offshore production, or state-level environmental agencies.
attributes.references: EPA Authority Framework, FERC Jurisdiction, BSEE Regulatory Scope

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or docket identifier for the regulatory filing associated with this status change. Links to EPA submissions, FERC tariff amendments, or state agency notifications for compliance tracking.
attributes.references: EPA Submission Standards, FERC Docket System

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifecycle status change requires formal filing or notification to regulatory authorities such as EPA, FERC, BSEE, or state environmental agencies. True for regulatory-withdrawn status and for discontinuation of products with environmental permits.
attributes.references: EPA Reporting Requirements, FERC Filing Standards, BSEE Compliance Framework

attributes.name: sales_cutoff_date
attributes.description: Date after which no new sales orders or term contracts will be accepted for this petroleum product. Typically follows production cutoff date to allow sell-through of remaining inventory. Critical for sales force guidance and customer relationship management.
attributes.references: Sales Operations Standard, Contract Management Framework

attributes.name: status_change_notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes and context about the lifecycle status change, including stakeholder communications, lessons learned, or special handling instructions. Supports knowledge management and future decision-making.

attributes.name: transition_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the primary business reason for the lifecycle status change. Market demand indicates customer or market-driven changes; regulatory compliance indicates changes due to environmental or safety regulations; technical obsolescence indicates superseded by newer formulations; strategic portfolio indicates corporate strategy alignment; cost optimization indicates economic viability decisions; safety concern indicates HSE-driven withdrawal.

attributes.name: transition_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative explanation of the business rationale and circumstances that led to the lifecycle status change. Provides context for audit, compliance, and business intelligence purposes.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or system identifier of the person or automated process that created this lifecycle status record. Used for audit trail and data governance.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Standard, SOX Compliance Controls

products.name: uom_conversion
products.description: Enterprise reference table for unit-of-measure conversion factors critical to petroleum volume and energy accounting. Covers barrels-to-metric-tons (product-specific, using API gravity or density), MCF-to-BOE, MMBtu-to-tonnes (LNG), gallons-to-barrels (NGL), and temperature/pressure correction factors (ASTM D1250 / API MPMS Ch. 11). Each conversion record specifies from-unit, to-unit, product type or API gravity range, conversion factor, effective date, and governing standard. Used enterprise-wide by production accounting, revenue, logistics, and finance for consistent volumetric and energy reporting.

attributes.name: uom_conversion_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the unit of measure conversion record. Primary key for the conversion table.

attributes.name: inverse_conversion_id
attributes.description: Reference to the inverse conversion record (to-unit back to from-unit). Null if no explicit inverse record exists or if bidirectional_flag is True.

attributes.name: superseded_by_conversion_uom_conversion_id
attributes.description: Reference to the conversion record that replaces this one when status is 'superseded'. Maintains audit trail of conversion factor changes.

attributes.name: api_gravity_max
attributes.description: Maximum API gravity value for which this conversion factor is valid. Used for density-dependent barrel-to-mass conversions. Null if conversion is not API-gravity-dependent.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

attributes.name: api_gravity_min
attributes.description: Minimum API gravity value for which this conversion factor is valid. Used for density-dependent barrel-to-mass conversions. Null if conversion is not API-gravity-dependent.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

attributes.name: applicable_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or jurisdiction where this conversion is applicable (e.g., 'USA', 'EUR', 'GBR', 'GLOBAL'). Some conversions vary by regional standards.

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: Role or individual who approved this conversion factor for use (e.g., 'Chief Petroleum Engineer', 'VP Production Accounting', 'Regulatory Compliance Manager').

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this conversion factor was formally approved for use in production systems.

attributes.name: audit_trail_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting the rationale for conversion factor changes, approvals, or special handling instructions. Critical for SOX compliance and audit support.

attributes.name: bidirectional_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the conversion can be applied in both directions (from-to and to-from) using the reciprocal factor. True if bidirectional, False if unidirectional.

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Business unit or division that uses this conversion (e.g., 'Upstream', 'Downstream', 'Midstream', 'Refining', 'Marketing'). Null if enterprise-wide.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Method used to perform the conversion: direct multiplication by factor, table lookup, formula-based calculation, or correction for temperature/pressure/density.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: conversion_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the conversion rule, used for external reference and system integration.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: conversion_factor
attributes.description: Numeric multiplier used to convert from the source unit to the target unit. Precision to 8 decimal places to support accurate petroleum volume and energy calculations.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: conversion_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name describing the conversion (e.g., 'Barrels to Metric Tons - WTI Crude', 'MCF to BOE - Natural Gas').

attributes.name: conversion_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the conversion record. Active conversions are used in production calculations; superseded conversions are retained for historical audit.

attributes.name: conversion_type
attributes.description: Category of physical measurement being converted (volume, mass, energy, temperature, pressure, density).
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this conversion record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this conversion factor becomes valid and should be used in calculations. Critical for historical accuracy in production accounting and revenue reporting.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this conversion factor is no longer valid. Null if the conversion remains active indefinitely.

attributes.name: from_unit
attributes.description: Source unit of measure being converted from (e.g., BBL, MCF, MT, GAL, MMCF, MMBTU, TONNES).
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: governing_standard
attributes.description: Industry standard or specification that defines this conversion methodology (e.g., 'API MPMS Ch. 11.1', 'ASTM D1250', 'ISO 91-1', 'GPA 2145').
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the individual who last modified this conversion record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this conversion record was last updated.

attributes.name: precision_decimal_places
attributes.description: Number of decimal places to which converted values should be rounded for reporting and financial calculations.

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Petroleum product type or grade this conversion applies to (e.g., 'WTI Crude', 'Brent Crude', 'Natural Gas', 'LNG', 'Diesel', 'Gasoline'). Product-specific conversions account for density and API gravity variations.

attributes.name: reference_pressure_kpa
attributes.description: Standard reference pressure in kilopascals at which the conversion factor is defined. Critical for gas volume conversions (e.g., standard cubic feet to actual cubic feet).
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: reference_temperature_c
attributes.description: Standard reference temperature in Celsius at which the conversion factor is defined (typically 15°C or 60°F equivalent). Used for temperature-corrected volume conversions per ASTM D1250.

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Regulatory body or authority that mandates this conversion (e.g., 'SEC', 'BSEE', 'EPA', 'FERC'). Null if not regulatory-driven.

attributes.name: regulatory_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this conversion is mandated by regulatory or compliance requirements (e.g., SEC reserves reporting, BSEE production reporting). True if regulatory-mandated.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200, BSEE Production Reporting

attributes.name: rounding_method
attributes.description: Rounding methodology to apply when converting values (e.g., round half up, round down, truncate). Critical for consistent financial and volumetric reporting.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Operational system or reference source from which this conversion was derived (e.g., 'SAP MM', 'Avocet Production', 'API MPMS Tables', 'Manual Entry').

attributes.name: standard_version
attributes.description: Version or edition of the governing standard (e.g., '2004 Edition', 'Rev 2', 'Amendment 1').
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: to_unit
attributes.description: Target unit of measure being converted to (e.g., MT, BOE, BBL, MMBTU, TONNES, MCF).
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: usage_context
attributes.description: Business process or system context where this conversion is applied (e.g., 'Production Accounting', 'Revenue Distribution', 'Logistics Planning', 'Financial Reporting', 'Regulatory Filing').

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User ID or name of the individual who created this conversion record.

products.name: substitution
products.description: Defines approved product substitution relationships — identifying which products can substitute for another in specific use cases (e.g., Jet A-1 substituting for Jet A in certain markets, VLSFO substituting for HSFO post-IMO 2020, or equivalent NGL fractions). Captures primary product, substitute product, substitution conditions, approval authority, quality adjustment required, and effective date range. Used by supply chain and commercial teams during supply disruptions.
products.reference: API / IATA Fuel Quality Requirements / IMO MARPOL

attributes.name: substitution_id
attributes.description: Primary key for substitution

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Product substitutions require technical and commercial approval for quality equivalence, pricing adjustment, and customer acceptance. Essential for supply disruption response, contract flexibility, an

attributes.name: substitution_petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary petroleum product that may be substituted. Links to the petroleum_product master data.

attributes.name: substitution_substitute_product_petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substitute petroleum product that can replace the primary product. Links to the petroleum_product master data.

attributes.name: applicable_market
attributes.description: Geographic markets, regions, or jurisdictions where this substitution is permitted, using three-letter ISO country codes or regional identifiers (e.g., USA, EUR, MEA, APAC).

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: Name or role of the business authority, technical committee, or regulatory body that approved this substitution relationship (e.g., Chief Commercial Officer, Product Quality Committee, Regional Supply Chain Director).

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the substitution relationship was formally approved by the designated authority.

attributes.name: approval_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number or document identifier for the formal approval decision, linking to authorization for expenditure (AFE), management of change (MOC), or technical review documentation.

attributes.name: conditions
attributes.description: Specific technical, operational, or regulatory conditions that must be met for the substitution to be valid, including quality adjustments, blending requirements, or customer approval prerequisites.
attributes.references: API Standards, Internal Product Substitution Standard

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: Reference to specific contracts, term agreements, or production sharing agreements (PSA) that govern or permit this substitution relationship.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this substitution relationship record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: customer_approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether explicit customer or counterparty approval is required before executing this substitution in a commercial transaction or delivery.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the substitution relationship becomes valid and can be used in supply chain planning, commercial operations, and customer fulfillment.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the substitution relationship expires or is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended substitution relationship.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: Permitted frequency or pattern for using this substitution (unrestricted use, occasional use, emergency situations only, one-time authorization, or seasonal availability).

attributes.name: hse_impact_assessment
attributes.business_glossary_term: Health Safety and Environment (HSE) Impact Assessment
attributes.description: Summary of health, safety, and environmental considerations or impact assessment results for this substitution, including any changes to hazard classification, handling requirements, or emissions profiles.
attributes.references: OSHA, EPA, API RP 75, Internal HSE Standard

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who last modified this substitution relationship record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this substitution relationship record was last modified in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes, operational guidance, or special instructions related to this substitution relationship for use by supply chain planners and commercial teams.

attributes.name: price_adjustment_method
attributes.description: Method used to calculate pricing adjustments when the substitute product is used instead of the primary product (no adjustment, fixed differential, percentage adjustment, market index-based, or case-by-case negotiation).

attributes.name: price_differential_amount
attributes.description: Fixed price differential amount applied when the substitute product is used, expressed in the pricing currency. Positive values indicate premium, negative values indicate discount.

attributes.name: price_differential_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage-based price adjustment applied when the substitute product is used. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0250 for 2.5% premium or -0.0150 for 1.5% discount).

attributes.name: pricing_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the price differential amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: quality_adjustment_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the quality adjustments, blending ratios, additives, or treatment processes required to make the substitute product meet the specifications of the primary product.
attributes.references: API Standards, Internal Product Substitution Standard

attributes.name: quality_adjustment_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether quality adjustments, blending, or treatment are required when substituting the primary product with the substitute product.
attributes.references: API Standards, Internal Product Substitution Standard

attributes.name: regulatory_compliance_notes
attributes.description: Documentation of regulatory considerations, compliance requirements, or restrictions that apply to this substitution (e.g., IMO 2020 sulfur limits, EPA fuel category restrictions, FERC tariff provisions).

attributes.name: substitution_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the substitution relationship, used in supply chain and commercial systems for quick reference.

attributes.name: substitution_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the substitution relationship indicating whether it is currently approved and available for use.

attributes.name: substitution_type
attributes.description: Classification of the substitution relationship indicating the nature and scope of substitutability (full replacement, partial replacement, conditional use, emergency only, or planned transition).

attributes.name: supply_disruption_priority
attributes.description: Priority ranking for this substitution option during supply disruptions or shortages. Lower numbers indicate higher priority (1 = first choice, 2 = second choice, etc.).

attributes.name: technical_review_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a technical review or engineering assessment is required each time this substitution is executed, typically for complex or high-risk substitutions.

attributes.name: use_case_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific business scenarios, market conditions, or operational contexts in which this substitution is permitted (e.g., Jet A-1 substituting for Jet A in European markets, VLSFO substituting for HSFO post-IMO 2020 compliance).

attributes.name: volume_limit_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Volume Limit Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Maximum volume of the substitute product that can be used in place of the primary product, expressed in barrels of oil equivalent (BOE). Null indicates no volume restriction.
attributes.references: SPE PRMS, Internal Product Substitution Standard

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the person who created this substitution relationship record in the system.

products.name: handling_requirement
products.description: Captures special handling, storage, and transportation requirements for petroleum products — including temperature maintenance (heated crude, LNG cryogenic), pressure requirements (LPG pressurized), inert gas blanketing, segregation requirements (avgas from MOGAS), NORM handling protocols, H2S safety requirements, and compatibility restrictions. Links to petroleum_product and is used by logistics, terminal operations, and HSE for safe product handling.
products.reference: IMDG Code / ADR / API RP 2003 / OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 PSM

attributes.name: handling_requirement_id
attributes.description: Primary key for handling_requirement

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the petroleum product for which these handling requirements apply. Links to the petroleum_product master data.

attributes.name: requirement_author_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Handling requirements require HSE technical author for temperature control, vapor recovery, H2S protocols, and NORM handling procedures. Critical for operational safety, regulatory compliance, and eme

attributes.name: coating_lining_requirement
attributes.description: Description of internal coating or lining requirements for tanks, vessels, and pipelines to prevent corrosion, contamination, or product degradation. Includes epoxy coatings, phenolic linings, or specialized polymer systems.
attributes.references: API RP 652 - Lining of Aboveground Petroleum Storage Tank Bottoms

attributes.name: container_material_specification
attributes.description: Specification of acceptable container and piping materials for storage and transportation, such as carbon steel, stainless steel, or specialized alloys. Critical for preventing corrosion and material compatibility issues with sour crude, high-TAN crudes, and corrosive petrochemicals.
attributes.references: API RP 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this handling requirement record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this handling requirement becomes effective and must be implemented in operations. Used for managing regulatory changes and operational transitions.

attributes.name: emergency_response_procedure
attributes.description: Summary of emergency response procedures required for spills, leaks, fires, or exposure incidents involving this product. References detailed emergency response plans and material safety data sheets.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 112 - Oil Pollution Prevention

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this handling requirement expires or is superseded by updated requirements. Null for requirements with indefinite validity.

attributes.name: fire_protection_requirement
attributes.description: Description of fire protection systems and equipment required for storage and handling areas, including foam systems, water deluge, dry chemical systems, and fire detection equipment.
attributes.references: API RP 2001 - Fire Protection in Refineries

attributes.name: h2s_content_threshold_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Content Threshold (Parts Per Million)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable concentration of hydrogen sulfide in parts per million. Products exceeding this threshold require special Health Safety and Environment (HSE) handling protocols including gas detection, respiratory protection, and emergency response procedures.

attributes.name: h2s_safety_protocol
attributes.description: Detailed description of safety protocols required when handling products with hydrogen sulfide content, including personal protective equipment (PPE), gas monitoring, confined space entry procedures, and emergency response measures.
attributes.references: API RP 55 - Conducting Oil and Gas Producing and Gas Processing Plant Operations Involving Hydrogen Sulfide

attributes.name: incompatible_products
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of petroleum products that are chemically incompatible and must never be mixed or stored in adjacent tanks. Used to prevent hazardous reactions, product degradation, or specification violations.

attributes.name: inert_gas_blanketing_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether inert gas blanketing (typically nitrogen) is required to prevent oxidation, contamination, or explosive atmosphere formation in storage tanks and vessels.

attributes.name: inert_gas_type
attributes.description: Type of inert gas required for blanketing operations. Nitrogen is most common, but carbon dioxide or argon may be specified for certain petrochemical applications.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this handling requirement record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date when this handling requirement was last reviewed and validated by subject matter experts or regulatory compliance personnel.

attributes.name: loading_rate_max_m3_per_hour
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Loading Rate (Cubic Meters Per Hour)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable loading or transfer rate in cubic meters per hour to prevent static electricity buildup, pressure surges, or product degradation during transfer operations.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next mandatory review of this handling requirement to ensure continued compliance and operational accuracy.

attributes.name: norm_handling_protocol
attributes.business_glossary_term: Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM) Handling Protocol
attributes.description: Detailed description of NORM handling protocols including radiation monitoring, worker exposure limits, personal protective equipment, waste disposal procedures, and regulatory reporting requirements.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 61 - National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants

attributes.name: norm_handling_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM) Handling Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether special Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM) handling protocols are required. Certain crude oils and produced water contain elevated levels of radioactive isotopes requiring specialized handling, disposal, and worker protection measures.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 61 - National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants

attributes.name: personal_protective_equipment
attributes.description: Detailed description of personal protective equipment required for personnel handling this product, including respiratory protection, chemical-resistant gloves, face shields, flame-resistant clothing, and safety footwear.

attributes.name: pressure_control_method
attributes.description: Description of the method or equipment required to maintain pressure within specified range, such as pressure relief valves, vapor recovery systems, or refrigeration.
attributes.references: API RP 520 - Sizing, Selection, and Installation of Pressure-Relieving Devices

attributes.name: pressure_max_kpa
attributes.description: Maximum allowable pressure in kilopascals for safe containment. Exceeding this pressure may compromise vessel integrity and create safety hazards.

attributes.name: pressure_min_kpa
attributes.description: Minimum pressure in kilopascals required for safe storage and transportation. Critical for pressurized products like Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) and Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG).

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Name of the primary regulatory authority or governing body that mandates or oversees this handling requirement, such as Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), or Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE).

attributes.name: regulatory_citation
attributes.description: Specific regulatory citation, code section, or standard reference that mandates this handling requirement, enabling traceability to legal and regulatory obligations.

attributes.name: requirement_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the handling requirement type to enable filtering and grouping of similar requirements across the product portfolio. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: temperature_control|pressure_control|inert_gas_blanketing|segregation|hse_safety|compatibility|norm_handling|vapor_control — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: API RP 2003 - Protection Against Ignitions Arising Out of Static, Lightning, and Stray Currents

attributes.name: requirement_code
attributes.description: Unique business code identifying this specific handling requirement within the product catalog. Used for operational reference and system integration.
attributes.references: API RP 500 - Recommended Practice for Classification of Locations

attributes.name: requirement_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the handling requirement for business user identification and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: requirement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the handling requirement indicating whether it is currently in force, has been superseded by newer requirements, or is under regulatory review.

attributes.name: requirement_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the handling requirement is mandatory for regulatory compliance, recommended as best practice, conditional based on circumstances, or prohibited.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106 - Flammable and Combustible Liquids

attributes.name: review_frequency_days
attributes.description: Number of days between mandatory reviews of this handling requirement to ensure continued accuracy, regulatory compliance, and operational relevance.

attributes.name: segregation_requirement
attributes.description: Detailed description of segregation requirements specifying which products or product families must be kept separate during storage, transportation, and handling to prevent cross-contamination or hazardous reactions. Examples include aviation gasoline (AVGAS) from motor gasoline (MOGAS), or sour crude from sweet crude.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 18.2 - Custody Transfer of Crude Oil from Lease Tanks

attributes.name: spill_containment_requirement
attributes.description: Description of spill containment and secondary containment requirements for storage and handling areas, including berm capacity, drainage systems, and spill response equipment specifications.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 112 - Oil Pollution Prevention

attributes.name: static_electricity_precautions
attributes.description: Description of static electricity control measures required during product transfer and handling operations, including bonding and grounding requirements, flow rate limitations, and equipment specifications to prevent ignition hazards.
attributes.references: API RP 2003 - Protection Against Ignitions Arising Out of Static, Lightning, and Stray Currents

attributes.name: temperature_control_method
attributes.description: Description of the method or equipment required to maintain temperature within specified range, such as steam coils, heat tracing, insulation, or refrigeration systems.
attributes.references: API RP 2001 - Fire Protection in Refineries

attributes.name: temperature_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum temperature in degrees Celsius allowed for safe storage and handling. Exceeding this temperature may cause product degradation, vapor pressure issues, or safety hazards.

attributes.name: temperature_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum temperature in degrees Celsius required for safe storage and handling of the petroleum product. Critical for products like heated crude oil and high pour-point fuels.

attributes.name: transportation_mode_restriction
attributes.description: Description of restrictions or requirements for transportation modes (pipeline, tanker truck, rail car, marine vessel, barge) based on product characteristics, regulatory requirements, or safety considerations.
attributes.references: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 195 - Transportation of Hazardous Liquids by Pipeline

attributes.name: unloading_rate_max_m3_per_hour
attributes.business_glossary_term: Maximum Unloading Rate (Cubic Meters Per Hour)
attributes.description: Maximum allowable unloading or discharge rate in cubic meters per hour to ensure safe product transfer and prevent equipment damage or safety hazards.

attributes.name: vapor_control_method
attributes.description: Description of vapor control or recovery method required, such as vapor recovery units, thermal oxidizers, flares, or closed-loop systems to manage volatile organic compound emissions.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 60 Subpart XX - Standards of Performance for Bulk Gasoline Terminals

attributes.name: vapor_recovery_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether vapor recovery systems are required during loading, unloading, and storage operations to capture volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and prevent atmospheric emissions. Mandatory for many refined products under EPA regulations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 60 Subpart XX - Standards of Performance for Bulk Gasoline Terminals

products.name: emission_factor
products.description: Reference data for greenhouse gas (GHG) and criteria pollutant emission factors associated with petroleum products — including CO2 emission factors (kg CO2/GJ or kg CO2/bbl), methane emission factors, NOx/SOx factors for combustion, lifecycle carbon intensity (gCO2e/MJ) for fuel regulatory compliance (EU ETS, California LCFS, UK ETS). Captures product type, emission category, factor value, unit, applicable regulation, and data source (EPA AP-42, IPCC, GREET model).
products.reference: EPA AP-42 / IPCC Guidelines / EU ETS / California LCFS / GREET Model

attributes.name: emission_factor_id
attributes.description: Primary key for emission_factor

attributes.name: data_steward_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Emission factors require environmental data steward for GHG reporting, carbon intensity calculation, and regulatory citation maintenance. Essential for EPA/BSEE reporting, carbon tax compliance, and s

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the petroleum product for which this emission factor applies. Links to the petroleum product master catalog.

attributes.name: applicable_regulation
attributes.description: Regulatory framework or program for which this emission factor is applicable. Examples: EPA GHG Reporting Rule (40 CFR Part 98), EU ETS, California LCFS, UK ETS, IPCC National Inventory Guidelines, SEC Climate Disclosure.
attributes.references: EPA, EU ETS, California LCFS, UK ETS, SEC

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: Regulatory body, standards organization, or internal authority that approved or published this emission factor. Examples: EPA, IPCC, EU Commission, California Air Resources Board (CARB), internal HSE department.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the emission factor was officially approved or published by the approval authority.

attributes.name: control_efficiency_percent
attributes.description: Percentage reduction in emissions achieved by the control technology. Used to calculate net emissions after control. Example: 90% control efficiency means 90% of pollutant is removed.

attributes.name: control_technology
attributes.description: Emission control or abatement technology assumed in the emission factor. Examples: none, selective catalytic reduction (SCR), flue gas desulfurization (FGD), electrostatic precipitator (ESP), carbon capture and storage (CCS), vapor recovery unit (VRU).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this emission factor record was first created in the data system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Authoritative source or publication from which the emission factor was obtained. Examples: EPA AP-42, IPCC 2006 Guidelines, GREET Model 2023, API Compendium, DEFRA Conversion Factors, EIA.
attributes.references: EPA AP-42, IPCC, GREET, API, DEFRA, EIA

attributes.name: data_source_version
attributes.description: Version or publication year of the data source. Ensures traceability and allows for updates when new emission factor datasets are released.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this emission factor becomes valid and applicable for emissions calculations and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: emission_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the emission type: greenhouse gas (GHG), criteria pollutant (NOx, SOx), volatile organic compound (VOC), particulate matter, hazardous air pollutant (HAP), or lifecycle assessment.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act, IPCC Guidelines

attributes.name: emission_source_type
attributes.description: Type of emission source activity: combustion, flaring, venting, fugitive emissions, process emissions, transportation, storage, or full lifecycle assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: combustion|flaring|venting|fugitive|process|transportation|storage|lifecycle — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA GHG Reporting Rule, API Compendium

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which this emission factor is no longer valid. Null if the factor remains valid indefinitely or until superseded.

attributes.name: factor_code
attributes.description: Unique business code identifying the emission factor. Used for external reference and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: factor_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name of the emission factor, including pollutant type and product context.

attributes.name: factor_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the emission factor. Active factors are approved for use in regulatory reporting. Superseded factors have been replaced by newer versions. Deprecated factors are no longer valid.

attributes.name: factor_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the emission factor value. Common units include kg CO2/bbl, kg CO2/GJ, g CO2e/MJ, kg NOx/tonne, lb SO2/MMBtu.

attributes.name: factor_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the emission factor. Represents the quantity of pollutant emitted per unit of product activity (e.g., kg CO2 per barrel, g NOx per GJ).
attributes.references: EPA AP-42, IPCC Guidelines, GREET Model

attributes.name: fuel_quality_adjustment
attributes.description: Fuel quality characteristic that may affect the emission factor. Examples: low sulfur, ultra-low sulfur, high sulfur, sour crude, sweet crude, heavy crude, light crude. Used to differentiate emission factors based on product specifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: none|low_sulfur|ultra_low_sulfur|high_sulfur|sour|sweet|heavy|light — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic region or country for which this emission factor is applicable. Use ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g., USA, GBR, CAN) or regional codes (e.g., EUR for Europe-wide factors).

attributes.name: gwp_version
attributes.description: IPCC Assessment Report version used for GWP calculation when converting non-CO2 greenhouse gases to CO2 equivalents. AR4 (Fourth Assessment Report), AR5 (Fifth Assessment Report), AR6 (Sixth Assessment Report).

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this emission factor record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this emission factor record was last modified in the data system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: last_review_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent internal review or validation of this emission factor. Used to ensure factors remain current and accurate.

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.description: Stage in the product lifecycle for which this emission factor applies. Used for lifecycle carbon intensity calculations. Includes extraction, production, processing, refining, transportation, distribution, combustion, end-use, well-to-tank (WTT), tank-to-wheel (TTW), or well-to-wheel (WTW). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: extraction|production|processing|refining|transportation|distribution|combustion|end_use|well_to_tank|tank_to_wheel|well_to_wheel — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GREET Model, California LCFS, EU RED II

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: Method used to derive the emission factor: default (from published source), measured (direct stack testing or monitoring), modeled (simulation), calculated (mass balance), or engineering estimate.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this emission factor. Ensures factors are updated as new scientific data or regulatory requirements emerge.

attributes.name: oxidation_factor
attributes.description: Fraction of carbon in the fuel that is oxidized during combustion. Typically ranges from 0.95 to 1.00. Used to adjust theoretical CO2 emissions based on incomplete combustion.

attributes.name: pollutant_type
attributes.description: Specific pollutant or greenhouse gas species: carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulfur oxides (SOx), carbon monoxide (CO), particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), volatile organic compounds (VOC), benzene, hydrogen sulfide (H2S). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: co2|ch4|n2o|co2e|nox|sox|co|pm10|pm2_5|voc|benzene|h2s — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA AP-42, IPCC Guidelines, GHG Protocol

attributes.name: regulatory_citation
attributes.description: Specific regulatory citation or section reference where this emission factor is defined or required. Example: 40 CFR 98 Subpart C Table C-1.

attributes.name: technology_type
attributes.description: Specific technology or process configuration to which this emission factor applies. Examples: conventional combustion, fluidized bed combustion, gas turbine, reciprocating engine, flare (enclosed/elevated), carbon capture and storage (CCS).

attributes.name: tier_level
attributes.description: IPCC tier level indicating the methodological complexity and data quality of the emission factor. Tier 1 uses default factors, Tier 2 uses country-specific factors, Tier 3 uses facility-specific measurements and models.

attributes.name: time_horizon_years
attributes.description: Time horizon in years over which the GWP is calculated. Typically 20, 100, or 500 years. Most regulatory frameworks use 100-year GWP.

attributes.name: uncertainty_percentage
attributes.description: Estimated uncertainty or confidence interval of the emission factor value, expressed as a percentage. Used for quality assurance and sensitivity analysis in emissions inventories.
attributes.references: IPCC Good Practice Guidance, EPA QA/QC

attributes.name: usage_notes
attributes.description: Additional guidance, limitations, or context for applying this emission factor. May include applicability conditions, calculation examples, or references to related factors.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that created this emission factor record in the data system.

products.name: tariff_code
products.description: Maps petroleum products to applicable tariff and duty codes for international trade — including HS (Harmonized System) 6-digit codes, country-specific import/export tariff schedules, excise duty categories, VAT classifications, and free trade agreement (FTA) preferential rates. Captures product, country/jurisdiction, tariff code, duty rate, effective date, and applicable trade agreement. Used by supply chain, customs, and finance for trade compliance and cost calculation.
products.reference: WCO Harmonized System / WTO Tariff Schedules / CBP HTSUS

attributes.name: tariff_code_id
attributes.description: Primary key for tariff_code

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the petroleum product being classified for tariff purposes.

attributes.name: superseded_by_tariff_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the newer product_tariff_code record that replaces this classification. Only populated when tariff_status is superseded.

attributes.name: anti_dumping_duty_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether anti-dumping duties are currently in effect for this product from specific origin countries. True if anti-dumping measures apply; false otherwise.
attributes.references: WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement; Country-Specific Trade Remedy Measures

attributes.name: classification_ruling_number
attributes.description: Official customs ruling or binding tariff information (BTI) reference number issued by the customs authority confirming the tariff classification for this product.

attributes.name: countervailing_duty_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether countervailing duties (to offset foreign subsidies) are currently in effect for this product. True if countervailing measures apply; false otherwise.
attributes.references: WTO Subsidies and Countervailing Measures Agreement

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code identifying the jurisdiction where this tariff classification applies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this tariff code mapping record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: customs_valuation_method
attributes.description: Method used to determine the customs value for duty calculation purposes, as defined by WTO Valuation Agreement (e.g., transaction value, computed value).
attributes.references: WTO Agreement on Customs Valuation (Article VII GATT)

attributes.name: duty_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the duty rate (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Applicable for specific duty rates or when duty is expressed in a specific currency.

attributes.name: duty_rate_percent
attributes.description: Ad valorem duty rate expressed as a percentage of the customs value (CIF or FOB basis). Null if duty is specific (per-unit) rather than ad valorem.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this tariff classification and associated duty rates become effective for customs purposes.

attributes.name: excise_duty_rate_percent
attributes.description: Excise tax rate applied to petroleum products as a percentage of value or per unit. Common for refined fuels such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel.

attributes.name: excise_duty_specific_rate
attributes.description: Specific excise duty rate per unit of measure (e.g., USD per gallon, EUR per liter). Used for volume-based excise taxation of petroleum products.

attributes.name: excise_duty_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the excise duty specific rate. Only applicable when excise_duty_specific_rate is populated.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this tariff classification and associated duty rates cease to be valid. Null for open-ended classifications.

attributes.name: hs_code
attributes.description: Six-digit or extended Harmonized System tariff classification code for international trade. The first six digits are standardized globally; additional digits may be country-specific extensions.

attributes.name: import_export_classification
attributes.description: Indicates whether this tariff code mapping applies to import transactions, export transactions, or both.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that last modified this tariff code mapping record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this tariff code mapping record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: license_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether an import or export license is required for this product in the specified jurisdiction. True if licensing is mandatory; false otherwise.

attributes.name: license_type
attributes.description: Type or category of import/export license required (e.g., automatic license, non-automatic license, strategic goods license). Only applicable when license_requirement_flag is true.

attributes.name: national_tariff_code
attributes.description: Country-specific tariff schedule code that extends or replaces the HS code for domestic customs purposes. May include additional digits beyond the HS 6-digit base.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, clarifications, or special instructions related to the tariff classification, duty calculation, or compliance requirements for this product-country combination.

attributes.name: origin_requirement
attributes.description: Rules of origin criteria that must be satisfied to qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the applicable trade agreement (e.g., minimum local content percentage, substantial transformation).
attributes.references: Free Trade Agreement (FTA) Rules of Origin

attributes.name: preferential_duty_rate_percent
attributes.description: Reduced duty rate available under a free trade agreement or preferential trade program. Lower than the standard MFN rate when trade agreement conditions are met.

attributes.name: quota_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this product is subject to a tariff rate quota (TRQ) in the specified jurisdiction. True if quota limits apply; false otherwise.

attributes.name: quota_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the quota volume (e.g., barrels, metric tons). Only applicable when quota_applicable_flag is true.

attributes.name: quota_volume
attributes.description: Maximum volume or quantity allowed under the tariff rate quota before higher out-of-quota duty rates apply. Only applicable when quota_applicable_flag is true.

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: Name of the government agency or customs authority responsible for administering this tariff classification (e.g., U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HM Revenue & Customs).

attributes.name: ruling_date
attributes.description: Date on which the customs classification ruling was issued by the regulatory authority.

attributes.name: sanctioned_country_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether trade of this product with the specified country is subject to economic sanctions or embargoes. True if sanctions apply; false otherwise.
attributes.references: OFAC Sanctions Programs; UN Security Council Sanctions; EU Sanctions

attributes.name: specific_duty_rate
attributes.description: Specific duty rate applied per unit of measure (e.g., USD per barrel, EUR per metric ton). Used when duty is calculated on quantity rather than value.

attributes.name: specific_duty_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the specific duty rate (e.g., barrel, metric ton, liter). Only applicable when specific_duty_rate is populated.

attributes.name: strategic_goods_classification
attributes.description: Export control classification for strategic or dual-use petroleum products (e.g., certain petrochemicals). References export control lists such as the Commerce Control List (CCL) or EU Dual-Use Regulation.
attributes.references: U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR); EU Dual-Use Regulation

attributes.name: tariff_description
attributes.description: Official description of the tariff classification as published in the customs tariff schedule, providing detailed product categorization.

attributes.name: tariff_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the tariff code mapping. Active indicates the classification is currently in force; superseded indicates it has been replaced by a newer classification.

attributes.name: trade_agreement_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the applicable free trade agreement (FTA) or preferential trade arrangement (e.g., USMCA, EU-FTA, ASEAN). Null if most-favored-nation (MFN) rates apply.
attributes.references: World Trade Organization (WTO) Trade Agreements; Regional FTA Documentation

attributes.name: vat_rate_percent
attributes.description: Value Added Tax or Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate applicable to the petroleum product in the specified jurisdiction, expressed as a percentage.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: User identifier or system account that created this tariff code mapping record.

products.name: safety_data_sheet
products.description: Manages Safety Data Sheets (SDS/MSDS) for petroleum products and chemicals — covering GHS hazard classification, physical/chemical properties, first aid measures, fire-fighting measures, accidental release measures, handling and storage, exposure controls/PPE, transport information (UN number, packing group), and regulatory information. Captures SDS version, effective date, issuing authority, and language. Required for HSE compliance and REACH/OSHA HazCom.
products.reference: GHS Rev 9 / OSHA HazCom 29 CFR 1910.1200 / REACH Article 31

attributes.name: safety_data_sheet_id
attributes.description: Primary key for safety_data_sheet

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the petroleum product or chemical for which this safety data sheet is issued. Links to the product master catalog.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: SDS documents are often provided by product vendors/suppliers. Tracking vendor enables regulatory compliance, SDS update management, and supplier accountability for hazard communication in procurement

attributes.name: accidental_release_containment_methods
attributes.business_glossary_term: Accidental Release - Containment and Cleanup Methods
attributes.description: Recommended methods and materials for containing and cleaning up spills or releases, including absorbent materials, recovery procedures, and disposal considerations.

attributes.name: appearance
attributes.description: Visual description of the products appearance including color, clarity, and physical form (e.g., clear amber liquid, white crystalline powder).

attributes.name: autoignition_temperature_c
attributes.description: Minimum temperature at which the product will spontaneously ignite without an external ignition source, measured in degrees Celsius.
attributes.references: ASTM E659 Standard Test Method for Autoignition Temperature

attributes.name: conditions_to_avoid
attributes.description: Environmental conditions that may cause hazardous reactions or decomposition, such as heat, sparks, static electricity, shock, or incompatible materials.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this safety data sheet record was first created in the data management system.

attributes.name: disposal_considerations
attributes.description: Recommended disposal methods and regulatory requirements for the product and contaminated containers, including waste treatment options and applicable waste codes.

attributes.name: document_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the safety data sheet document indicating whether it is in draft, active use, superseded by a newer version, archived, or withdrawn.

attributes.name: ecological_information
attributes.description: Environmental impact data including aquatic toxicity, persistence and degradability, bioaccumulative potential, mobility in soil, and effects on wildlife.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this safety data sheet becomes the official document for the product, replacing any prior versions.

attributes.name: emergency_phone_number
attributes.description: 24-hour emergency contact telephone number for incidents involving the product, typically a poison control center or manufacturer emergency line.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this safety data sheet expires and must be reviewed or replaced, typically required every 3-5 years depending on jurisdiction.

attributes.name: exposure_limits
attributes.description: Workplace air concentration exposure limits including OSHA Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL) and ACGIH Threshold Limit Value (TLV), expressed as time-weighted average (TWA), short-term exposure limit (STEL), or ceiling limit.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000 Table Z-1; ACGIH TLVs and BEIs

attributes.name: firefighting_extinguishing_media
attributes.description: Appropriate fire extinguishing agents for fires involving the product (e.g., foam, CO2, dry chemical, water spray). Critical for emergency response planning.

attributes.name: firefighting_special_hazards
attributes.description: Special fire and explosion hazards associated with the product, including toxic combustion products, explosive vapor formation, and reactivity with water.

attributes.name: first_aid_eye_contact
attributes.description: Recommended first aid procedures for eye contact with the product, including flushing duration, removal of contact lenses, and when to seek medical attention.

attributes.name: first_aid_ingestion
attributes.description: Recommended first aid procedures if the product is swallowed, including whether to induce vomiting, aspiration hazards, and medical treatment guidance.

attributes.name: first_aid_inhalation
attributes.description: Recommended first aid procedures if the product is inhaled, including moving to fresh air, oxygen administration, and when to seek medical attention.

attributes.name: first_aid_skin_contact
attributes.description: Recommended first aid procedures for skin contact with the product, including washing procedures, removal of contaminated clothing, and medical treatment guidance.

attributes.name: flammability_limits_lower_pct
attributes.description: Lower explosive limit (LEL) or lower flammability limit, expressed as volume percent in air, below which the vapor-air mixture is too lean to ignite.
attributes.references: ASTM E681 Standard Test Method for Concentration Limits of Flammability

attributes.name: flammability_limits_upper_pct
attributes.description: Upper explosive limit (UEL) or upper flammability limit, expressed as volume percent in air, above which the vapor-air mixture is too rich to ignite.
attributes.references: ASTM E681 Standard Test Method for Concentration Limits of Flammability

attributes.name: flash_point_c
attributes.description: Lowest temperature at which vapors of the product will ignite when exposed to an ignition source, measured in degrees Celsius. Critical for fire hazard assessment.
attributes.references: ASTM D93 Standard Test Methods for Flash Point

attributes.name: ghs_classification
attributes.description: Globally Harmonized System hazard classification for the product, including hazard classes and categories (e.g., Flammable Liquids Category 2, Acute Toxicity Category 4).

attributes.name: handling_precautions
attributes.description: Safe handling practices and precautions to minimize exposure and prevent accidents, including grounding requirements, ventilation needs, and incompatible materials to avoid.

attributes.name: hazard_class
attributes.description: UN transport hazard class or division number indicating the primary hazard for transportation (e.g., Class 3 Flammable Liquids, Class 2.1 Flammable Gases).
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: hazard_pictograms
attributes.description: List of GHS hazard pictogram codes applicable to the product (e.g., GHS02 Flame, GHS07 Exclamation Mark, GHS08 Health Hazard), separated by semicolons.

attributes.name: hazard_statements
attributes.description: Standardized GHS hazard statements describing the nature and degree of the hazards (e.g., H225 Highly flammable liquid and vapor, H304 May be fatal if swallowed and enters airways).

attributes.name: hazardous_decomposition_products
attributes.description: Hazardous substances that may be formed when the product decomposes or burns, such as carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulfide, sulfur oxides, or nitrogen oxides.

attributes.name: incompatible_materials
attributes.description: Materials and chemical classes that should not come into contact with the product due to risk of hazardous reactions, including strong oxidizers, acids, bases, or reactive metals.

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: Date when this version of the safety data sheet was officially issued or published by the responsible party.

attributes.name: issuing_authority
attributes.description: Name of the organization or entity responsible for issuing and maintaining the safety data sheet, typically the manufacturer, importer, or distributor.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 639-2 language code indicating the language in which the safety data sheet is written (e.g., ENG for English, SPA for Spanish).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp indicating when this safety data sheet record was last updated or modified in the data management system.

attributes.name: odor
attributes.description: Characteristic odor or smell of the product (e.g., petroleum-like, sweet, pungent, odorless), important for leak detection and worker awareness.

attributes.name: packing_group
attributes.description: UN packing group indicating the degree of danger for transport: I (high danger), II (medium danger), III (low danger). Not applicable for all hazard classes.
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: physical_state
attributes.description: Physical state or form of the product at normal temperature and pressure (solid, liquid, gas, vapor, or aerosol).

attributes.name: ppe_requirements
attributes.description: Comprehensive personal protective equipment requirements including respiratory protection, hand protection (glove material and breakthrough time), eye and face protection, and skin and body protection specifications for safe handling of the product.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132 General Requirements for PPE; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 Respiratory Protection

attributes.name: precautionary_statements
attributes.description: Standardized GHS precautionary statements describing recommended measures to minimize or prevent adverse effects (e.g., P210 Keep away from heat/sparks/open flames, P280 Wear protective gloves/eye protection).

attributes.name: proper_shipping_name
attributes.description: Official UN proper shipping name for the product as it must appear on shipping documents and package markings for transport of dangerous goods.
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: regulatory_information
attributes.description: Summary of applicable regulatory requirements including TSCA status, SARA Title III reporting, California Proposition 65, REACH registration, and other jurisdiction-specific regulations.
attributes.references: EPA TSCA; SARA Title III; REACH Regulation (EC) 1907/2006

attributes.name: revision_date
attributes.description: Date when the safety data sheet was last revised or updated, indicating the most recent modification to the document content.

attributes.name: sds_number
attributes.description: Unique business identifier for the safety data sheet document, typically assigned by the issuing authority or manufacturer.

attributes.name: sds_version
attributes.description: Version number or revision identifier of the safety data sheet, used to track updates and changes over time.

attributes.name: signal_word
attributes.description: GHS signal word indicating the relative level of severity of hazard: Danger for more severe hazards, Warning for less severe hazards.

attributes.name: solubility_in_water
attributes.description: Description of the products solubility or miscibility in water (e.g., negligible, slightly soluble, miscible, insoluble), important for spill response and environmental impact.

attributes.name: specific_gravity
attributes.description: Ratio of the density of the product to the density of water at a specified temperature. Values less than 1.0 indicate the product floats on water; greater than 1.0 indicates it sinks.
attributes.references: ASTM D891 Standard Test Methods for Specific Gravity

attributes.name: stability
attributes.description: Indication of whether the product is chemically stable under normal storage and handling conditions, or if it may undergo hazardous reactions.

attributes.name: storage_requirements
attributes.description: Safe storage conditions and requirements including temperature limits, ventilation needs, container specifications, segregation from incompatible materials, and special storage considerations.

attributes.name: toxicological_information
attributes.description: Summary of toxicological data including acute toxicity (LD50/LC50), routes of exposure, target organs, chronic health effects, carcinogenicity, and reproductive toxicity.

attributes.name: un_number
attributes.description: Four-digit United Nations identification number for dangerous goods used in international transport (e.g., UN1203 for gasoline, UN1075 for LPG).
attributes.references: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: vapor_pressure_kpa
attributes.description: Pressure exerted by the vapor of the product at a specified temperature, measured in kilopascals. Indicates volatility and evaporation rate.
attributes.references: ASTM D323 Standard Test Method for Vapor Pressure

products.name: price_history
products.description: Transactional record of historical realized and posted prices for petroleum products — capturing daily/monthly posted prices, spot market prices, netback values, and transfer prices by product grade, market, and pricing period. Includes benchmark price, differential applied, final realized price, currency, volume basis, and price source. Used for revenue analysis, contract settlement verification, and SEC reserves valuation (SEC 12-month average price).
products.reference: SEC Rule 4-10 / PRMS Price Basis / Platts Price History

attributes.name: price_history_id
attributes.description: Primary key for price_history

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Reference to the petroleum product for which the price is recorded. Links to the product master catalog.

attributes.name: pricing_benchmark_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_pricing_benchmark. Business justification: Links historical price records to the pricing benchmark used for that transaction. price_history currently has pricing_index as a STRING field containing benchmark names. Adding FK to product_pricing_

attributes.name: profit_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Product pricing is tracked by profit center for revenue recognition, realized margin calculation, and performance attribution in oil-and-gas trading and marketing operations.

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: The API gravity of the crude oil or petroleum product at the time of pricing, used for quality-based price adjustments.

attributes.name: benchmark_price
attributes.description: The base reference price from the applicable pricing index before any adjustments or differentials are applied. Expressed in the pricing currency per unit of measure.

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the sales contract, purchase agreement, or term contract under which this price was established or applied.

attributes.name: counterparty_name
attributes.description: The name of the buyer or seller counterparty involved in the transaction for which this price applies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this price history record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: final_price
attributes.description: The actual price per unit after applying all differentials and adjustments to the benchmark price. This is the realized or posted price used for revenue calculation and contract settlement.

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal accounting period (month and year) to which this price record is assigned for financial reporting purposes.

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The user identifier or system account that most recently modified this price history record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this price history record was most recently updated, supporting audit trail and change tracking requirements.

attributes.name: market_region
attributes.description: The geographic market or trading region where this price is applicable, such as Gulf Coast, Permian Basin, North Sea, or Asia Pacific.

attributes.name: price_adjustment_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for any price revision or adjustment, documenting the business rationale for changes to previously posted prices.

attributes.name: price_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code indicating the currency in which the price is denominated. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USD|EUR|GBP|CAD|AUD|JPY|CNY — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: price_date
attributes.description: The specific date on which the price was set, posted, or realized. Primary business event timestamp for the price record.

attributes.name: price_differential
attributes.description: The adjustment amount (positive or negative) applied to the benchmark price to arrive at the final price. Reflects quality, location, and market factors.

attributes.name: price_effective_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this price became effective for transactions and settlements.

attributes.name: price_expiration_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this price ceased to be effective, marking the end of its applicability period.

attributes.name: price_notes
attributes.description: Additional comments, explanations, or contextual information about the price record, including special conditions or market factors.

attributes.name: price_record_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the price record, used for external reference and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: price_source
attributes.description: The authoritative source or system from which the price was obtained, such as trading platform, pricing service, contract agreement, or internal calculation.

attributes.name: price_source_system
attributes.description: The name of the source system or application from which the price data was extracted or received, such as trading system, ERP, or pricing service feed.

attributes.name: price_status
attributes.description: The current status of the price record in its lifecycle: preliminary (initial estimate), confirmed (validated), revised (updated after initial posting), final (locked for accounting), or cancelled (voided).

attributes.name: price_type
attributes.description: Classification of the price record indicating the nature of the pricing: posted price (published reference), spot market price (immediate delivery), realized price (actual received), netback value (after transportation and processing costs), transfer price (inter-company), benchmark price (index reference), or contract price (negotiated term). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: posted|spot|realized|netback|transfer|benchmark|contract — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: price_unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for which the price is quoted: Barrel (BBL), Metric Ton (MT), Thousand Cubic Feet (MCF), Million British Thermal Units (MMBTU), Gallon (GAL), Pound (LB), Kilogram (KG), or Cubic Meter (M3). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BBL|MT|MCF|MMBTU|GAL|LB|KG|M3 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: pricing_period_end_date
attributes.description: The ending date of the period for which this price is applicable. For spot prices, may equal start date.

attributes.name: pricing_period_start_date
attributes.description: The beginning date of the period for which this price is applicable. Used for daily, monthly, or custom period pricing.

attributes.name: pricing_point
attributes.description: The physical or commercial location where the price applies, such as wellhead, custody transfer point, refinery gate, or delivery terminal.

attributes.name: processing_cost
attributes.description: The per-unit processing or treatment cost deducted from the benchmark price to calculate netback value, expressed in the same currency and unit of measure as the price.

attributes.name: product_grade
attributes.description: The specific grade or quality specification of the product for which the price applies, such as sweet crude, sour crude, premium gasoline, or pipeline quality natural gas.

attributes.name: sec_pricing_flag

attributes.description: Indicates whether this price record is used for SEC reserves valuation and disclosure purposes, specifically for calculating the 12-month average price required by SEC regulations.

attributes.name: settlement_reference

attributes.name: sulfur_content_percent

attributes.name: transportation_cost

attributes.name: volume_basis

attributes.name: created_by
