attributes.name: allocated_volume_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Allocated Volume in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: The production volume allocated under this quota, expressed in barrels of oil per day (BOPD). This is the target or ceiling production rate for the allocation period.
attributes.references: OPEC Production Quota Standards, SPE (Society of Petroleum Engineers) Production Reporting Guidelines

attributes.name: allocation_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the quota allocation record, formatted as QA-YYYYMMDD for traceability and external reference.

attributes.name: allocation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the quota allocation: draft (pending approval), active (in effect), suspended (temporarily halted), expired (period ended), revised (superseded by new allocation), or cancelled (voided).

attributes.name: allocation_type
attributes.description: Classification of the quota allocation by organizational or contractual scope: OPEC country-level quota, internal asset allocation, equity partner entitlement, field-level production cap, joint venture allocation, or production sharing agreement allocation.
attributes.references: OPEC Production Quota Framework, PSA (Production Sharing Agreement) Standards

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: The name or title of the executive or committee that approved the quota allocation (e.g., VP Commercial, OPEC Ministerial Council, Joint Venture Management Committee).
attributes.references: Internal Authorization Matrix, JOA Governance Standards

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the quota allocation was formally approved by the designated authority. Marks the transition from draft to active status.

attributes.name: benchmark_reference
attributes.description: The crude oil pricing benchmark or reference basket used for quota valuation and compliance reporting: OPEC Reference Basket, WTI (West Texas Intermediate), Brent, Dubai, Urals, or other regional benchmark.
attributes.references: OPEC Reference Basket Methodology, WTI and Brent Pricing Standards

attributes.name: compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether actual production is within the compliance threshold. True indicates compliance, False indicates a breach requiring reporting or corrective action.

attributes.name: compliance_threshold_percentage
attributes.description: The allowable tolerance percentage for over-production or under-production relative to the allocated quota before triggering compliance action or penalty. Typically expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5.00 for 5%).

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the country to which the OPEC quota is allocated (e.g., SAU for Saudi Arabia, IRQ for Iraq). Applicable for OPEC country-level allocations.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3, OPEC Member Country Registry

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this quota allocation record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Policy, SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Compliance

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the individual who last modified this quota allocation record. Supports audit trail and accountability.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Policy, SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Compliance

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this quota allocation record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Policy, SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Compliance

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, special conditions, or operational notes related to the quota allocation (e.g., seasonal adjustments, partner-specific terms, force majeure declarations).

attributes.name: overlift_position_barrels
attributes.description: Cumulative volume of crude oil produced in excess of the allocated quota during the period, measured in barrels. Used for equity crude balancing and partner settlement.
attributes.references: Equity Crude Lifting Standards, JIB (Joint Interest Billing) Guidelines

attributes.name: quota_manager_name
attributes.description: The name of the individual responsible for day-to-day management and compliance monitoring of this quota allocation.

attributes.name: quota_period_end_date
attributes.description: The effective end date of the quota allocation period. Null indicates an open-ended allocation subject to revision.

attributes.name: quota_period_start_date
attributes.description: The effective start date of the quota allocation period, typically aligned with OPEC quota cycle or fiscal planning period.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_obligation
attributes.description: The regulatory or compliance reporting requirement associated with this quota allocation: OPEC monthly production report, SEC annual reserves disclosure, BSEE quarterly offshore production report, internal management reporting only, or no external reporting.
attributes.references: OPEC Reporting Standards, SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200, BSEE Production Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: reporting_deadline_date
attributes.description: The deadline date by which compliance or production data for this quota allocation must be submitted to the relevant regulatory authority (OPEC, SEC, BSEE, etc.).
attributes.references: OPEC Reporting Calendar, SEC Filing Deadlines, BSEE Reporting Schedule

attributes.name: responsible_business_unit
attributes.description: The organizational unit or division responsible for managing and monitoring compliance with this quota allocation (e.g., Upstream Commercial, Marketing & Trading, Joint Venture Operations).
attributes.references: Internal Organizational Hierarchy, SAP S/4HANA Organizational Structure

attributes.name: underlift_position_barrels
attributes.description: Cumulative volume of crude oil produced below the allocated quota during the period, measured in barrels. Represents unutilized entitlement that may be carried forward or settled.
attributes.references: Equity Crude Lifting Standards, JIB (Joint Interest Billing) Guidelines

attributes.name: variance_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Variance in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: The difference between allocated volume and actual production, expressed in BOPD. Positive values indicate over-production (over-lift), negative values indicate under-production (under-lift).
attributes.references: OPEC Compliance Reporting, Internal Production Variance Analysis

products.name: lifting_program
products.description: Operational master record defining the monthly or quarterly equity crude oil lifting program for each equity partner or working interest (WI) holder under a joint operating agreement (JOA) or production sharing agreement (PSA). Captures lifting month, partner entity, equity entitlement volume (BOPD), scheduled lifting dates, terminal allocation, and over/under-lift balance. Coordinates commercial entitlements with production allocation and cargo nomination.

attributes.name: lifting_program_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the lifting program record. Primary key for the lifting program entity.

attributes.name: cargo_nomination_id
attributes.description: Reference to the cargo nomination submitted by the partner for this lifting program. Links to the detailed vessel and cargo specifications.

attributes.name: commercial_term_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.term_contract. Business justification: Lifting programs can be linked to term contracts for equity crude lifting under contractual arrangements. This FK links a lifting program to the term contract it executes. Nullable - lifting programs

attributes.name: crude_grade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.crude_grade. Business justification: Lifting programs specify crude grade for equity entitlement allocation. Business process: joint venture crude lifting requires grade-specific volume allocation and pricing.

attributes.name: customer_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_counterparty. Business justification: Lifting programs allocate equity crude volumes to specific customers under PSA/JOA arrangements. Critical for entitlement tracking, overlift/underlift balancing, and coordinating customer lifting sche

attributes.name: field_id
attributes.description: Reference to the oil or gas field from which crude oil or natural gas is being lifted under this program.
attributes.references: Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE) Field Classification

attributes.name: h2s_monitoring_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to hse.h2s_monitoring. Business justification: Lifting operations at sour crude production facilities require H2S monitoring during cargo transfer. Production facility safety requirement links lifting programs to H2S monitoring for personnel safet

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Joint Operating Agreement under which this lifting program is executed. Links to the governing JOA contract.
attributes.references: American Petroleum Institute (API) Joint Operations Standards

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Lifting programs allocate crude production from specific leases to JV partners based on working interest and net revenue interest. Essential for equity crude entitlement calculations, underlift/overli

attributes.name: marine_services_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Lifting programs specify approved vendors for marine services (vessel agents, stevedores, surveyors) at export terminals. Required for vendor performance tracking, cost allocation to lifting operation

attributes.name: modified_by_user_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Modified By User Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Lifting program modifications affect JV partner entitlements and revenue allocation; audit trails must link changes to employee records for dispute resolution, compliance investigations, and operation

attributes.name: offtake_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.offtake_agreement. Business justification: Lifting programs execute offtake agreements. This FK links a lifting program to the offtake agreement it fulfills. Nullable - lifting programs can be driven by JOAs, PSAs, or offtake agreements.

attributes.name: opec_quota_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.opec_quota_position. Business justification: Lifting programs must comply with OPEC quota positions; production scheduling depends on quota compliance status. Oil-and-gas companies in OPEC countries must link lifting schedules to quota positions

attributes.name: partner_id
attributes.description: Reference to the equity partner or working interest holder entitled to lift crude oil or natural gas under this program. May be an International Oil Company (IOC), National Oil Company (NOC), or other joint venture partner.

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Production Sharing Agreement under which this lifting program is executed. Links to the governing PSA contract.

attributes.name: terminal_id
attributes.description: Reference to the export terminal, loading facility, or Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel where the partner will lift their crude oil or natural gas.

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: The API gravity of the crude oil being lifted, a measure of how heavy or light the petroleum liquid is compared to water. Higher API gravity indicates lighter crude oil.

attributes.name: approval_authority
attributes.description: The name or title of the individual or committee that approved this lifting program. Used for governance and audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) and Approval Standards

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: The date when this lifting program was formally approved by the authorized authority.
attributes.references: Authorization for Expenditure (AFE) and Approval Standards

attributes.name: balance_volume_uom
attributes.description: The unit of measure for underlift, overlift, and net balance volumes. Must be consistent with entitlement volume unit of measure.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this lifting program record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for pricing and settlement of this lifting program (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: entitlement_volume_uom
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the equity entitlement volume. Common units include BBL (barrels) for crude oil, BOE (barrel of oil equivalent), MMBTU (million British thermal units), MCF (thousand cubic feet), or MMCF (million cubic feet) for natural gas.

attributes.name: equity_entitlement_volume
attributes.description: The total volume of crude oil or natural gas the partner is entitled to lift during this program period, calculated based on their net revenue interest and the field production allocation.

attributes.name: estimated_lifting_value
attributes.description: The estimated total commercial value of the crude oil or natural gas to be lifted under this program, calculated based on entitlement volume, benchmark price, and price differential.

attributes.name: lifting_month
attributes.description: The calendar month for which this lifting program applies, formatted as YYYY-MM. Used for monthly lifting schedule coordination.

attributes.name: lifting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the lifting period covered by this program, typically the last day of a calendar month or quarter.
attributes.references: Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) Guidelines

attributes.name: lifting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the lifting period covered by this program, typically the first day of a calendar month or quarter.
attributes.references: Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) Guidelines

attributes.name: lifting_quarter
attributes.description: The calendar quarter for which this lifting program applies (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4). Used for quarterly lifting schedule coordination.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this lifting program record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: net_balance_volume
attributes.description: The net cumulative lifting balance for the partner, calculated as underlift balance minus overlift balance. A positive value indicates underlift, a negative value indicates overlift.

attributes.name: net_revenue_interest_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of production revenue the partner is entitled to receive after deducting royalties, overriding royalty interests (ORRI), and other burdens. NRI is typically less than or equal to WI.
attributes.references: Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) NRI Standards

attributes.name: opec_quota_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) Quota Impact Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifting program is subject to OPEC production quota restrictions. True if the field production is constrained by OPEC quota management.
attributes.references: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) Quota Framework

attributes.name: overlift_balance_volume
attributes.description: The cumulative volume by which the partner has lifted more than their equity entitlement in prior periods. A positive overlift balance indicates the partner must reduce future liftings or compensate other partners.

attributes.name: price_differential
attributes.description: The premium or discount applied to the benchmark price for this specific crude grade or delivery point, expressed in currency per barrel or per unit. Used to calculate the actual lifting price.

attributes.name: pricing_benchmark
attributes.description: The market benchmark index used for pricing the crude oil or natural gas lifted under this program. Common benchmarks include WTI (West Texas Intermediate), Brent, Dubai for crude oil, and Henry Hub or JKM (Japan Korea Marker) for natural gas.

attributes.name: program_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional operational notes, special instructions, or comments related to this lifting program. May include coordination details, exceptions, or partner-specific requirements.

attributes.name: program_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the lifting program, typically formatted as LP- followed by numeric sequence. Used for external communication and operational reference.

attributes.name: program_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the lifting program. Draft indicates planning phase, approved indicates authorization received, active indicates execution in progress, completed indicates all liftings fulfilled, cancelled indicates program terminated, suspended indicates temporary hold.

attributes.name: scheduled_lifting_end_date
attributes.description: The planned date when the partner will complete lifting their equity crude oil or natural gas under this program.

attributes.name: scheduled_lifting_start_date
attributes.description: The planned date when the partner will begin lifting their equity crude oil or natural gas under this program.

attributes.name: sulfur_content_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of sulfur content in the crude oil being lifted. Low sulfur content (sweet crude) is more valuable than high sulfur content (sour crude).

attributes.name: terminal_allocation_slot
attributes.description: The specific time slot or berth allocation assigned to the partner for loading operations at the terminal. Used for coordinating vessel scheduling and avoiding conflicts.
attributes.references: Terminal Scheduling and Slot Management Standards

attributes.name: underlift_balance_volume
attributes.description: The cumulative volume by which the partner has lifted less than their equity entitlement in prior periods. A positive underlift balance indicates the partner is owed additional volume in future liftings.

attributes.name: working_interest_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage ownership interest held by the partner in the field or well, representing their share of capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operating expenditure (OPEX) obligations as well as production entitlement.
attributes.references: Council of Petroleum Accountants Societies (COPAS) WI Standards

products.name: marketing_deal
products.description: Master record for crude oil and petroleum product marketing deals negotiated by the commercial marketing team, covering equity crude marketing, third-party trading, and product exchange arrangements. Captures deal type (crude marketing, product marketing, exchange, buy-back), commodity, origin field or refinery, destination market, counterparty, volume, pricing basis and realized differential, marketing margin, deal status (negotiating, confirmed, executing, closed), trader responsible, and deal approval chain. Supports commercial performance tracking, marketing revenue attribution, and trader performance benchmarking.

attributes.name: marketing_deal_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the marketing deal record. Primary key for the marketing deal entity.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Marketing deals executed with customer accounts for margin tracking and performance reporting. Required for account-level profitability analysis, marketing margin attribution, and customer relationshi

attributes.name: commercial_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the external party (buyer or seller) with whom the marketing deal is executed. May be an IOC, NOC, trading house, refiner, or end consumer.

attributes.name: commercial_term_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.term_contract. Business justification: Marketing deals can be structured under term contracts. This FK links a marketing deal to the parent term contract it executes. Nullable - marketing deals can be standalone or contract-based.

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.procurement_contract. Business justification: Marketing deals reference transportation or processing procurement contracts that affect netback calculations. Required for margin analysis, cost allocation, and profitability reporting in integrated

attributes.name: delivery_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific physical location where commodity delivery will occur, such as a pipeline interconnect, marine terminal, storage facility, or refinery gate.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee responsible for negotiating and executing the marketing deal. Used for performance tracking, commission calculation, and accountability.

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Marketing deals monetize JV equity crude per partner entitlements. Links deal to JOA for working interest allocation, lifting rights verification, and underlift/overlift impact on partner balances.

attributes.name: ngl_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.ngl_stream. Business justification: NGL marketing deals specify stream composition (ethane, propane, butane). Business process: NGL marketing requires stream-specific pricing and logistics planning.

attributes.name: origin_refinery_id
attributes.description: Reference to the refinery or processing plant from which the marketed product originates. Applicable for refined product and petrochemical marketing deals where the company is selling output from its downstream facilities.

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Marketing deals specify which petroleum product is being marketed. Business process: deal structuring and margin calculation require product identification for pricing and logistics.

attributes.name: pricing_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.pricing_agreement. Business justification: Marketing deals reference pricing agreements for pricing terms. This FK links a marketing deal to the pricing agreement governing its pricing. Nullable - some marketing deals use ad-hoc pricing rather

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: Marketing deals for PSA contractor/government crude. Links deal to PSA for profit oil entitlement, cost recovery status, and compliance with domestic market obligation and export license requirements.

attributes.name: refined_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.refined_product. Business justification: Refined product marketing deals require specific grade identification. Business process: downstream marketing operations require refined product specs for deal structuring.

attributes.name: approval_authority_level
attributes.description: Organizational level required to approve the marketing deal based on deal value, risk exposure, or strategic importance. Trader for routine deals; desk head for moderate deals; VP Commercial for large deals; CFO for very large deals; board for strategic transactions.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the marketing deal received final approval from the designated authority. Required before deal execution can commence.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual who provided final approval for the marketing deal. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: benchmark_price
attributes.description: Reference price from the selected pricing basis at the time of deal execution or settlement. Expressed in currency per unit (e.g., USD per barrel for crude oil, USD per MMBtu for natural gas).

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Organizational business unit responsible for the marketing deal. Typically aligns with upstream (E&P), midstream (pipelines, storage), or downstream (refining, marketing) divisions.

attributes.name: confirmation_date
attributes.description: Date when the marketing deal terms were confirmed and agreed upon by both parties. Marks the transition from negotiating to confirmed status.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference to the master term contract or framework agreement under which this marketing deal is executed, if applicable. Null for standalone spot deals.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the marketing deal record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: deal_end_date
attributes.description: Date when commodity delivery or performance under the marketing deal is scheduled to complete. Marks the end of the execution phase.

attributes.name: deal_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, special terms, or operational notes related to the marketing deal. Used for trader handoff, audit trail, and institutional knowledge capture.

attributes.name: deal_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the marketing deal, formatted as MD-YYYYNNNN where YYYY is year and NNNN is sequence number. Used for communication with counterparties and internal tracking.

attributes.name: deal_start_date
attributes.description: Date when commodity delivery or performance under the marketing deal begins. Marks the start of the execution phase.

attributes.name: deal_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the marketing deal. Negotiating indicates terms are being discussed; confirmed indicates agreement reached; executing indicates active delivery; closed indicates completed; cancelled indicates terminated before completion; suspended indicates temporarily halted.

attributes.name: deal_type
attributes.description: Classification of the marketing deal by transaction structure. Crude marketing covers equity crude sales; product marketing covers refined product sales; exchange covers product swaps; buy-back covers temporary sales with repurchase obligation; NGL marketing covers natural gas liquids sales; LNG marketing covers liquefied natural gas sales.

attributes.name: destination_market
attributes.description: Geographic market or region where the commodity will be delivered or consumed. Examples include US Gulf Coast, Northwest Europe, Asia Pacific, or specific trading hubs like Rotterdam or Singapore.

attributes.name: hedging_instrument_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the marketing deal is paired with a financial hedging instrument (futures, swaps, options) to mitigate price risk. True if hedged; false if unhedged spot exposure.

attributes.name: incoterms
attributes.description: Standard trade terms defining the responsibilities of buyer and seller for transportation, insurance, and risk transfer. FOB is Free on Board; CIF is Cost Insurance and Freight; CFR is Cost and Freight; DES is Delivered Ex Ship; DAP is Delivered at Place; EXW is Ex Works.

attributes.name: marketing_margin
attributes.description: Gross profit margin earned on the marketing deal, calculated as the difference between realized sales price and acquisition or production cost, multiplied by volume. Expressed in the deal currency. Business-confidential metric used for trader performance evaluation.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier or name of the individual who last modified the marketing deal record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when the marketing deal record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: negotiation_start_date
attributes.description: Date when commercial negotiations for the marketing deal were initiated. Used for tracking deal cycle time and trader efficiency.

attributes.name: opec_quota_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) Quota Impact Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the marketing deal involves crude oil production subject to OPEC production quota management. True if the deal impacts quota compliance; false otherwise. Relevant for NOCs and IOCs operating in OPEC member countries.

attributes.name: origin_field_code
attributes.description: Reference to the upstream oil or gas field from which the marketed commodity originates. Applicable for equity crude marketing deals where the company is selling production from its own operated or non-operated fields.

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Number of days after delivery or invoice date within which payment is due. Common terms include 30, 60, or 90 days. Used for cash flow forecasting and credit risk management.

attributes.name: price_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the pricing and settlement of the deal. Most oil and gas transactions are denominated in USD, but regional deals may use EUR, GBP, JPY, or other currencies.

attributes.name: price_differential
attributes.description: Premium or discount applied to the benchmark price to arrive at the realized transaction price. Reflects quality adjustments, location basis, and market conditions. Positive values indicate premium; negative values indicate discount.

attributes.name: price_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the pricing. Per_bbl is per barrel for crude and refined products; per_mmbtu is per million British thermal units for natural gas; per_mt is per metric ton for petrochemicals; per_gallon is per gallon for retail products.

attributes.name: pricing_basis
attributes.description: Benchmark or pricing mechanism used to determine the deal price. WTI is West Texas Intermediate crude; Brent is North Sea crude; Dubai and Oman are Middle East crudes; Henry Hub is US natural gas; JKM is Japan Korea Marker for LNG; fixed indicates a set price; formula indicates a custom calculation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wti|brent|dubai|oman|henry_hub|jkm|fixed|formula — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: realized_price
attributes.description: Final transaction price per unit achieved in the marketing deal, calculated as benchmark price plus price differential. This is the actual price at which the commodity was sold or purchased.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the marketing deal is subject to mandatory regulatory reporting requirements (e.g., FERC for natural gas, CFTC for derivatives, SEC for material transactions). True if reporting required; false otherwise.

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_status
attributes.description: Result of screening the counterparty and transaction against international sanctions lists (OFAC, UN, EU). Cleared indicates no sanctions concerns; pending indicates screening in progress; flagged indicates potential match requiring review; blocked indicates prohibited transaction.

attributes.name: total_deal_value
attributes.description: Total monetary value of the marketing deal, calculated as volume quantity multiplied by realized price. Represents the gross revenue or cost associated with the transaction. Expressed in the deal currency.

attributes.name: trading_book
attributes.description: Internal trading desk or book to which the marketing deal is assigned. Used for P&L attribution, risk management, and organizational reporting. Examples include Crude Trading, Products Trading, NGL Trading, International Marketing.

attributes.name: volume_quantity
attributes.description: Total volume of commodity covered by the marketing deal. Measured in barrels for crude oil and refined products, cubic feet or cubic meters for natural gas, or metric tons for petrochemicals.

attributes.name: volume_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the volume quantity. BBL is barrels, MMBBL is million barrels, MCF is thousand cubic feet, MMCF is million cubic feet, BCF is billion cubic feet, MT is metric tons, KMT is thousand metric tons. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BBL|MMBBL|MCF|MMCF|BCF|MT|KMT — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

products.name: performance
products.description: Transactional record capturing periodic (monthly/quarterly) commercial performance actuals against plan for each term contract, offtake agreement, or marketing deal. Records period, commodity, planned volume, actual delivered volume, planned revenue, actual revenue, realized price vs. benchmark, marketing margin, and variance commentary. Serves as the operational performance ledger for the commercial domain — distinct from financial revenue recognition owned by the revenue domain.

attributes.name: performance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the commercial performance record. Primary key for this transactional performance ledger entry.

attributes.name: commercial_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the buyer or seller counterparty involved in this commercial transaction. Links to the customer.customer_counterparty product.

attributes.name: commercial_term_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying term contract for which performance is being tracked. Links to the commercial.term_contract product.

attributes.name: created_by_user_employee_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Created By User Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Performance reporting accountability requires linking report creators to employee records for data quality investigations, audit trails, and segregation of duties validation. Text field created_by_use

attributes.name: delivery_point_id
attributes.description: Reference to the physical delivery location or hub where the commodity was delivered. Links to the customer.delivery_point product.

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Commercial performance reporting for JV production sales. Links performance to JOA for partner revenue allocation, lifting performance vs. entitlement, and underlift/overlift financial impact analysis

attributes.name: marketing_deal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.marketing_deal. Business justification: Commercial performance tracking can measure marketing deal execution. This FK links performance records to the specific marketing deal being tracked. Nullable - performance can track various commercia

attributes.name: offtake_agreement_id
attributes.description: Reference to the offtake agreement for which performance is being tracked. Links to the commercial.offtake_agreement product. Nullable if performance is for a term contract or spot trade.

attributes.name: petroleum_product_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.petroleum_product. Business justification: Performance tracking requires product identification for margin analysis. Business process: commercial performance reporting and variance analysis require product-level metrics.

attributes.name: pricing_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.pricing_agreement. Business justification: Commercial performance tracking measures actual pricing vs. agreed pricing terms. This FK links performance records to the pricing agreement being evaluated. Nullable - not all performance tracking in

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: Performance reporting for PSA entitlement crude sales. Links performance to PSA for contractor/government revenue split, cost recovery tracking, and profit oil realization vs. PSA fiscal terms.

attributes.name: sales_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.sales_order. Business justification: Commercial performance tracking can measure sales order execution performance. This FK links performance records to the specific sales order being tracked. Nullable - performance can track contracts,

attributes.name: spot_trade_id
attributes.description: Reference to the spot trade for which performance is being tracked. Links to the commercial.spot_trade product. Nullable if performance is for a term contract or offtake agreement.

attributes.name: actual_delivered_volume_quantity
attributes.description: The actual volume quantity delivered during the reporting period. Represents the realized volume for performance measurement.

attributes.name: actual_revenue_amount
attributes.description: The actual revenue amount realized during the reporting period based on delivered volumes and realized pricing. Represents the achieved revenue for performance measurement.

attributes.name: approved_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who approved this commercial performance record. Audit trail for approval authority.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this commercial performance record was approved and finalized. Represents the point at which the performance data became official.

attributes.name: benchmark_price
attributes.description: The benchmark reference price (e.g., WTI, Brent, Henry Hub) applicable for the reporting period. Used to calculate price differentials and realized pricing performance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this commercial performance record was first created in the system. Audit trail for record creation.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this performance record (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

attributes.name: hedging_cost_amount
attributes.description: The net cost or benefit of hedging instruments (futures, swaps, options) associated with this commercial transaction during the reporting period.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who last modified this commercial performance record. Audit trail for accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this commercial performance record was last modified. Audit trail for record updates.

attributes.name: marketing_margin_amount
attributes.description: The gross marketing margin realized during the reporting period, calculated as revenue minus direct costs (transportation, quality adjustments, hedging costs). Represents the commercial performance contribution.

attributes.name: marketing_margin_per_unit
attributes.description: The marketing margin per unit of volume (e.g., per barrel, per MCF). Calculated as total marketing margin divided by actual delivered volume.

attributes.name: opec_quota_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) Quota Impact Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commercial performance record is subject to or impacted by OPEC production quota management. True if OPEC quota constraints apply, false otherwise.

attributes.name: performance_status
attributes.description: The current lifecycle status of this performance record: draft (being prepared), submitted (under review), approved (finalized), closed (archived), or adjusted (revised after initial approval).

attributes.name: period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the reporting period for which commercial performance is being measured. Defines the close of the performance window.

attributes.name: period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the reporting period (monthly or quarterly) for which commercial performance is being measured. Defines the beginning of the performance window.

attributes.name: planned_revenue_amount
attributes.description: The planned or budgeted revenue amount for the reporting period based on contracted pricing and planned volumes. Represents the target revenue for performance measurement.

attributes.name: planned_volume_quantity
attributes.description: The planned or committed volume quantity for the reporting period as per the contract or agreement. Represents the target volume for performance measurement.

attributes.name: price_differential
attributes.description: The difference between the realized price and the benchmark price. Positive indicates a premium, negative indicates a discount.

attributes.name: price_uom
attributes.description: The unit of measure for pricing: per barrel, per BOE, per MCF, per MMBTU, per metric ton, or per gallon.

attributes.name: quality_adjustment_amount
attributes.description: The total pricing adjustments (positive or negative) applied due to product quality variations from specification (e.g., API gravity, sulfur content, TAN adjustments).

attributes.name: realized_price
attributes.description: The actual realized price per unit achieved during the reporting period, including all adjustments, differentials, and quality premiums or discounts.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this commercial performance record must be included in regulatory reporting (e.g., FERC, SEC, OPEC). True if regulatory reporting is required, false otherwise.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K, FERC Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: reporting_period_type
attributes.description: The frequency or type of the reporting period: monthly, quarterly, annual, or spot (for one-time trades).

attributes.name: responsible_business_unit
attributes.description: The business unit or division responsible for this commercial performance (e.g., Upstream Marketing, Downstream Sales, LNG Trading). Used for organizational performance tracking.

attributes.name: revenue_variance_amount
attributes.description: The variance between planned and actual revenue (actual minus planned). Positive indicates revenue over-performance, negative indicates revenue under-performance.

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: The financial settlement status for this performance period: pending (not yet settled), partial (partially invoiced/paid), complete (fully settled), or disputed (under dispute resolution).

attributes.name: trader_name
attributes.description: The name of the trader or commercial manager responsible for executing and managing this commercial transaction.

attributes.name: trading_book
attributes.description: The trading book or portfolio to which this commercial performance is allocated for risk management and P&L tracking purposes.

attributes.name: transportation_cost_amount
attributes.description: The total transportation and logistics costs incurred during the reporting period to deliver the commodity to the delivery point.

attributes.name: variance_commentary
attributes.description: Free-text commentary explaining significant variances between planned and actual performance, including root causes, market conditions, operational issues, or force majeure events.

attributes.name: volume_uom
attributes.description: The unit of measure for volume quantities: barrels (bbl), Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE), thousand cubic feet (MCF), million cubic feet (MMCF), billion cubic feet (BCF), million British thermal units (MMBTU), metric tons (MT), or gallons (gal). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: bbl|boe|mcf|mmcf|bcf|mmbtu|mt|gal — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: volume_variance_quantity
attributes.description: The variance between planned and actual delivered volume (actual minus planned). Positive indicates over-delivery, negative indicates under-delivery.

products.name: commodity_exposure
products.description: Transactional record quantifying the net commodity price exposure of the commercial portfolio at a given valuation date, broken down by commodity, tenor bucket, and instrument type (physical, futures, swaps, options). Captures gross long exposure, gross short exposure, net exposure in BOE, delta-equivalent volume, value-at-risk (VaR), and stress-test scenario results. Supports commercial risk management and treasury reporting.
products.reference: CTRM Risk Exposure Report / IFRS 7 Market Risk Disclosure

attributes.name: commodity_exposure_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the commodity exposure record. Primary key for the commodity exposure transactional snapshot.

attributes.name: commercial_term_contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.term_contract. Business justification: Commodity exposure includes term contract positions. This FK links exposure records to specific term contracts. Nullable - exposure can represent various position types or aggregated portfolio exposur

attributes.name: hedging_instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.hedging_instrument. Business justification: Commodity exposure includes hedging instrument positions. This FK links exposure records to specific hedging instruments. Nullable - exposure can represent physical positions, financial hedges, or agg

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Commodity risk exposure from JV production commitments. Links exposure to JOA for partner entitlement volume risk, underlift/overlift exposure, and value-at-risk calculation for JV equity crude.

attributes.name: portfolio_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the trading portfolio or risk management portfolio to which this exposure belongs. Enables portfolio-level aggregation and analysis.

attributes.name: primary_commodity_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key reference to the trader or risk manager responsible for this exposure position. Supports performance attribution and accountability tracking.

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: Risk exposure from PSA entitlement crude. Links exposure to PSA for contractor profit oil volume risk, cost recovery ceiling impact, and mark-to-market valuation of government/contractor positions.

attributes.name: spot_trade_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.spot_trade. Business justification: Commodity exposure includes spot trade positions. This FK links exposure records to specific spot trades. Nullable - exposure can represent various position types or aggregated portfolio exposure.

attributes.name: trading_position_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to commercial.trading_position. Business justification: Commodity exposure is calculated from trading positions. This FK links an exposure calculation to the specific trading position it represents. Nullable - exposure can be aggregated across multiple pos

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Approval workflow status for the exposure position: pending (awaiting review), approved (authorized), rejected (not authorized), or under review (in approval process).

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the exposure position was approved by the authorized user. Critical for audit trail and compliance with internal authorization policies.

attributes.name: benchmark_price_reference
attributes.description: The market benchmark or index used for pricing this exposure (e.g., NYMEX WTI, ICE Brent, Henry Hub, Platts). Defines the pricing basis for valuation.

attributes.name: benchmark_price_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Benchmark Price in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Current market price of the benchmark reference at the valuation date, expressed in USD per unit (barrel, MMBtu, gallon). Used for mark-to-market calculations.

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: The business unit or division responsible for managing this exposure (e.g., Upstream Marketing, Downstream Trading, NGL Trading). Supports organizational reporting and accountability.

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The methodology or model used to calculate the exposure metrics (e.g., Historical Simulation VaR, Monte Carlo VaR, Parametric VaR, Delta-Normal). Documents the risk calculation approach for audit and validation.

attributes.name: commodity_grade
attributes.description: Specific grade or quality specification of the commodity (e.g., WTI, Brent, Henry Hub, Ethane, Propane). Defines the exact product being traded or hedged.

attributes.name: commodity_type
attributes.description: The primary commodity category for this exposure position. Aligns with upstream and downstream product classifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: crude_oil|natural_gas|ngl|lng|lpg|refined_products|petrochemicals — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: counterparty_concentration_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) signaling whether this exposure contributes to a counterparty concentration risk that exceeds internal risk limits or regulatory thresholds.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this exposure record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data lineage and change tracking.

attributes.name: credit_valuation_adjustment_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA) in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Credit valuation adjustment in USD reflecting the market value of counterparty credit risk. Represents the expected loss due to counterparty default over the life of the exposure.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the exposure valuation (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Defines the reporting currency for all monetary amounts.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: The upstream system or trading platform from which the exposure data was sourced (e.g., SAP SD, Endur, Allegro, RightAngle). Provides data lineage for reconciliation and audit.

attributes.name: delta_equivalent_volume_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Delta-Equivalent Volume in Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Risk-adjusted exposure volume accounting for option delta and other non-linear instrument sensitivities. Represents the equivalent linear exposure for risk management purposes.

attributes.name: exposure_number
attributes.description: Business-facing unique reference number for the exposure snapshot, formatted as EXP-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX for traceability and audit purposes.

attributes.name: exposure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the exposure position: active (open position), closed (settled), expired (matured without rollover), rolled (extended to next tenor), or cancelled.

attributes.name: gross_long_exposure_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Long Exposure in Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Total long (buy) position exposure expressed in BOE. Represents the aggregate volume the company is committed to purchase or receive across all instruments in this commodity/tenor/instrument combination.

attributes.name: gross_short_exposure_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gross Short Exposure in Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Total short (sell) position exposure expressed in BOE. Represents the aggregate volume the company is committed to deliver or sell across all instruments in this commodity/tenor/instrument combination.

attributes.name: hedge_designation
attributes.description: Accounting hedge designation status under IFRS 9 or GAAP: cash flow hedge, fair value hedge, net investment hedge, economic hedge (not designated for accounting), or not designated.

attributes.name: hedge_effectiveness_percentage
attributes.description: Measured effectiveness of the hedge relationship, expressed as a percentage. Must typically fall within 80-125% range to qualify for hedge accounting treatment under IFRS 9.

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: Classification of the financial or physical instrument contributing to this exposure: physical contracts, exchange-traded futures, OTC swaps, options, basis swaps, crack spreads, or collar structures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: physical|futures|swaps|options|basis_swaps|crack_spreads|collars — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: mark_to_market_value_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Mark-to-Market Value in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Current fair value of the exposure position based on prevailing market prices at the valuation date. Reflects unrealized gain or loss on the position.

attributes.name: net_exposure_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Net Exposure in Barrels of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Net commodity exposure calculated as gross long exposure minus gross short exposure, expressed in BOE. Positive values indicate net long position; negative values indicate net short position.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, commentary, or special instructions related to this exposure position. Used for documenting unusual circumstances or risk management decisions.

attributes.name: notional_value_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Notional Value in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Total notional value of the exposure position in USD, calculated as net exposure volume multiplied by current market price. Used for portfolio sizing and limit monitoring.

attributes.name: opec_quota_impact_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) Quota Impact Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) identifying whether this exposure is subject to or influenced by OPEC production quota agreements and market coordination decisions.

attributes.name: price_differential_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Price Differential in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Basis differential or quality adjustment applied to the benchmark price, expressed in USD per unit. Accounts for location, quality, or delivery timing differences.

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator (True/False) signaling whether this exposure must be included in regulatory filings such as SEC disclosures, FERC reports, or CFTC position reports.

attributes.name: risk_limit_utilization_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of the applicable risk limit consumed by this exposure, calculated as (exposure amount / limit threshold) * 100. Used for limit monitoring and escalation triggers.

attributes.name: stress_test_result_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Stress Test Result in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Estimated profit or loss in USD under the specified stress test scenario. Negative values indicate potential losses; positive values indicate potential gains.

attributes.name: stress_test_scenario
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the stress test scenario applied to this exposure (e.g., WTI Down 30%, OPEC Production Cut, Demand Shock). Links to predefined scenario library.

attributes.name: tenor_bucket
attributes.description: Time horizon classification for the exposure: spot (immediate delivery), prompt (next month), M1-M3 (monthly buckets), Q1-Q4 (quarterly), CAL (calendar year strips), or long-term (beyond 3 years). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spot|prompt|m1|m2|m3|q1|q2|q3|q4|cal_1|cal_2|cal_3|long_term — 13 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: trading_book
attributes.description: The trading book or portfolio to which this exposure is allocated. Used for P&L attribution, risk limit monitoring, and trader performance evaluation.

attributes.name: valuation_date
attributes.description: The business date on which this commodity exposure position was calculated and valued. Represents the snapshot date for mark-to-market valuation.

attributes.name: valuation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the exposure calculation was executed, including time zone. Critical for intraday position reconciliation and audit trail.

attributes.name: value_at_risk_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Value at Risk (VaR) in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Statistical measure of potential loss in USD over a defined time horizon (typically 1-day or 10-day) at a specified confidence level (typically 95% or 99%). Quantifies downside risk exposure.

attributes.name: var_confidence_level
attributes.business_glossary_term: Value at Risk (VaR) Confidence Level Percentage
attributes.description: Confidence level used in the VaR calculation, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 95.00, 99.00). Indicates the probability that actual losses will not exceed the VaR estimate.

attributes.name: var_time_horizon_days
attributes.business_glossary_term: Value at Risk (VaR) Time Horizon in Days
attributes.description: Time horizon in days over which the VaR is calculated (typically 1, 10, or 20 days). Represents the holding period assumption for the risk calculation.

products.name: commercial_counterparty
products.description: Master record for commercial counterparties and their credit profiles, covering entities engaged in crude oil trading, LNG/LPG sales, refined product distribution, and petrochemical marketing — including IOCs, NOCs, independent traders, refiners, utilities, and industrial buyers. Captures counterparty legal name, entity type, country of incorporation, credit rating, approved credit limit (amount, currency, type — unsecured/LC/parent guarantee), credit utilization and available headroom, approved commodity list, ISDA agreement status, KYC/AML compliance status, and credit review schedule. Scoped to commercial trading relationships and credit risk management; full customer identity master is owned by the customer domain.
products.reference: ISDA Counterparty Classification / COPAS Partner Record

attributes.name: commercial_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the commercial counterparty record. Primary key for the commercial counterparty master data product.

attributes.name: relationship_manager_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Counterparty relationship management, credit review coordination, and commercial performance tracking require linking relationship managers to employee records for CRM analytics, performance reviews,

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Commercial counterparties (trading houses, refiners) are often also vendors in procurement. Required for master data management, consolidated credit limit tracking, sanctions screening coordination, a

attributes.name: aml_status
attributes.description: Current Anti-Money Laundering screening status for this counterparty. Cleared (no issues), flagged (potential concern), under review (investigation in progress), or blocked (prohibited from trading).

attributes.name: approved_commodity_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of commodity types this counterparty is approved to trade. May include crude oil, LNG, LPG, NGL, refined products (gasoline, diesel, jet fuel), petrochemicals. Restricts trading activity to approved product categories.

attributes.name: approved_credit_limit
attributes.description: The maximum credit exposure amount approved for this counterparty by the credit committee. Expressed in the credit limit currency. Represents the total unsecured exposure the company is willing to accept.
attributes.references: Basel III; COPAS Credit Management Guidelines

attributes.name: available_credit
attributes.description: The remaining credit capacity available for new transactions with this counterparty. Calculated as approved credit limit minus credit utilization. Used for real-time credit checks during trade execution.
attributes.references: Basel III; COPAS Credit Management Guidelines

attributes.name: commercial_counterparty_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of the counterparty relationship. Active (approved for trading), inactive (no current activity but approved), suspended (temporarily restricted), or blocked (prohibited from trading).

attributes.name: country_of_incorporation
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the jurisdiction where the counterparty is legally incorporated. Critical for sanctions screening and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this counterparty record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: credit_limit_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO currency code for the approved credit limit. Typically USD for international oil and gas trading.

attributes.name: credit_limit_type
attributes.description: The type of credit support backing the approved limit. Unsecured (no collateral), letter of credit (LC), parent company guarantee, or cash collateral. Determines risk mitigation approach.
attributes.references: Basel III; COPAS Credit Management Guidelines

attributes.name: credit_rating
attributes.description: The current credit rating assigned to the counterparty by the specified rating agency. Format varies by agency (e.g., AAA, Baa2, BBB+). Drives credit limit and collateral requirements.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: credit_rating_agency
attributes.description: The agency providing the credit rating for this counterparty. Moody's, S&P (Standard & Poor's), Fitch, internal rating, or not rated.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: credit_rating_date
attributes.description: The date when the current credit rating was assigned or last affirmed. Used to determine if rating is current for credit decisions.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: credit_review_frequency
attributes.description: The scheduled frequency for periodic credit review of this counterparty. Determined by credit rating, exposure level, and risk tier. Higher risk counterparties require more frequent reviews.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: credit_utilization
attributes.description: The current amount of credit exposure utilized by this counterparty across all open transactions and commitments. Expressed in the credit limit currency. Updated in near real-time from trading and invoicing systems.
attributes.references: Basel III; COPAS Credit Management Guidelines

attributes.name: duns_number
attributes.description: Nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet identifier for the counterparty. Used for credit assessment and third-party data enrichment.

attributes.name: entity_type
attributes.description: Classification of the counterparty organization type. IOC (International Oil Company), NOC (National Oil Company), independent trader, refiner, utility, or industrial buyer. Determines credit assessment approach and commercial terms.

attributes.name: headquarters_address
attributes.description: The full street address of the counterparty's corporate headquarters. Used for legal notices and correspondence.

attributes.name: headquarters_city
attributes.description: The city where the counterparty's corporate headquarters is located.

attributes.name: headquarters_country
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code for the country where the counterparty's corporate headquarters is located. May differ from country of incorporation.

attributes.name: isda_agreement_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Agreement Date
attributes.description: The effective date of the executed ISDA master agreement. Null if no agreement is in place.

attributes.name: isda_agreement_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Agreement Status
attributes.description: Status of the ISDA master agreement with this counterparty. Executed (in force), pending (under negotiation), not required (no derivatives trading), or expired. Required for hedging and derivative transactions.

attributes.name: kyc_completion_date
attributes.description: The date when the most recent KYC review was completed and approved. Used to determine when the next periodic refresh is due.

attributes.name: kyc_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date when the current KYC approval expires and a refresh review is required. Typically 12-24 months from completion date based on risk tier.

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Current status of the Know Your Customer due diligence process for this counterparty. Approved (cleared for trading), pending (under review), expired (requires refresh), or rejected (not approved for business).

attributes.name: last_credit_review_date
attributes.description: The date when the most recent credit review was completed by the credit committee. Documents recency of credit assessment.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: legal_name
attributes.description: The full legal name of the counterparty as registered with the governing authority in their country of incorporation. Used for contract execution and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who last modified this counterparty record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this counterparty record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: next_credit_review_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date for the next periodic credit review. Used to trigger credit committee review workflow.
attributes.references: Basel III; Credit Risk Management Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or context about the counterparty relationship. Used for operational guidance and institutional knowledge.

attributes.name: onboarding_date
attributes.description: The date when this counterparty was first approved and onboarded for commercial trading. Marks the start of the business relationship.

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: The standard number of days allowed for payment after invoice date for this counterparty. Common terms are 30, 60, or 90 days. Negotiated based on credit profile and relationship.

attributes.name: primary_contact_email
attributes.description: The email address of the primary business contact. Used for trade confirmations, invoicing, and commercial correspondence.

attributes.name: primary_contact_name
attributes.description: The name of the primary business contact at the counterparty organization for commercial and credit matters.

attributes.name: primary_contact_phone
attributes.description: The phone number of the primary business contact. Used for urgent commercial and operational communications.

attributes.name: risk_tier
attributes.description: Internal risk classification tier for this counterparty based on credit rating, country risk, payment history, and exposure. Drives approval authority levels and monitoring intensity.
attributes.references: Basel III; Internal Risk Management Framework

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_date
attributes.description: The date when the most recent sanctions screening was performed. Screening is typically performed daily or in real-time for active counterparties.
attributes.references: OFAC Sanctions; UN Security Council Sanctions; EU Sanctions

attributes.name: sanctions_screening_status
attributes.description: Result of sanctions list screening against OFAC, UN, EU, and other regulatory watchlists. Cleared (no match), flagged (potential match requiring review), or blocked (confirmed match, trading prohibited).
attributes.references: OFAC Sanctions; UN Security Council Sanctions; EU Sanctions

attributes.name: short_name
attributes.description: Abbreviated or trading name of the counterparty used for operational reference and reporting displays.

attributes.name: status_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for the current status, particularly for suspended or blocked counterparties. Documents business justification for status changes.

attributes.name: tax_identification_number
attributes.description: The counterparty's tax identification number or equivalent (EIN, VAT number, etc.) in their country of incorporation. Used for tax reporting and withholding compliance.

attributes.name: venture_partner_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.partner. Business justification: Commercial counterparties are often JV partners buying/selling equity crude. Links counterparty to partner for credit limit alignment, netting agreement coordination, and partner-specific commercial t

products.name: credit_limit
products.description: Master record managing the commercial credit limits assigned to each trading counterparty, defining the maximum financial exposure the company is willing to accept. Captures counterparty reference, approved credit limit amount, currency, credit limit type (unsecured, letter of credit, parent guarantee), utilization amount, available headroom, review date, approving authority, and credit limit status. Supports pre-trade credit checking and commercial risk controls.
products.reference: ISDA Credit Support Annex (CSA) / Basel III Credit Risk Framework

attributes.name: credit_limit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the credit limit record. Primary key for the credit limit master data.

attributes.name: commercial_counterparty_id
attributes.description: Reference to the trading counterparty to whom this credit limit is assigned. Links to the customer counterparty master record.

attributes.name: venture_partner_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.partner. Business justification: Credit limits for JV partners in commercial crude transactions. Links credit limit to partner for partner-specific credit terms, netting agreement impact, and credit risk management in JV equity crude

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the credit limit was formally approved by the designated authority. Used for audit trail and compliance verification.

attributes.name: approved_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum financial exposure the company is willing to accept from this counterparty, expressed in the limit currency. Represents the ceiling for outstanding receivables and open trade positions.

attributes.name: approving_authority
attributes.description: Name or title of the individual or committee that approved this credit limit. Reflects delegation of authority based on limit size and counterparty risk rating.

attributes.name: available_amount
attributes.description: Remaining credit headroom available for new transactions, calculated as approved limit minus utilized amount. Used for pre-trade credit checks.

attributes.name: breach_count
attributes.description: Number of times this credit limit has been exceeded. Triggers escalation and potential limit suspension.

attributes.name: business_unit
attributes.description: Business unit or trading desk responsible for managing this credit relationship. Typically aligned with commodity type (crude, NGL, LNG, refined products).

attributes.name: collateral_amount
attributes.description: Value of collateral or credit support posted by the counterparty to secure this limit. Null for unsecured limits.

attributes.name: collateral_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the collateral or credit support. May differ from the limit currency.

attributes.name: collateral_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this credit limit requires cash collateral, letter of credit, or other credit support. True for secured limits, false for unsecured.

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: User ID or name of the individual who created this credit limit record. Supports audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this credit limit record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: credit_manager_name
attributes.description: Name of the credit risk manager responsible for monitoring this counterparty relationship and limit utilization.

attributes.name: credit_rating
attributes.description: Current credit rating assigned to the counterparty by the specified rating agency or internal credit team. Influences limit size and collateral requirements.

attributes.name: credit_rating_agency
attributes.description: External rating agency whose assessment was used in the credit limit determination. Internal indicates proprietary credit scoring; none indicates unrated counterparty.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this credit limit becomes active and available for trading operations. Aligns with credit approval and documentation completion.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this credit limit expires and must be renewed or replaced. Null for evergreen limits subject to periodic review.

attributes.name: guarantor_credit_rating
attributes.description: Credit rating of the guarantor entity. Must be equal to or better than the counterparty rating to provide credit enhancement.

attributes.name: guarantor_name
attributes.description: Legal name of the parent company or third party providing the credit guarantee. Null if no guarantee is in place.

attributes.name: kyc_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current KYC documentation expires and must be refreshed. Triggers compliance workflow.

attributes.name: kyc_status
attributes.description: Status of the counterparty KYC due diligence process. Approved status is required before credit limit activation.

attributes.name: last_breach_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent credit limit breach. Used for risk reporting and counterparty performance tracking.

attributes.name: last_utilization_check_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent credit utilization calculation. Updated by real-time pre-trade credit checking system.

attributes.name: limit_currency
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the credit limit is denominated. Typically USD for international crude oil and LNG trading.

attributes.name: limit_reference_number
